### The .NET SDK checked before anything is created

2026-11-09, a live finding in the fresh-deploy test of #41, which includes #40: T1's and T2's Artifacts steps failed about 15 minutes into the run, after preflight passed. `DEPLOY.ARTIFACTS.BUILD` said "dotnet publish failed with exit code -2147450725: The command could not be loaded, possibly because: ... A compatible .NET SDK was not found", with a generic remediation ("Run New-DemoBootstrapBundle and Publish-DemoWorkloadRunner yourself to see the error").

**The cause:** in that terminal, `dotnet` was `C:\Program Files\dotnet\dotnet.exe`, a runtime-only install: the host (`host\fxr\10.0.14`) and the shared runtimes, with no `sdk` folder, ahead on `PATH`. `DOTNET_ROOT` was empty, and the folder with SDKs 10.0.402 and 10.0.403 wasn't on `PATH`. Earlier runs on that PC had passed only because `Publish-DemoWorkloadRunner` reused the runner's zip; #40 changed the runner's inputs (`global.json` 10.0.403), so it had to build. Real users can hit the same: a runtime-only install, which Windows apps and Visual Studio leave behind, or the 10.0.402 SDK the docs pinned until 2026-11-09, which `global.json`'s `latestFeature` can't roll back to. Reproduced the same day on that PC, read-only: `dotnet --version` in `workload-generator` exits with -2147450725 (`0x8000809B`, the host's SDK resolution failure) and prints the same text, and `dotnet --list-sdks` exits with 0 and prints nothing.

**Work summary.**

1. **`PREFLIGHT.TOOLS.DOTNETSDK`** (`Test-DemoDotNetSdk`, `Get-DemoDotNetSdkStatus`, in the new `Private/DotNetSdkHelpers.ps1`), right after the subscription guard, unless `-SkipRunner`:
   - It runs the `dotnet` the build runs (`Get-DemoDotNetPath`: the first on `PATH`, which `Invoke-DemoDotNet` now uses too) with `--version` in `workload-generator`, so `global.json` applies as it does to `dotnet publish` ([global.json](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/tools/global-json)).
   - **Pass** has the SDK's version, the `dotnet`'s path, and the pin in its evidence.
   - **Fail**, before anything is created: which `dotnet` ran, which SDKs it has (`--list-sdks`), what `global.json` needs, in words (the pin, `rollForward` `latestFeature`: "10.0.403 or any later 10.0 SDK"), and the exact fix. On Windows that's `winget install Microsoft.DotNet.SDK.10` ([install .NET on Windows](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/install/windows); winget's newest .NET 10 SDK is 10.0.403, checked on 2026-11-09) or Microsoft's installer; elsewhere, the installer or the dev container; and `-SkipRunner` as the way to deploy without the runner.
   - It runs `--version` with each other well-known folder's `dotnet`: `DOTNET_ROOT`, `%ProgramFiles%\dotnet`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\dotnet`, and `~/.dotnet`, where [the install scripts](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/tools/dotnet-install-script) put it. When one has an SDK that `global.json` accepts, the message says so, and the fix starts with the command that puts that folder first on `PATH` in the terminal, and where to make it stay.
   - On Windows, when the `dotnet` that ran isn't in `%ProgramFiles%\dotnet`, the fix adds that winget and the installer put the SDK there, so that folder must come first.
2. **`-SkipRunner`:** `Invoke-DemoPreflight -SkipRunner` makes the check **Not selected** and runs no `dotnet`. `deploy.ps1`'s parallel and sequential paths pass their `-SkipRunner`, and `preflight.ps1` has the switch. `validate.ps1`'s preflight area builds nothing, so it passes `-SkipRunner` and drops the record.
3. **`DEPLOY.ARTIFACTS.BUILD`:** when the build's error is the SDK (`Test-DemoDotNetSdkFailure`: the host's exit code or words, or `Invoke-DemoDotNet`'s "not found on PATH"), its remediation is the check's own diagnosis and fix, read again then (`Get-DemoArtifactBuildRemediation`). Any other build error keeps the generic step.
4. **Docs:** the prerequisites (the SDK that `global.json` accepts, first on `PATH`, and the check), troubleshooting (a row for the check under Preflight, and one for the build's failure), the CHANGELOG, and this report.

**Checked on the PC of the live finding (read-only, with its own `dotnet` installs; nothing ran against Azure):**

- **The live finding's terminal:** **Fail** in about 1 second: "The dotnet first on PATH, C:\Program Files\dotnet\dotnet.exe, has no .NET SDK, only runtimes, and workload-generator/global.json needs 10.0.403 or any later 10.0 SDK (rollForward latestFeature), so the workload runner can't be built." The fix was the winget and installer step.
- **The same terminal with `DOTNET_ROOT` set to the tools folder** (SDKs 10.0.402 and 10.0.403, not on `PATH`): **Fail**, which named that folder ("has the .NET SDK 10.0.403, which it accepts, but isn't first on PATH"). The fix started with `$env:PATH = '<that folder>;' + $env:PATH`.
- **With the tools first on `PATH`:** **Pass**, "The .NET SDK 10.0.403 builds the workload runner", in about 1 second.
- **The live run's `DEPLOY.ARTIFACTS.BUILD` message**, given to `Get-DemoArtifactBuildRemediation`: the same diagnosis and fix as the check. A bundle error kept the generic step.

**Changed files.**

- Scripts: `scripts/preflight.ps1`; in `scripts/modules/DbHubDemo`, `Private/DotNetSdkHelpers.ps1` (new), `Private/WorkloadHelpers.ps1` (`Invoke-DemoDotNet -DotNetPath`), `Private/ParallelDeployment.ps1` and `Public/Invoke-DemoDeployment.ps1` (`-SkipRunner` to preflight; the build's remediation), `Private/ValidationAreas.ps1`, and `Public/Invoke-DemoPreflight.ps1`.
- Tests: `tests/unit/DbHubDemo.DotNetSdk.Tests.ps1` (new), `DbHubDemo.Preflight.Tests.ps1`, and `DbHubDemo.Tracks.Tests.ps1`.
- Docs: `docs/prerequisites.md`, `docs/troubleshooting.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and this report.

**Validation.** Static, 2026-11-09, on Windows with PowerShell 7.6.9, Pester 5.9.1 in strict mode, PSScriptAnalyzer 1.25.0, and markdownlint-cli2 0.23.3. Only the affected files ran, at the coordinator's request; CI runs the rest, on Windows and Linux.

- Pester, the new `DbHubDemo.DotNetSdk` (30 tests): passed.
- Pester, the affected files (`DbHubDemo.Tracks`, `.Lifecycle`, `.Workload`, `.Validation`, `.Preflight`, `.DotNetSdk`, and `.OneCommand`, plus `Repo.Conventions`): 781 passed, 0 failed. `Docs.Walkthrough` and `Repo.NeutralWording`: 71 passed.
- PSScriptAnalyzer with the repository's settings on the 10 changed PowerShell files: no findings; each parses and is ASCII-only. `./tests/Invoke-StaticValidation.ps1 -Check Markdown -CI`: **Pass**.
- **Live:** none from here. Nothing ran against Azure; [still to verify](#still-to-verify).

**Risks.** R740 to R742, new.

#### Proposal: deploy.ps1 installs the pinned SDK per user

Decided on 2026-11-09: the owner chose "Install it automatically (Recommended)" (R742). [As built](#as-built-deployps1-installs-the-pinned-sdk), below, says where it differs. The owner wants one click after `az login`. The check above turns a 15-minute failure into a clear stop before anything is created, but the SDK is still a manual install. `deploy.ps1` could install the pinned SDK for the user when the check finds none that `global.json` accepts, and no other well-known folder has one:

- **Where:** a folder of the demo's own, per user, with no administrator rights: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\DbHubDemo\dotnet\<version>` on Windows, and `~/.local/share/dbhub-demo/dotnet/<version>` on Linux and macOS.
  - Not `%ProgramFiles%\dotnet`, which needs elevation and changes the machine for every app.
  - Not the install scripts' default folders, which other tools use.
  - Nothing changes on `PATH` or in the registry. The build runs that `dotnet` by its full path, which `Invoke-DemoDotNet -DotNetPath` (added here) already supports, so `global.json` and its `rollForward` still decide the SDK. The check would then be a **Pass** that names the demo's own SDK.
- **What, and its size:** Microsoft's SDK archive for the platform, from Microsoft's own download server (`https://builds.dotnet.microsoft.com/dotnet/Sdk/<version>/dotnet-sdk-<version>-<rid>.zip`, or `.tar.gz` on Linux and macOS). Measured on 2026-11-09 for 10.0.403 on win-x64, it's a 286.8 MB download and about 770 MB on disk:
  - the SDK, 399 MB;
  - its three runtimes, 199 MB;
  - the reference packs, 160 MB;
  - the templates, 10 MB.

  That's once per SDK pin, and the previous version is deleted after the new one passes. It takes about one to three minutes on a fast connection, and it would run alongside preflight, before the build that needs it.
- **Verification, fail closed:**
  - **The pin:** `config/versions.json` pins each archive's URL, file name, and SHA-512, taken from Microsoft's release metadata (`release-metadata/10.0/releases.json`), as `dotnetRuntime` is pinned for the VMs today. A Pester test keeps it equal to `global.json` and `tools.dotnetSdk`, and a Dependabot bump of `global.json` then needs the new hashes, which a helper script would fill in from the metadata.
  - **The download:** HTTPS to a temporary file, whose SHA-512 must match the pin; otherwise it's deleted and the check is a **Fail**.
  - **The install:** the archive is extracted to a temporary folder, which is then moved into place, so an interrupted install is never used.
  - **The result:** on Windows, `Get-AuthenticodeSignature` on `dotnet.exe` must be **Valid** and signed by Microsoft Corporation. Then `dotnet --version` in `workload-generator` must print the pinned version.
- **Alternatives considered:**
  - **Microsoft's `dotnet-install.ps1`:** the script is signed, but it means downloading a script and running it during the deploy, and the archive's check would rest on it, not on the repository's pin.
  - **`global.json` `paths`:** since the .NET 10 SDK, `"paths": [".dotnet", "$host$"]` lets even a runtime-only .NET 10 host, such as this PC's 10.0.14, find an SDK next to the repository. But it changes `global.json`, which is one of the runner's inputs, so every deployment would rebuild and resend the runner once. It also needs a .NET 10 host, and the full path already does the job.
  - **`winget install` from the script:** it's machine-wide, needs elevation (a UAC prompt), and isn't one click.
- **Recommendation:** install it automatically when no accepted SDK is found, and say so on the console and the status page. Keep `-SkipRunner` as it is, and add an opt-out for a machine whose owner doesn't want the download.

#### As built: deploy.ps1 installs the pinned SDK

2026-11-09, the owner's decision on the proposal above: "Install it automatically (Recommended)", under the rule of one click after `az login`. A second commit on #43's branch.

**Work summary.**

1. **`DEPLOY.DOTNETSDK`** (`Initialize-DemoDotNetSdk`, in `Private/DotNetSdkHelpers.ps1`): right after the subscription guard in both of `deploy.ps1`'s paths, before anything is created, once per run, and only when the run builds the workload runner: its Artifacts or Bootstraps steps, or a resume that compares the runner with the VMs'. Not with `-SkipRunner` or `-WhatIf`, and the status page's new .NET SDK row then says why.
   - **Pass, nothing installed:** the `dotnet` first on `PATH` has an SDK that `global.json` accepts; or the SDK it installed earlier is complete (its record, `dbhub-sdk.json`, is for the pinned archive) and passes its checks again, Microsoft's signature and `dotnet --version`.
   - **Otherwise, on Windows, it installs the pin** (`Install-DemoDotNetSdk`), with no prompt, no administrator rights, and nothing on `PATH` or in the registry:
     - **The pin:** `config/versions.json` `dotnetSdkInstall`, Microsoft's SDK zip for `win-x64` and `win-arm64`, whichever the machine is, with its URL, size, and SHA-512 from the release metadata, for the same version as `tools.dotnetSdk`; a Pester test keeps them equal.
     - **The download:** over HTTPS, to a `.partial-` file in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\DbHubDemo\dotnet` (or the folder `DBHUB_DOTNET_INSTALL_ROOT` names), with its size, then its progress every 10%, on the console and the status page's row. A download that gets no data for 2 minutes fails.
     - **The checks, fail closed:** the SHA-512; then the extracted copy's `dotnet.exe`, whose Authenticode signature must be valid and from Microsoft Corporation; then its `dotnet --version` in `workload-generator`, which must print the pin. Only then is the folder renamed to the version, and its record written last.
     - **The cleanup:** what an install that didn't finish left (`.partial-` files and folders, or a version folder without a valid record) is removed first. The zip is deleted afterwards, and so is an earlier version that this installed, renamed first so that one still in use is left whole. A lock file makes a second run wait for the first, at most 30 minutes, then use what it installed.
   - **Fail**, which ends the run before preflight, with nothing created: the install failed, with why, and the fix (run `deploy.ps1` again, install the SDK yourself, or `-SkipRunner`); or the platform has no pinned archive (Linux and macOS: #43's manual fix).
2. **Every build runs that `dotnet` by its full path:** `Resolve-DemoBuildDotNet` gives `Publish-DemoWorkloadRunner` the `dotnet` first on `PATH` when its SDK passes, otherwise the one installed for the user, so each caller uses it: the Artifacts step in both paths, the build's own process, and a resume's comparison. With neither, it stops with the check's message and fix and builds nothing; a zip it reuses needs no SDK.
3. **The check:** `PREFLIGHT.TOOLS.DOTNETSDK` passes with the installed SDK ("by its full path, checked again"). On Windows, where `deploy.ps1` would install it, a missing SDK is a **Warning** that says so, which is what `./scripts/preflight.ps1` on its own shows, since it installs nothing.
4. **No opt-out switch:** `-SkipRunner` already builds no runner and needs no SDK, the owner's rule is one click, and `deploy.ps1`'s parameters stay as they are.
5. **Docs:** the prerequisites (on Windows the SDK needn't be installed first), troubleshooting (`DEPLOY.DOTNETSDK`, and the other SDK rows), the README's tool lists, deployment, the security model (a tampering row, and the supply chain), ADR 0010's amendment, the CHANGELOG, and this report.

**Differences from the proposal:** Windows only, as the owner allowed (Linux and macOS keep the manual fix); no opt-out; it runs right after the subscription guard, not alongside preflight, because the build's own process starts before preflight, and a resume compares the runner before that; and it covers Arm64 too, which the PC of the live finding turned out to be.

**Checked on the PC of the live finding** (2026-11-09; Windows on Arm64, PowerShell 7.6.9; `C:\Program Files\dotnet`, runtime-only, first on `PATH`; `DBHUB_DOTNET_INSTALL_ROOT` set to a temporary folder; nothing ran against Azure). Two runs of the same steps; the second, with the final code:

### Phase 27 follow-up: the glob and minimatch overrides

2026-11-09. R723: `npm audit` in `fabric/app` reported 14 moderate advisories, all in development dependencies: glob (GHSA-3g3m-2fjr-6pw4, `>=9.0.0 <=14.0.1`, fixed in 14.0.2) and minimatch (GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249, `>=7.0.0 <11.0.1`, fixed in 11.0.1), both published 2026-10-30. The owner asked to finish the remaining work, including "fix the development-only npm advisories".

**What they needed** (checked 2026-11-09, read-only):

- **No parent declares a fixed version:** ESLint 10.14.0, the newest, still declares minimatch `^10.2.6`, and `@eslint/config-array` 0.23.5, the newest, `^10.2.4`; typescript-eslint 8.72.1, the newest stable release, `^10.2.2`; `archiver-utils` 5.0.2, the newest, glob `^10.0.0`; and the Rayfin CLI 1.36.2, the newest, glob `^13.0.6`. `archiver` 8.0.0 drops `archiver-utils`, but the CLI declares `archiver` `^7.0.1`. So updating a direct dependency can't clear them, and each needs an override.
- **The fixed releases against their users** ([glob's changelog](https://github.com/isaacs/node-glob/blob/main/changelog.md), [minimatch's](https://github.com/isaacs/minimatch/blob/main/changelog.md)): minimatch 11 matches each portion with a `Matcher` in place of a `RegExp`, and removes `makeRe()`, `Minimatch#regexp`, the `AST` class, and the `debug` option; glob 14 uses it and keeps `glob`, `globSync`, and `sync`. ESLint and `@eslint/config-array` use only `new Minimatch(pattern, { dot, flipNegate })`, `match(path, partial)`, and `pattern`; typescript-estree uses `minimatch()` only for `allowDefaultProject`, which this app doesn't set; the CLI imports `glob` and `globSync` with `cwd`, `absolute`, `dot`, `nodir`, and `ignore`; and `archiver-utils` requires glob for `file.expand`, which `archiver` never calls. `archiver` packages a folder with `readdir-glob` 1.1.3, which declares minimatch `^5.1.0`, outside the advisory's range. Both need Node.js 20 or later (glob `18 || 20 || >=22`, minimatch `20 || >=22`), as the CLI does.

**Work summary.**

1. **`fabric/app`:** `package.json` overrides `glob@>=9.0.0 <14.0.2` to 14.0.3 and `minimatch@>=7.0.0 <11.0.1` to 11.0.4. npm applies a keyed override only where a parent's declared range intersects the key's, so `readdir-glob` keeps minimatch 5.1.9, which a plain `minimatch` override would have moved six major versions. The lock file, regenerated with Node.js 24.22.2 and npm 11.19.1, as #40's was, drops `archiver-utils`' nested glob 10.5.0 and minimatch 9.0.9 and glob 10's dependencies (745 entries to 724), and adds `path-scurry` 3.0.0 and `@isaacs/nonrecursive-glob-match` 1.0.3. This PC's npm goes through a mirror, so the five new entries' `resolved` URLs were set back to `registry.npmjs.org`; each one's files matched jsDelivr's copy from the public registry, by SHA-256 (262 files, no difference), and CI's `npm ci` checks their SHA-512 integrity.
2. **The proof as a test:** `src/test/overrides.test.ts` checks the installed versions, and that `readdir-glob` keeps minimatch 5; runs the CLI's `packageStaticFolder`, the function behind `rayfin up`'s static hosting step, on a folder of files, and reads the ZIP from its central directory, inflating each entry and checking its CRC-32 and content; runs the CLI's `analyzeFunctionsProject` on its glob path, which must skip tests, specs, `types.ts`, and `.d.ts` files in nested folders; and checks ESLint's ignores, the configuration it picks for an app file and a test file, and the files it lints for a pattern.
3. **The Pester test** for the overrides accepts a key with the advisory's range: the range must end at the recorded `fixedIn`, the override must be at or after it, and every copy of the package in the lock file within the range must be the override's version. Against `main`'s lock file, it names glob 10.5.0 and 13.0.6, and minimatch 9.0.9 and 10.2.6.
4. **`config/versions.json`** records both overrides with their advisories and their parents' ranges (`fabricApp.overrides`).
5. **Docs:** the app's README (its overrides), the CHANGELOG, and this report: R723 is closed and R750 is new. ADR 0010's pin section lists the .NET pins only, so it doesn't change.

**Changed files.** `fabric/app/package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `README.md`, and `src/test/overrides.test.ts`; `config/versions.json`; `tests/unit/DbHubDemo.FabricApp.Tests.ps1`; `CHANGELOG.md`; and this report.

### The Insights app with the Azure CLI's tokens

2026-11-09, user-directed: "It should always do a one click and never have a user do their own sign in", then "Yes keep Az login, I am more concerned about the SQL set up. They should not need to manually do a wizard. They should sign into Az login and then have everything deployed. It is okay if rayfin needs another sign in but prefer not to." The coordinator asked for the Azure CLI's tokens first, as `RAYFIN_TOKEN` per command and audience, with the browser sign-in kept as the automatic fallback, a run that still ends **DONE** when Fabric refuses a token, a proposal for `FABRIC.APP.BROWSER`, and no change to the run's orchestration files, which another change had in flight.

**What the pinned CLI does** (read in `@microsoft/rayfin-cli` 1.36.2's code on 2026-11-09; Learn's [CLI reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/apps/cli-reference) doesn't document `RAYFIN_TOKEN`):

- An ambient `RAYFIN_TOKEN` "is returned immediately, bypassing MSAL entirely" (`dist/auth/index.js`), for every command, whatever scopes it asks for. `dist/auth/token-audience.js` warns that one Fabric-audience token satisfies every command's request but not every command's requirement.
- `rayfin up` and `rayfin up status` ask for the CLI's default, the Fabric API (`https://api.fabric.microsoft.com/.default`). `rayfin connector invoke` on a semantic model needs the Power BI API, and checks the token's `aud` claim itself (`dist/auth/db-token.js`). With an ambient token, `rayfin login status` reports an external identity and checks nothing.

**Work summary.**

1. **A token per command:** `Invoke-DemoRayfinCli -Token -TokenAudience` sets `RAYFIN_TOKEN` in the child's environment only and registers the token for redaction. A token for another audience than the command needs (`Get-DemoRayfinTokenAudience`) throws before anything runs, and `login` and `logout` never get one. `Get-DemoRayfinTokenRefusal` recognizes an authorization failure in the redacted output, and `out/fabric-app-auth.json` records the outcome, the reason, the tenant, and the time, never a token (`Get-` and `Set-DemoRayfinAuthRecord`).
2. **`configure-fabric-app.ps1`:** after its guard, the Fabric token for `rayfin up` and `rayfin up status`, and the Power BI token for the connector's queries; `FABRIC.APP.SIGNIN` is a **Pass** without `rayfin login status`. A refused `rayfin up` adds `FABRIC.APP.TOKEN`, a **Warning**, and deploys again with the CLI's own sign-in; without one, `FABRIC.APP.DEPLOY` is **Not selected** with `signInNeeded`, and `-SignIn` opens the browser sign-in right there. Refused connector calls went on with the CLI's own sign-in; since the live finding they go on through Execute Queries with the same token ([the revision](#revision-the-apps-queries-with-only-az-login-2026-11-09-live-finding)). `-RayfinSignIn` keeps the old way.
3. **`deploy.ps1`'s start:** `DEPLOY.FABRIC.APPSIGNIN` is **Not selected**, "Not needed", unless the record says Fabric refused the token for the demo's tenant (`Test-DemoRayfinSignInWanted`); then the sign-in starts as before, through the stage's CLI with node, never `npx`. No orchestration file changed: `DeployHelpers.ps1` only in a comment, and `DeployExperience.ps1` only in the sentence that says how to add the app.
4. **`FABRIC.APP.BROWSER`:** **Not selected**, "Not needed", when `FABRIC.APP.CONNECTOR` passed and `FABRIC.APP.QUERIES` is **Pass** or **Warning**, so **DONE** no longer lists it under "Please confirm"; otherwise **Manual action required**, as before. Its note and condition were made exact in [the revision](#revision-the-apps-queries-with-only-az-login-2026-11-09-live-finding).
5. **No `npx`:** the remediations name `./scripts/configure-fabric-app.ps1 -SignIn` or `./out/fabric-app/node_modules/.bin/rayfin`, and a status read without a stage is Unknown.
6. **Docs:** ADR 0023's amendment, with the owner's words; ADR 0012's statuses and the ADR index; the README; deployment; prerequisites (P14); troubleshooting, with a `FABRIC.APP.TOKEN` row; the automation support matrix (rows 124, 125, 152, and 173); the security model; the presentation; limitations; the app's README; the CHANGELOG; and this report.

#### Revision: the app's queries with only `az login` (2026-11-09 live finding)

The coordinator ran 280699f's `./scripts/configure-fabric-app.ps1` against the day's fresh test workspace, 15:40 to 15:46 ET, on a PC that already had a Rayfin sign-in:

- **The deploy needs only `az login`:** `FABRIC.APP.DEPLOY` **Pass**, "rayfin up deployed ... in 162 s ... with the Azure CLI's token"; `FABRIC.APP.STATUS` **Pass**; `out/fabric-app-auth.json` **Accepted**.
- **The connector's direct route refused the Azure CLI's Power BI token:** `rayfin connector invoke` on the semantic model connector calls Power BI's `executeDaxQueries` (`POST https://api.powerbi.com/v1.0/myorg/groups/{workspace}/datasets/{model}/executeDaxQueries`; `@microsoft/rayfin-connector-fabric-semanticmodel` 1.36.2, `dist/directExecute.js`), which answered HTTP 401 `{"error":{"code":"Unauthorized","pbi.error":{"code":"Unauthorized",...,"exceptionCulprit":1}}}`. The check then fell back to the PC's cached Rayfin sign-in and passed (evidence `auth` `rayfinSignIn`, `tokenRefused`).
- **A new tester would have seen red:** without a Rayfin sign-in, that fallback can't sign in in `--json` mode, so every first deploy would end with `FABRIC.APP.CONNECTOR` **Fail** and `FABRIC.APP.BROWSER` **Manual action required**, with the app deployed and working.
- **The documented API takes the same token:** [Execute Queries In Group](https://learn.microsoft.com/rest/api/power-bi/datasets/execute-queries-in-group) (`Invoke-DemoDaxQuery`, as `configure-powerbi.ps1` uses it), with `Get-DemoPowerBIToken`'s Azure CLI token, ran all 14 of the app's exported queries on the same model: HTTP 200 for each, with the connector run's row counts (`incident-windows` and `readiness-checks` returned 0, as in `FABRIC.APP.QUERIES`' **Warning**).
- **The browser note overclaimed:** "worked through its connector ..., the one the app uses". The CLI's own comment on `connector invoke --transport` says the direct route never crosses the deployed app's route (its backend, then User Data Functions, then a delegated on-behalf-of call), and Execute Queries doesn't either.

**Work summary.**

1. **The routes (`Test-DemoFabricApp`):** each query runs through the connector's direct route with the Azure CLI's Power BI token; once that route refuses the token, through Execute Queries with the same token, for that query and every one after it. The Rayfin CLI's own sign-in runs them only with `-RayfinSignIn`, never as a fallback, so a run does the same on a PC with or without a Rayfin sign-in. Without a token and without `-RayfinSignIn` (`-FabricToken`, which runs no subscription guard, or a Power BI token the Azure CLI didn't give), no query runs, and `FABRIC.APP.CONNECTOR` is a **Warning** that says so.
2. **What Execute Queries does differently:** one query per request, and no `resultSetRowCountLimit`, so each result's row count is compared with the bound in the query's payload; over it, the query fails as `overflow`, as the app's connector would fail it. Its rows come back keyed by column name and are read in order, like the connector's columns.
3. **Not an auth refusal:** the connector's refusal is `connectorRefusal` in the evidence, never `tokenRefused`. Only `rayfin up`'s outcome writes `out/fabric-app-auth.json`, so no `FABRIC.APP.TOKEN` record and no browser sign-in follow from it, in this run or a later one.
4. **The evidence:** `route` (`connector` or `executeQueries`), `auth` (`azureCli` or `rayfinSignIn`), and `connectorRefusal` on `FABRIC.APP.CONNECTOR`; on `FABRIC.APP.QUERIES`, each query's route and `rowBound`.
5. **When Execute Queries refuses the token too:** `FABRIC.APP.CONNECTOR` is a **Fail** that names both answers, with the fix for what Power BI answered: HTTP 401, sign in again as the configured account; 403, Read and Build on the model and the Dataset Execute Queries REST API setting; 404, deploy the model; 400, the DAX; anything else, check again. No fix names `configure-fabric-app.ps1`, so `deploy.ps1`'s summary keeps it.
6. **`FABRIC.APP.BROWSER`:** still **Not selected**, "Not needed", when the connector check passed, every query ran, and the app is deployed (in this run, or its hosting answered). The note now says exactly what was verified: the app is deployed, its hosting is protected, and every query it runs returned its data from `SM_DatabaseHub_History` under your identity, with the route. Then it says that the app's own route in the browser can't be checked from a script, and gives the link to open the app. Without a confirmed deployment it's **Manual action required**, and says why.
7. **`configure-fabric-app.ps1`** gives the check the workspace, the model, whether it deployed in this run, and `-RayfinSignIn`. Execute Queries proves the Dataset Execute Queries REST API setting directly, as `FABRIC.APP.CONNECTOR` did before.
8. **No default sign-in in the docs or the run's own text:** the README (its steps, quick start, assistant section, "Still manual", and "Where you sign in"), `AGENTS.md`, the FAQ, the deployment guide's start and durations, the prerequisites' dev container note, `deploy.ps1`'s help, the start banner's expectations and its notice for a session that can't take keyboard input, `init.ps1`'s next steps, and the status page's sign-in row still said that a browser opens at the start of every run for the Insights app's sign-in. B changed the behavior and the tables, not these. They now say that the app deploys with your `az login`, and that the Rayfin CLI's browser sign-in starts only after Fabric refused that token. Only text changed; dated records stay as they were.

### deploy.ps1 updates itself from GitHub

2026-11-09. A tester's AI agent re-ran an older demo from a clone pulled earlier that day, before #41 merged, and got #41's already-fixed T2 refusal: `deploy.ps1` runs the code in its folder and never asked GitHub. The owner chose, from the options offered: "Update itself: fast-forward a clean checkout to the latest main, then run (Recommended)". The question was: "Should deploy.ps1 check at the start whether the local copy is behind the latest code on GitHub? With the recommended option, a clean checkout updates itself (fast-forward only) and restarts with the new code. If the copy has local changes, is on another branch, or GitHub can't be reached, it shows a warning with the git pull command instead."

**Work summary.**

1. **`Invoke-DemoSelfUpdate`** (new, public), which `deploy.ps1` calls right after it loads DbHubDemo, before the transcript, the configuration, the status page, or any Azure call. It fetches origin's `main` (`git fetch ... +refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main`, at most 20 seconds, with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and `GCM_INTERACTIVE=never`, so no credential prompt waits for a person). It updates only a clean `main` that tracks `origin/main` and is an ancestor of it with commits to take: `git merge --ff-only` to the fetched commit, one line from which commit to which and how many came from GitHub, then the script again in a fresh `pwsh` (`-NoLogo -NoProfile -File`, `Process.Start` with nothing redirected, so it writes to the same console and reads its keyboard), with `$PSBoundParameters` passed on as they were (`ConvertTo-DemoScriptArgument`: `-Name value`, `-Switch`, `-Switch:$false`, each value one argument), and its exit code is the run's. A restart that can't start is an Error and exit code 2: the old code never goes on.
2. **The loop guard and the note:** the restarted process gets `DBHUB_SELF_UPDATED` (`<from>;<to>;<commits>`), for it only. It never checks again, and the update is `DEPLOY.SELFUPDATE` **Pass**, the first note in the banner and on the status page (`Start-DemoDeploymentRun -Note`, before what the run ignores in the configuration).
3. **Otherwise a Warning, and the run goes on:** `DEPLOY.SELFUPDATE` **Warning**, with the reason, the exact command (`Get-DemoSelfUpdateWarning`), and the same note: local changes in tracked files (`git status --untracked-files=no`, so the Git-ignored `config/` and `out/` never count), another branch or a detached `HEAD`, a `main` that tracks something other than `origin/main`, diverged, `-WhatIf`, a fetch that fails or times out, a fast-forward that fails, Git missing, and a folder that isn't a checkout (`git rev-parse --show-prefix`, which a short 8.3 path can't fool). A checkout that has everything on GitHub's `main` is a **Pass**, even on another branch or with local commits or changes: there's nothing to take, so the coordinator's "diverged or ahead" warns only when it's diverged. A check that throws is a **Warning**, never a stop.
4. **Opt-outs:** `-NoSelfUpdate`, `DBHUB_NO_SELF_UPDATE` (`1` or `true`), and CI (`GITHUB_ACTIONS`, `CI`, `TF_BUILD`) are **Not selected**, with no git call. When the repository's own code runs `deploy.ps1` (a test, another script: the existing `$entryNested`), there's no check and no result.
5. **Resumes:** the restarted run continues an unfinished deployment as any plain run does, and #37's check then sends a changed bootstrap bundle or runner to the VMs that lack it (`DEPLOY.ARTIFACTS.CHANGED_*`), so one command updates this PC and the VMs.
6. **Docs:** the README's quick start, deployment (a new section, and the option), troubleshooting (each Warning, what it means, and how to opt out), `AGENTS.md` (don't pull or switch branches yourself; report the Warning), the CHANGELOG, and this report.

**Changed files.** `scripts/deploy.ps1`; `scripts/modules/DbHubDemo/DbHubDemo.psd1`; the new `Public/Invoke-DemoSelfUpdate.ps1` and `Private/SelfUpdateHelpers.ps1`; `Public/Start-DemoDeploymentRun.ps1`; the new `tests/unit/DbHubDemo.SelfUpdate.Tests.ps1`; `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/deployment.md`, `docs/troubleshooting.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and this report.

**Validation.**

- **Static (2026-11-09, Windows, PowerShell 7.6.9, Pester 5.9.1, PSScriptAnalyzer 1.25.0, Git 2.56.0):**
  - `./tests/Invoke-StaticValidation.ps1 -Check PSScriptAnalyzer, Pester`: Pester **Pass**, 4009 passed, 17 skipped, 0 failed. PSScriptAnalyzer had one finding in the new test file (a helper's own `-WhatIf` parameter), renamed; the new and changed files then had none.
  - `tests/unit/DbHubDemo.SelfUpdate.Tests.ps1`: 34 passed. With git and the restart mocked: the update with its arguments (a path with spaces and quotes, a switch, `-Switch:$false`, an empty string, an int, common parameters), its line and marker, a restart that can't start, the restarted process's **Pass** and loop guard, every Warning case, `-WhatIf`, a check that throws, the opt-outs, and `-Nested`; `deploy.ps1` calls it before `Resolve-DemoUserPath`, the transcript, the first run, the configuration, the status page, and the deployment. With real git against a bare repository in TestDrive (two commits) and a real restart in a fresh `pwsh`: a clean `main` fast-forwards, the restarted script prints the new commit's marker once, with the same arguments, and its exit code; the next run is current; local changes, a diverged `main`, another branch, and an unreachable origin only warn and leave `HEAD` as it was; a Git-ignored configuration doesn't count; `DBHUB_NO_SELF_UPDATE=1` doesn't even fetch.
  - `-Check Markdown`: **Pass**.
- **The real `deploy.ps1`, offline:** a temporary clone of this branch one commit behind its origin, whose second commit makes `deploy.ps1` print a marker and exit right after the self-update. `pwsh -File <clone>/scripts/deploy.ps1 'configs with space/it''s.json' -Resume -NoBrowser -T2WaitMinutes 33` printed the update line, then the new code's marker with the same `-ConfigPath` (given by position), `-Resume`, `-NoBrowser`, and `-T2WaitMinutes`, and the **Pass** note, and exited with the new code's 5; the first process wrote no `out/`. Nothing ran against Azure.
- **Linux:** this PC has no WSL or Docker. The code has no OS-specific branch, and CI's PowerShell job runs the same Pester file on `ubuntu-latest` and `windows-latest`.

### T4: a refused `t4SkuName` falls back too, and every size change says what it cost (2026-11-09)

**Why.** A tester re-ran an older demo whose configuration set `t4SkuName` to `Standard_B1ms`, most likely after an agent followed `PREFLIGHT.COST.MONTHLY`'s old fix "set t4SkuName to Standard_B1ms" under `init.ps1`'s old 250 ceiling. West US 3 refused `Standard_B1ms` with `SkuNotAvailable`, as on 2026-10-26, and a size the configuration set had no fallback, so T4 stayed out and the run ended **NOT DONE**. Their agent reported: "Azure still rejects the approved Standard_B1ms size with SkuNotAvailable. I did not silently select a more expensive tier."

**Decision sources.** The owner, verbatim: "Yes, fall back automatically, cheapest first, with a Warning (Recommended)", then "make sure to add a notification of it though to say what you tried to deploy and what was deployed included cost difference". R727's 250 ceiling: the coordinator's decision under the owner's one-click-upgrade rule ([ADR 0019](adr/0019-t4-postgresql-flexible-server.md#2026-11-09-user-directed-a-size-t4skuname-sets-falls-back-too-and-every-automatic-size-change-says-what-it-cost)).

**Work summary.**

1. **The fallback for a size `t4SkuName` sets** (`Get-DemoT4FallbackOrder`, `Get-DemoT4NextSku`, `Invoke-DemoTemplateDeployment`): while T4's server doesn't exist, Azure's `SkuNotAvailable` moves it on: the size once more in another zone the region lists for it (`Get-DemoT4SkuZone`, now in the size's own edition, Burstable included), then the other documented sizes that cost as much or more, cheapest first, then the cheaper ones, nearest first, by tier and vCores, never a price. Each size's cost check runs right before it's tried and only reports (a `DEPLOY.T4.SKU` **Warning**). Without `t4SkuName`, the order is as before. A run tries at most 8 template attempts (6 without `t4SkuName`).
2. **The notice for every automatic size change,** the default's included (`New-DemoT4SizeChangeResult`, `Format-DemoT4SizeChangeText`, `Get-DemoT4SizeChangeCost`): `DEPLOY.T4.FALLBACK`, a **Warning**, with the size asked for and every size Azure refused with the zones tried, the size deployed, and T4's monthly estimate at both, light use and worst case, with the difference in USD, labeled as estimates (`ConvertTo-DemoT4FallbackCost` now gives `T4LightUseMonthlyUsd` and `LightUseMonthlyUsd` too, and `Get-DemoT4GeneralPurposeCost -Cache` shares reads and prices between sizes). It's the console line, the Infrastructure row's note, T4's row (`T4.SIZE`, through the tracks' handoff), and the **DONE** or **NOT DONE** note (`Complete-DemoDeploymentRun`, `Get-DemoT4FallbackNote -Notice`); `status.ps1` gives it afterwards (`STATUS.T4.SIZE`, `Get-DemoT4RecordedSizeChange`). The status page keeps it whole (the rows' and the summary's length limits are raised for it).
3. **The record:** the new `DbHubT4Refused` tag (`ConvertTo-DemoT4RefusedRecord`) holds what Azure refused, the asked size first, with the zones and when, next to `DbHubT4Size`. A record holds while the configuration asks for the size Azure refused (`Test-DemoT4RecordInEffect`, used by `Resolve-DemoEffectiveConfig`, whose copy keeps the asked size in `t4SkuPinned`), so later runs keep a server the fallback created: no resize, restart, or refusal again. A `t4SkuName` that names another size clears it.
4. **Preflight:** a refused or unlisted `t4SkuName` is a **Warning** with where `deploy.ps1` starts (`PREFLIGHT.T4.CAPABILITY`, `PREFLIGHT.T4.SKU`), and `PREFLIGHT.T4.FALLBACK` names the order. The start a run takes from preflight follows the configuration's order (`Select-DemoT4StartSku -Order`); an older run's `None` counts as `Standard_D2ds_v5`, part of the cleanup PR's item 4.
5. **The monthly ceiling** (`Get-DemoCostEstimate`, so preflight, `start-demo.ps1`, and `estimate-cost.ps1`): when only a T4 size the person didn't choose puts the month over `monthlyCeilingUsd`, and the month fits at the reference size, `PREFLIGHT.COST.MONTHLY` is a **Warning** that names the amount: a fallback size, priced at the size `t4SkuName` sets, or exactly 250 without `t4SkuName` (R727), priced at `Standard_B1ms`. Checked first that a Warning there is safe: `start-demo.ps1`'s guardrail runs the same check, so a **Fail** would stop every start after a pricier fallback; the value isn't changed, the budget keeps alerting at it, and `start-demo.ps1`'s actual-cost check still stops starts once the month reaches it.
6. **Fix texts:** no remediation or schema description asks for a size to be set any more (`PREFLIGHT.COST.MONTHLY`, the schema's `t4SkuName` and `monthlyCeilingUsd`, `New-DemoT4SkuFailureResult`); raising the ceiling stays the fix, and a test fails on any script or the schema that says "set t4SkuName to" a Burstable size. A refused scale of an existing T4 to the default now puts the Region access request before setting `t4SkuName`, and no text says a size you set never changes. The default chain's every-size-refused fix is unchanged, as asked.

**Changed files.**

### The self-update's git off PATH

2026-11-09, a live finding on #45 (merged as 8cda319): a clone of `main` ran `./scripts/deploy.ps1` in a terminal where `git` isn't on `PATH`, on a PC whose only git is an app's bundled one. `DEPLOY.SELFUPDATE` warned, correctly by its rules, "Git isn't installed ..." with the advice to install Git, clone again, and copy `config/demo.config.json`, and the run went on with the old code. A tester who cloned with GitHub Desktop, or another tool that bundles git without putting it on `PATH`, would never self-update: the stale-code problem the owner wanted gone.

**Work summary.**

1. **Git off PATH** (`Get-DemoGitLocation`): the git on `PATH` (`Get-DemoGitOnPath`), or else the first candidate (`Get-DemoGitCandidatePath`) that is a file and answers `git --version` with `git version ...` within 10 seconds (`Test-DemoGitExecutable`). On Windows: `%ProgramFiles%\Git\cmd\git.exe`, `%ProgramFiles(x86)%\Git\cmd\git.exe`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Git\cmd\git.exe` ([Git for Windows](https://gitforwindows.org/)); GitHub Desktop's `%LOCALAPPDATA%\GitHubDesktop\app-*\resources\app\git\cmd\git.exe`, newest version first; and Visual Studio's `Common7\IDE\CommonExtensions\Microsoft\TeamFoundation\Team Explorer\Git\cmd\git.exe` in each installation that [vswhere](https://github.com/microsoft/vswhere/wiki/Installing) lists (`Invoke-DemoVsWhere`, when vswhere is there). On macOS and Linux: `/usr/bin/git`, `/usr/local/bin/git`, `/opt/homebrew/bin/git`. `Get-DemoCheckoutState` resolves it once and passes it by full path (`Invoke-DemoGit -GitPath`) to every call, the merge and its check too; `PATH` is never changed.
2. **Said when it's off PATH** (`Format-DemoGitUsedText`): "It used the git at `<path>` (`<source>`), which isn't on PATH." ends the update line, the restarted run's note (a fourth field of `DBHUB_SELF_UPDATED`), and the **Pass**; a result's evidence has `git` and `gitOnPath`.
3. **Better advice:** no git at all, in a folder with `.git` (a directory, or a worktree's file), is the new case `NoGitCheckout`: "Install Git (`https://git-scm.com/downloads`), then run git pull --ff-only in `<this folder>`". A folder that isn't a checkout keeps the clone advice, which now names this run's configuration: `deploy.ps1` passes its `-ConfigPath` (resolved with `Resolve-DemoUserPath`) to `Invoke-DemoSelfUpdate`. `config/demo.config.json` is copied to `config/` in the new folder; another file in this folder to the same place, run with its `-ConfigPath`; a file outside the folder stays where it is, with the same `-ConfigPath`.
4. **Docs:** troubleshooting (which git it uses, and the two "Git isn't installed" Warnings), deployment, the CHANGELOG, and this report.

**Changed files.** `scripts/deploy.ps1`; `scripts/modules/DbHubDemo/Private/SelfUpdateHelpers.ps1`; `Public/Invoke-DemoSelfUpdate.ps1`; `tests/unit/DbHubDemo.SelfUpdate.Tests.ps1`; `docs/deployment.md`, `docs/troubleshooting.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and this report.

**Validation.** See the pull request's description for the exact commands and results: `DbHubDemo.SelfUpdate.Tests.ps1` 52 passed (18 new: each lookup, its order, the newest GitHub Desktop first, vswhere's installations, the Linux list, PATH first, the first candidate that runs, none, `git --version` against the real git and another program; the update, the restarted run's note, and the **Pass** with a git off PATH, every git call by its full path; the checkout without Git; the four clone advices). Nothing ran against Azure.

**Risks.** R800 to R802 new.

### T4: a refused server's shell isn't T4 (live finding, 2026-11-09)

**Why.** The coordinator ran #46's live check on the test environment `rg-dbhubfv-demo`, as the tester's case: T4 deleted, `t4SkuName` `Standard_B1ms`, `monthlyCeilingUsd` 250, then a plain `./scripts/deploy.ps1` from a clone at 8cda319, which updated itself to 71ea144 ("Updated this copy from GitHub's main: 8cda319 to 71ea144, 4 new commit(s)").

- Preflight passed at 20:41 ET: `PREFLIGHT.T4.FALLBACK` **Pass** ("t4SkuName sets Standard_B1ms. If Azure refuses it ... tries it once more in another zone..."), and `PREFLIGHT.COST.*` passed with the 250 ceiling at `Standard_B1ms`.
- At 01:41:36Z (20:41:36 ET), "Template create: dbhubfv-demo-main". It failed: `DEPLOY.TEMPLATE` **Fail**, "The template create failed: Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/flexibleServers pgflex01-lgif56: SkuNotAvailable: Specified SKU is not supported in this region. Please choose a different SKU."
- At 01:46:24Z: "[WARNING] T4's server exists after this failed attempt (it depends only on the network, so another resource's failure doesn't stop it): it's kept at Standard_B1ms, and the fallback stops here, so it isn't priced again, left out, or moved to another size."
- The run ended **NOT DONE** at `DEPLOY.TEMPLATE`: no retry in another zone, no `DEPLOY.T4.FALLBACK`, no `Standard_B2s`.
- The cause: Azure kept the server it refused as a shell. `az resource show` gave `properties.state` `Dropping` at 20:48:40 ET, and `az postgres flexible-server list` listed it too, mostly with nulls; by 20:49:15 ET it was gone (`ResourceNotFound`), about 3 minutes after the refusal was logged. `Invoke-DemoTemplateDeployment` took `Get-DemoT4State`'s `Exists` for a server the attempt had created (review of 64c28b2) and stopped the fallback. The default chain had the same flaw, never seen live because Azure always accepted `Standard_D4ds_v5`.

**Decision source.** The coordinator's request: a server counts as existing only when it's usable; wait for the shell, bounded, with progress on the console and the status page; then go on with the fallback; on a timeout, end **NOT DONE** and record the refusal so the plain rerun goes on with the fallback; check whether the deployment's operations identify the refusal; and audit every reader of `Get-DemoT4State`. The coordinator's timing: about 3 minutes live, so a bound of about 15 minutes, read every 15 to 30 seconds ([ADR 0019](adr/0019-t4-postgresql-flexible-server.md#2026-11-09-live-finding-a-server-azure-refused-is-a-shell-that-it-removes-not-t4)).

**Work summary.**

1. **What counts as T4** (`Get-DemoT4State`): a server in `Dropping` ("Server is being deleted", [ServerState](https://learn.microsoft.com/rest/api/postgresql/servers/get)) has `Exists` false, with the new `Removing` and `Present`. The states of a deployed server are listed once (`$script:T4DeployedStates`: Ready, Stopped, Starting, Stopping, Updating, Restarting, Disabled, Inaccessible). ServerState has no failed state: a failed creation shows only in the deployment's operations.
2. **The refusal first, then the state** (`Invoke-DemoTemplateDeployment`): after a failed attempt, a server in `Dropping` is a shell, and so is a server in another state than a deployed server's whose T4 deployment failed with `SkuNotAvailable` for the size the attempt sent. Yes, the operations identify the refusal directly: `Get-DemoT4CreateFailure` reads the `pgflex01` deployment's failed server operation, whatever the server's state, as it already did for the fallback's next step; the flaw was the order, since the state read stopped the fallback first. A server in a deployed server's state, or one with no refusal for the size sent, is kept as before: nothing is deleted or replaced on a guess.
3. **The wait:** the next attempt creates a server with the same name, so it waits until the shell is gone, at most 15 minutes, read every 15 seconds (`-T4RemovalWaitMinutes`, `-T4RemovalPollSeconds`). It's said on the console and on the status page's Infrastructure and T4 rows, Azure-side ("Azure is removing the T4 server it refused ..."), with a line about every minute and one when it's gone; the sequential path passes `-ProgressPath` too. A run that starts while a shell is there waits the same way. Then the fallback goes on with `DEPLOY.T4.SKU` and `DEPLOY.T4.FALLBACK` as designed, the notice with both estimates and the difference included.
4. **A shell that outlasts the bound:** the run records the next size of the fallback with what Azure refused (`DbHubT4Size`, `DbHubT4Refused`; the asked size's retry in another zone has no record of its own, so the rerun goes on to the next size) and ends **NOT DONE** with `DEPLOY.T4.REMOVING` (**Fail**), whose fix is the plain rerun. Nothing is recorded for a shell that the run didn't see refused, a server deleted by hand for example.
5. **Every other reader,** audited: the resume's `DEPLOY.T4.MISSING` (`Get-DemoT4MissingResult`), `start-demo.ps1`'s and `stop-demo.ps1`'s power actions (`Invoke-DemoT4PowerAction`, **Not selected**), `stop-demo.ps1`'s activity step, `status.ps1` (`STATUS.T4`; a shell's size is no longer read as T4's, and the size the fallback chose says its own tier, where it said General Purpose for a Burstable size), `validate.ps1` (`T4.SERVER`), `METRICS.T4` (no "start-demo.ps1 starts it"), the T4 workload's setup (`WORKLOAD.T4.ENABLE`), `reset-demo.ps1`, **DONE**'s note (`Complete-DemoDeploymentRun`), and preflight, where a shell's size no longer moves the default's start or passes `PREFLIGHT.T4.CAPABILITY` for it. Unchanged, since `Exists` already decides: the restart for `max_connections`, the validation's reasons, `status.ps1`'s check of an off record, the cost checks (preflight prices a new server while a shell is there; `estimate-cost.ps1` reads no server), and the scale path (only for a server that exists). The nightly safety stop's runbooks already treated `Dropping` like a missing server (`DbHubControl.Common.ps1`).

### A paused capacity isn't a missing lakehouse (live finding, 2026-11-10)

**Why.** A plain `./scripts/deploy.ps1` rerun on `main`'s code, 2026-11-10 from 00:14 to 00:50 ET, on `rg-dbhubfv-demo`. The workspace's capacity, "fabricmbprod" (F4), was **Active** at 00:32, when `FABRIC.P5.CAPACITY` passed for the Insights app. Its owner then paused it (`fabric.manageCapacity` is false: the owner manages it) before the validation, 00:47 to 00:49. The run said:

- `FABRIC.P5.CAPACITY` **Manual action required**: "The capacity "fabricmbprod" (F4) of the Fabric workspace "Database Hub Demo Final Test" is Inactive, so ...".
- `FABRIC.RESOLVE.LAKEHOUSE`: "The lakehouses in the workspace ... couldn't be listed: HTTP 404: CapacityNotActive: Internal error CapacityNotActive.Capacity...", with a workspace role as the fix.
- `FABRIC.ITEMS.REQUIRED` **Fail**: "The workspace "Database Hub Demo Final Test" is missing: the lakehouse LH_DatabaseHub."
- `DEPLOY.FABRIC.HISTORY` **Not selected**: "The Fabric track didn't create the workspace or the lakehouse...".
- **NOT DONE**, with `FABRIC.ITEMS.REQUIRED` as the reason, and "Run ./scripts/deploy.ps1 ... again: its Fabric track imports what's missing" as the next step.

The lakehouse existed. Fabric didn't list it because the capacity was paused ([Pause and resume your Fabric capacity](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/enterprise/pause-resume): "Pausing a capacity can prevent Microsoft Fabric content from being available"), and a rerun would have failed the same way until it was resumed. The run's other required items were found: Items - List Items still answered. **NOT DONE** took the first **Fail** over the capacity's **Manual action required**, and the lakehouse list's record came before the capacity's anyway (`configure-fabric.ps1` resolves before its checklist).

**Work summary.**

1. **Only a list that answered without an item makes it missing** (`Test-DemoFabricRequiredItem`). An item whose list failed couldn't be checked, and the message says that this doesn't mean it's missing:
   - Fabric answered that the capacity is paused or inactive: **Manual action required**, evidence `capacityInactive`. The capacity is read then (`Test-DemoFabricWorkspace`), and its `FABRIC.P5.CAPACITY` record comes first, so the message names it ("the capacity "fabricmbprod" (F4) of the workspace ... is Inactive, so Fabric didn't list the lakehouse LH_DatabaseHub (HTTP 404: CapacityNotActive: ...)"). The fix is to resume it, or have its administrator resume it, then run `./scripts/deploy.ps1` again.
   - HTTP 401 or 403: **Manual action required**, with the role and sign-in fix.
   - Anything else, throttling (HTTP 429) and service errors (5xx) included: a **Warning** with the HTTP status, whose fix is to run `./scripts/deploy.ps1` again in a few minutes. When other items are missing besides, it's the **Fail** as before, and it names what couldn't be checked too.
2. **NOT DONE names the paused capacity first** (`Get-DemoFabricCapacityBlock`, in `Get-DemoDeploymentOutcome`): the latest record that says the capacity isn't running, `FABRIC.P5.CAPACITY` preferred, unless a later `FABRIC.P5.CAPACITY` read it **Active**. Its fix is the next step, on the console and the status page alike (the same outcome writes both). `Invoke-DemoDoneGate` takes both records from the items check.
3. **The resolver** (`Resolve-DemoFabricConfig`): a lakehouse list that Fabric refuses for a paused capacity is **Manual action required**, with the resume as the fix and Learn's pause-and-resume page; a throttled or unanswered list (workspaces or lakehouses) says to run the script again in a few minutes. Every list that didn't answer has evidence `listed` false, with its `statusCode` and `error`, so its readers tell it from a missing item.
4. **The history report's snapshot** (`Invoke-DemoHistorySnapshotRun`): a lakehouse list refused for a paused capacity is the existing **Warning** `CapacityPaused` ("the workspace's capacity isn't running (HTTP 404: CapacityNotActive: ...)"); any other list that didn't answer is **Failed**, "couldn't be read"; only a list that answered without them is "The Fabric track didn't create the workspace or the lakehouse".
5. **The other readers:** `status.ps1`'s `STATUS.FABRIC` looks a paused capacity's lakehouse up among the workspace's items (Items - List Items, type Lakehouse) and passes, as its doc says it does for a capacity paused between sessions. `stop-demo.ps1 -SaveHistory` names the capacity, not "configure-fabric.ps1 creates what's missing". A notebook run whose list failed (`Invoke-DemoFabricNotebookRun`) no longer says to import the notebooks: a paused capacity is **Manual action required** with the resume, anything else a **Fail** whose fix is to run it again. `validate.ps1`'s Hub area and `configure-fabric.ps1` report the resolver's records, so they get its fixes.
6. **One wording for the fix** (`FabricResolveHelpers.ps1`): `Test-DemoFabricCapacityInactiveText` (the pattern the history snapshot already used), `Get-DemoFabricListFailureKind`, and `Get-DemoFabricCapacityResumeFix`, "Resume the capacity, or ask its administrator to (Azure portal: Microsoft Fabric, the capacity, Resume; that resumes its billing too).", which `FABRIC.P5.CAPACITY` now gives for a paused capacity too. No fix names a script that resumes or pauses it.

- Tests: `tests/unit/DbHubDemo.OneCommand.Tests.ps1`, `DbHubDemo.FabricResolve.Tests.ps1`, `DbHubDemo.HistorySnapshot.Tests.ps1`, `DbHubDemo.FabricTrack.Tests.ps1`, and `DbHubDemo.FirstRun.Tests.ps1`.
- Docs: `docs/troubleshooting.md` (a row), `docs/deployment.md` (what DONE needs), `docs/configuration.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and this report.

### Entry scripts use the module they imported (live finding, 2026-11-10)

**Why.** Live, 2026-11-10 at 12:01 ET, `./scripts/start-demo.ps1 -WarmUpMinutes 10` against the owner's demo stopped after the environment had started: "start-demo.ps1: The term 'DbHubDemo DbHubDemo DbHubDemo' is not recognized as a name of a cmdlet, function, script file, or executable program." The PowerShell window had imported the module from three clones over time. PowerShell keeps a module loaded once for each path it was imported from (an entry script's `-Force` replaces only the copy from its own path), so `$module = Get-Module -Name 'DbHubDemo'` (`start-demo.ps1`, line 135) returned all three, and `& $module { ... }` (the pending activity switch, line 225, and the `finally` block's, line 232) got the array, which PowerShell turned into one command name. The same lookup was in `start-demo.ps1`'s clipboard check before a one-time password (line 190) and in `setup-github-repo.ps1` when it reads `github.repository` (line 68). Running the scripts from a second clone in the same window is enough, for example after cloning again, which the docs advise for a folder that isn't a git checkout.

**Work summary.**

1. **Each script keeps the module it imported** (`start-demo.ps1`, `setup-github-repo.ps1`): `$module = Import-Module -Name (...'modules/DbHubDemo/DbHubDemo.psd1') -Force:(-not $entryNested) -PassThru` returns exactly this checkout's copy: loaded again from a terminal, or the one already loaded when the repository's own code runs the script (without `-Force`). Every `& $module { ... }` runs in it. The scripts' commands resolve to it as before: the import binds them to the copy imported last.
2. **The deployment-stack trial imports its own copy** (`tests/teardown/Invoke-DeploymentStackTrial.ps1`): it skipped its import when any DbHubDemo was loaded, so in a window that ran another copy's scripts it ran that copy's code. It always imports its own now, without `-Force`, so a copy from the same path that's loaded already keeps its state.
3. **The audit.** Every other `Get-Module -Name 'DbHubDemo'` is in a background job: the parallel tracks, the artifact builds, the policy inventory, and T1's monitoring (`Private/ParallelDeployment.ps1`, `Start-Job`), and the status page's writer (`Private/ProgressHelpers.ps1`, `Start-ThreadJob`, or `Start-Job` without the ThreadJob module). Each imports the module by its path from its own checkout, in its own process or runspace, where a probe with two copies loaded in the parent found only that one, so they're unchanged (R820). The other 22 entry scripts run no code in the module's scope.
4. **Tests** (`tests/unit/Repo.Conventions.Tests.ps1`, in "Entry scripts load this checkout's DbHubDemo on every run"), from the scripts' syntax trees:
   - no entry script and no tool under `tests/` (outside `tests/unit`) looks DbHubDemo up by name (`Get-Module`, or `Get-Command -Module`);
   - every `& <target> { ... }` in an entry script goes through `$module`, assigned once from the script's own `Import-Module ... -PassThru`;
   - every lookup in the module sits in a script block that the same function starts with `Start-Job` or `Start-ThreadJob -ScriptBlock`, after an `Import-Module` in that block (five lookups);
   - the behaviour: a child process loads two copies of the module from the test drive (`LOADED 2`); probes built from each entry script's own text (its import, the assignments of the variables it runs module code through, and those targets) run from the `scripts` folder of the copy it loaded first, top-level and nested, and each gets exactly that copy (one module, from its folder), with `Get-DemoConfig` resolving to it.

**Changed files.**

- Scripts: `scripts/start-demo.ps1` and `scripts/setup-github-repo.ps1`.

### `estimate-cost.ps1` reads the safety stop's coverage (found 2026-11-13)

**Why.** Found while pricing T4's read replica, 2026-11-13: signed in to the owner's subscription, `./scripts/estimate-cost.ps1` warned "The Defender for Cloud plans, the T3 free offer, or the golden snapshots weren't read ... The term 'Test-DemoT4Enabled' is not recognized", although it had just read all three, and its monthly check counted T4's 7-day restart for the rest of the month. Since 654145e (2026-11-04), the script called `Test-DemoT4Enabled` and `Get-DemoT4RestartCoverage`, two of the module's internal functions, from its own scope, where they aren't visible, so no signed-in estimate ever read whether a safety stop covers the restart: it counted 720 hours ($256.32 at `Standard_D4ds_v5`, a dated example) where the nightly safety stop holds it to about 96 ($34.18). Preflight and `start-demo.ps1` weren't affected: they read it inside the module.

**Work summary.**

1. **The script keeps the module it imported** (`$module = Import-Module ... -PassThru`, as `start-demo.ps1` does since 2026-11-10) and runs the two internal functions through it (`& $module { ... }`).
2. **Each read stands on its own:** the sign-in (`Assert-DemoAzContext`), the Defender for Cloud plans, the T3 free offer, the T2 golden snapshots, and the safety stop's coverage each have their own `try`. One that fails is one **Warning** line that says what the estimate left out; the others are still read. Not signed in is one line that names everything it leaves out.

**Changed files.** `scripts/estimate-cost.ps1`; `tests/unit/DbHubDemo.EstimateCost.Tests.ps1` (new); `CHANGELOG.md`; and this report.

**Validation.** `Invoke-Pester -Path tests/unit/DbHubDemo.EstimateCost.Tests.ps1`: 4 passed. Against `main`'s `scripts/estimate-cost.ps1`, the same 4 fail: the coverage is read 0 times, and none of the new lines is written. **Live:** the owner's kind of configuration signed in, 2026-11-13, before the fix: the misleading warning and the rest-of-month restart.

**Risks.** R823 new.

### T4's read replica, for each session (2026-11-13)

**Why.** User-directed, 2026-11-13 ("Postgres HA/DR"): add a read replica of T4 to the one-click deployment and its upgrade; account for the replica's lag and PostgreSQL's health in the activity notebook and the Insights app; keep it efficient and cost manageable; and break nothing, for new users and for those who deployed before. Database Hub's PostgreSQL dashboard charts **Read replica lag** (`physical_replication_delay_in_seconds`, on replicas only), which stayed empty because T4 had no replica. Hyperscale, an HA standby, and Azure SQL geo-replication are out of scope ([ADR 0025](adr/0025-t4-read-replica.md)).

**Work summary.**

1. **A live probe first** (West US 3, two `Standard_D2ds_v5` servers in a delegated subnet, about $1, deleted the same day):
   - A replica took 460 to 525 seconds to create, and a second deployment of its template fails (`ReadReplicaAlreadyExistWithGivenName`). A replica of a stopped primary is refused (`ReadReplicaServerInUnexpectedState`).
   - Azure enforces the power order both ways (`SourceReplicasStartStopOrder`).
   - Deleting a replica took about 100 seconds and left the primary Ready, and a deleted replica's metrics answer `ResourceNotFound`.
   - `max_standby_streaming_delay` is settable on the replica, and an idle replica's lag was 2 to 6 seconds.
2. **One replica per session** (ADR 0025's R1, approved within the owner's delegated scope). A lasting replica would bill its storage and Defender plans all month, and add a 7-day restart of its own: a first deployment's worst-case month would be about $576 against the $375 ceiling. Per session, that month is $315.82, with no change to the ceilings, the restart rule, or any role.
3. **The template and the module** (`infra/replica/pgreplica01.bicep`, `Private/T4ReplicaHelpers.ps1`):
   - `pgreplica01-<deploymentId>` is a same-region replica in T4's subnet and private DNS zone, at T4's actual size, with `max_standby_streaming_delay` 600000 ms.
   - Its creation starts without waiting and finishes later. It has the size fallback: only `SkuNotAvailable` moves it on, from T4's size to another zone, then to larger documented sizes, never fewer vCores, after the `Dropping` shell is gone.
   - The rest: the records (`DbHubT4ReplicaSize`, and `DbHubT4Replica` for an environment that has it), the delete, the start-first and stop-after order, the checks (`T4.REPLICA`, `METRICS.T4.REPLICA`, `HUB.ESTATE.T4.REPLICA`, `STATUS.T4.REPLICA`), DONE's gate, and the history's capture.
4. **The scripts:**
   - `deploy.ps1`: the T4 track's Replica step, DONE's requirements and gate, the status page's T4 row, and the replica's notes in DONE and NOT DONE.
   - `start-demo.ps1`: created once T4 is Ready and waited for at the end; `-SkipT4Replica` leaves it out.
   - `stop-demo.ps1`: the history's capture first, then the delete, in parallel with the VMs.
   - Also `status.ps1`, `validate.ps1`, `reset-demo.ps1` through the runner, `destroy.ps1` (deleted before the group), preflight (`PREFLIGHT.T4.REPLICA`), and `estimate-cost.ps1` (a **Replica session** column).
5. **Older environments:**
   - Without `DbHubT4Replica`, every script says "isn't deployed yet: run ./scripts/deploy.ps1", as **Not selected** or a **Warning**, never a **Fail**, and changes nothing. A plain `./scripts/deploy.ps1` adds the replica.
   - Coordinator direction: `deploy.ps1` republishes the on-demand control's runbooks when the control is set up (`Update-DemoActivityControlRunbook`, `CONTROL.RUNBOOKS`). When it can't, it's a **Warning**, with what fails until then and the exact command.
6. **The runbooks** (`DbHubControl.Common.ps1`):
   - The nightly safety stop, its T3 check, the control's T4 stop, and the auto-stop stop a replica a session left running, once T4 is Stopped.
   - A control run starts a stopped replica before T4, and says plainly when there's none: the replica beat isn't available, and `start-demo.ps1` creates the replica.
   - No role changes: the roles already allow read, start, and stop on flexible servers at the demo resource group.
7. **Cost** (`Get-DemoCostEstimate`):
   - It counts the replica's compute, storage, and Defender plans for a session's running hours only, with evidence and output fields such as `T4ReplicaSession` and `SessionCostWithoutReplica`.
   - The owner kept `sessionCeilingUsd` at $15. `PREFLIGHT.COST.SESSION` names the replica's share and `-SkipT4Replica` when a session is over it.
   - T4's one-time move to `Standard_D4ds_v5` (`ConvertTo-DemoT4FallbackCost`) is decided without that share, so `demo-day` keeps its move.
8. **The runner** (`workload-generator`, `database/postgresql`, `vm/bootstrap`):
   - `--replica-server` for T4's commands, and `profile run --t4-replica-server`.
   - The `replica-lag` scenario (`scenarios/replica-lag`, `demo.usp_scenario_replica_lag`, `demo.replica_lag_marks`). `stop` and `reset` end the demo's sessions on the replica, and are **Not selected** there when it isn't there.
   - T1's settings carry `t4.replicaServerFqdn` (empty on a Burstable T4); the control's relay and the activity host pass it on.
   - Against a local PostgreSQL 18.7 primary and hot standby, the replica's lag went 7.9, 22.5, then 36.8 seconds during a report, and 0.1 after it.
9. **The notebook and the Insights app, evaluated and changed:**
   - The activity notebook had no T4 content. A Fabric notebook can't read Azure Monitor (its tokens don't cover Azure Resource Manager), and T4 is private. So the operator's scripts read the metrics (`Get-DemoPostgresHistoryParameter`, 5-minute bins, at most 24 KiB) and pass them as `POSTGRES_METRICS`; `stop-demo.ps1 -SaveHistory` reads them before the delete.
     - On T4: CPU, memory, connections, failed connections, and replication bytes.
     - On the replica: Read Replica Lag, CPU, and connections.
   - The notebook's new PostgreSQL section checks that document, then adds rows (analysis `postgresql`, targets `T4` and `T4-replica`) and findings (a lag of 60 seconds or more, CPU, failed connections).
   - The history model's Target and Analysis dimensions add them, and the Insights app gets a **PostgreSQL** page with lag and health time lines (16 queries).
   - The notebook's estate pulse, locks, consumption, and correlation sections stay SQL-only: their source, the telemetry endpoint, has no PostgreSQL data.
   - Coordinator direction (2026-11-13, with the capacity paused for the live tests): a `-SaveHistory` that can't save mustn't lose the replica's metrics without saying so. So when the notebook run doesn't save them, `stop-demo.ps1` keeps the captured document in `out/history-pending` (`Save-DemoPostgresHistoryPending`, `STOP.T4.HISTORY.PENDING`, a **Warning** with the replica's peak lag and the command). `configure-fabric.ps1 -RunLiveActivity -PostgresMetricsPath <file>` adds it once the capacity runs, then moves the file to `out/history-pending/saved`. Without the parameter, `-RunLiveActivity` sends T4's and a running replica's metrics, after the subscription guard only.
10. **Live findings, fixed the same day:**
    - **A new deployment (`rg-dbhubha-demo`):** the T4 track waited for `max_connections`' pending restart, whose flag cleared while T4 was still restarting, and sent the replica. Azure refused it, `ReadReplicaServerInUnexpectedState`: "Cannot perform operation on read replica 'pgflex01-...' because it's in 'Restarting' state". The status page showed the T4 row's Replica step as Failed, with Azure's error.
      - Now the replica waits for T4 to read Ready.
      - A refusal of that kind (`SourceNotReady`) goes out again at the same size once T4 is Ready and has settled, at most 3 times. It's never taken for a size refusal.
      - If it still fails, the fix says so.
    - **The upgrade (`rg-dbhubup-demo`):** main's run had recorded T4's track at Telemetry, so the resume skipped the new Replica step, and the status page said it "Finished in an earlier run". DONE's gate would still have created the replica, out of sight of the T4 row.
      - Now a resume runs the Replica step until the environment has the replica (`DbHubT4Replica`).
    - **The new deployment's resume, after the refusal above:** the Replica step had recorded `DbHubT4Replica` whatever its outcome, so the resume skipped it as well, and only DONE's gate would have created the replica, out of sight of T4's row.
      - Now the step records it only once the replica is created, or isn't supported on a Burstable T4, so a resume runs a failed one again, on T4's row.
    - **The upgrade, after its replica was created** (`pgreplica01-aka7ep`, AsyncReplica at T4's `Standard_D4ds_v5`, from the resume's Replica step on the environment `main` deployed):
      - T4's Replica step stopped right after the creation: `Get-DemoT4ReplicaMetricSnapshot`'s private directory prefix had 22 characters, over the 20 that `Initialize-DemoPrivateDirectory` allows. Its new test found that it also piped `Get-DemoMemberList`'s list whole into `Where-Object`, so every point was dropped and `METRICS.T4.REPLICA`, a DONE requirement, would always have read no data. Both are fixed (ed1a394); no test had run the reader, whose callers are mocked one level up.
      - `replica-lag` was refused on T1 ("replica-lag needs T4's read replica, and T4's read replica isn't known"): the upgrade resumed `main`'s unfinished run, which skips the template, so T1's settings came from the older template's outputs, without the replica's name. A resume now adds `t4.replicaServerName` and `t4.replicaServerFqdn` to them (`Add-DemoT4ReplicaLoaderSetting`), as the template does; T1's loader runs again on such an upgrade, because its bundle changed. `demo-control.ps1` had reported **Pass** for setting the profile; the refusal shows in the runner's log on `sqlvm01` only.
      - The upgrade's `stop-demo.ps1 -SaveHistory` deleted the replica itself (accepted 00:14:18Z, Succeeded 00:16:11Z), then said `STOP.T4.REPLICA` "isn't there, so there's nothing to delete": a second delete call read it gone. It now says it was deleted (437afa9; live on the new deployment at 01:19Z).
    - **`demo-control.ps1` said Pass for a `replica-lag` the runner couldn't run, twice.** On the upgrade, T1's settings didn't name the replica (above). On the new deployment at 00:44Z, the safety stop's 19:30 pass (DbHub-Stop `-Scope T3Check`, ADR 0024) had stopped T4 and the replica, and `CONTROL.T4` still said **Pass**: `profile set` only stores the profile, and T1's profile host runs it later, where only its log says why it can't. Coordinator direction: the scenario is new on this branch, and failures surface.
      - Before it sends `replica-lag`, `Invoke-DemoControl` reads T4 and the replica from this PC (`Get-DemoT4ReplicaLagBlock`). T4 isn't Ready, the environment isn't set up for the replica, or the replica is missing, stopped, being created, or being deleted: `CONTROL.T4` is a **Warning** with the fix (`start-demo.ps1` or `deploy.ps1`), and nothing is sent. A Burstable T4 is **Not supported**. Other scenarios aren't read.
      - T1's settings are only on `sqlvm01`, so the relay checks them there, in the same Run Command: a `profile set` of `incident:replica-lag` for T4 whose `workload-install.json` names no replica is refused, with `replicaKnown` false, and nothing is stored. `demo-control.ps1` reports it as a **Warning** whose fix is `deploy.ps1`. The on-demand control's dispatches reach the same refusal, but don't wait for their result; the notebook orchestration's design shows it in the notebook's output.
      - `demo-control.ps1` writes no status page: the console's table and `out/demo-control.jsonl` carry the record, as for every `CONTROL.*`.
      - Tests: `DbHubDemo.Lifecycle.Tests.ps1` (T4 stopped, as live; the replica missing, stopped, or being created; not set up; Burstable; sent once all is Ready; `sqlvm01`'s refusal) and `Vm.WorkloadSteps.Tests.ps1` (the relay's refusal). Both fail on the code before the fix: **Pass**, where they expect **Warning** and **Fail**.
