### A Run Command name stuck in Deleting (live finding, 2026-11-13)

**Why.** Coordinator direction, 2026-11-13: fix it on this branch, in its own commit, although `main` has it too, because it held both live tests and would hold a new user's first deployment for hours. The requirements: a name stuck in Deleting never holds a run for more than about 15 minutes; the console, the status page, and **DONE** or **NOT DONE** say what happened, with the fix; no new manual step; a test; new and upgrading users both work.

**Root cause, from about 4 hours of `archost01`'s activity log on both test environments:**

- On the new host, Azure ended 27 of 29 real Run Command deletes with `InternalExecutionError` ("An internal execution error occurred. Please retry later.") after 343 to 676 seconds; 2 succeeded, after 386 and 429. Creates ended the same way after 344 to 661 seconds, though their scripts had finished within a minute. The upgrade host's log has the same pattern.
- A name whose delete failed stays marked for deletion: a PUT of it fails with `OperationNotAllowed` ("You can only retry the Delete operation"). `Invoke-DemoVmRunCommand` reused the name: it deleted it, waited 5 minutes, created it into that conflict, and waited 3 more minutes to delete it again. So each of T2's health reads took 8 minutes and failed, and `main`'s own run on the upgrade environment looped on them for 3 hours.
- Not the host's CPU (4 to 18% on average) or its own network setup (it blocks Azure's platform addresses only for the guest's switch port). `sqlvm01` doesn't show it. Azure takes 6 to 11 minutes to confirm each extension operation on the T2 host and mostly gives up, so a second delete sent within that window would only preempt the first. A new name ran at once.

**Work summary.**

1. **A fresh name** (`Resolve-DemoRunCommandFreshName`): when Azure still lists the name after the leftover wait (`-LeftoverWaitSeconds`, 300 by default), the script runs as `<name>-yyyyMMddHHmmss`. One read of the VM's Run Commands comes first: earlier fresh copies of the name, and chunk Run Commands left from finished transfers, get a delete without waiting, and with 24 or more listed (live, 20 were already listed on the new host, 9 of them such chunks), every state counting (Azure allows 25 and doesn't say whether one being deleted counts), there's no fresh one, and it throws as a Run Command that couldn't be created. A call that created nothing sends the delete again, without a second wait. The result has `UsedName`.
   - Live on the new host (825be6a, 17:36), each read then completed, but still took about 11 minutes: the whole leftover wait for a name known to be stuck, and 3 minutes waiting for the fresh name's own delete, which Azure doesn't finish there either. So later in the same process, a name that was stuck is waited for 30 seconds at most (`$script:DemoRunCommandStuckName`), and a fresh name's own delete isn't waited for.
   - Live again (ed1a394, 18:35), the host listed 20 Run Commands, 9 of them chunks left from finished transfers, and every read stopped at the limit check while T2's Ready wait polled each minute. So finished chunks get a delete too, the check allows up to 24, and the T2 host's waits (`Wait-DemoVmHealthState`, `Wait-DemoT2HostBuild`) stop after 15 minutes of reads that find no room, with that reason (`Full`; `DEPLOY.T2.WAIT`, `DEPLOY.T2.READY`), instead of polling until their deadline.
2. **What it says:** a **Warning** line on the console at once; `DEPLOY.RUNCOMMAND.STUCK_<VM>` (`Get-DemoRunCommandStuckResult`), a **Warning** on the row of the step where it happened (T2's host build and Arc onboarding rows included, and the host-build row while it lasts), reported once; and a note in **DONE** and **NOT DONE** (`Get-DemoRunCommandStuckNote`), which the status page's banner shows too.

**Changed files.** `scripts/modules/DbHubDemo/DbHubDemo.psm1`, `Public/Invoke-DemoVmRunCommand.ps1`, and in `Private/`: `RunCommandHelpers.ps1`, `TrackHelpers.ps1`, `ParallelDeployment.ps1`, `DeployExperience.ps1`, and `GuidedStopHelpers.ps1`; the tests in `tests/unit/DbHubDemo.Arc.Tests.ps1`, `DbHubDemo.Tracks.Tests.ps1`, and `DbHubDemo.OneCommand.Tests.ps1`; `docs/troubleshooting.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and this report.

**Validation.** `Invoke-Pester` on the Arc, OneCommand, and Tracks tests: 344 passed. On `main`'s module (3881ea1, in a separate worktree), both new Arc tests fail: it keeps no record of a stuck name and has no fresh name. Live, `main` creates the stuck name again and fails with `OperationNotAllowed` (the new-user run's log, above). PSScriptAnalyzer on the changed files: no findings.

**Not this fix:** the upgrade host's VM agent stopped reporting after its 2026-11-13 start ("VM status blob is found but not yet populated"); the start ended `VMStartTimedOut` after 71 minutes, and the watchdog's restart stayed pending for over an hour. No Run Command runs on a VM in that state, under any name. It goes to the owner as a separate finding.

**Risks.** R832 new.

### A first run that met a paused capacity never created the workspace (live finding, 2026-11-13)

**Why.** Coordinator direction, 2026-11-13: fix it on this branch, in its own commit; `main` has it too, and it breaks one-click. On the upgrade test environment (`rg-dbhubup-demo`), `main`'s first run reached its Fabric step at 17:07 ET while the capacity "fabricmbprod" was paused.

- `FABRIC.RESOLVE.WORKSPACE` was **Manual action required**: "doesn't exist, and it can't be created: The capacity "fabricmbprod" (F4) is Inactive".
- The step's outcome counted only a **Fail**, so `DbHubTrackFabric` recorded Fabric.
- Every later run resumed past it ("Finished in an earlier run"), with the capacity running, so the workspace was never created. DONE's `FABRIC.ITEMS.REQUIRED` would say "Run ./scripts/deploy.ps1 again: its Fabric track creates the workspace", which no rerun did.

**Work summary.**

1. **Not recorded** (`Invoke-DemoDeploymentTrack`): a Fabric step whose Fabric or Power BI records include **Manual action required** ends Open, as T1's T3 step does for its group.
   - It isn't recorded, `DEPLOY.TRACK.FABRIC` is a **Warning**, and the run ends **NOT DONE**, naming the paused capacity first (#50).
   - The next `deploy.ps1` runs it again. The Insights app's records still never count.
2. **Older records** (`Get-DemoFabricTrackRecheck`, `Resolve-DemoTrackPlan -ReopenFabric`): a resume whose `DbHubTrackFabric` says Fabric runs `FABRIC.ITEMS.REQUIRED`'s read-only check before it plans.
   - A **Fail** (a list answered without the workspace, the lakehouse, or an item) runs the step again: its record is lowered first (`Get-DemoTrackRecordReset`), and its rows on the status page say why.
   - Anything else (everything there, a paused capacity, access, throttling, an error) leaves the plan as recorded. It costs a few Fabric reads on such a resume.

**Changed files.** In `scripts/modules/DbHubDemo/Private/`: `TrackHelpers.ps1`, `ParallelDeployment.ps1`, `DeployExperience.ps1`, and `ProgressHelpers.ps1`; `tests/unit/DbHubDemo.Tracks.Tests.ps1`; `CHANGELOG.md`, and this report.

**Validation.** `Invoke-Pester` on `DbHubDemo.Tracks.Tests.ps1`: 149 passed. On `main` (3881ea1, in a separate worktree), both new tests fail. The Fabric step ends Pass and is recorded, and the resume doesn't run it ("Expected 'track Fabric: Fabric' to be found"). **Live:** it waits for the orchestration's live test, as the coordinator decided, so the capacity isn't kept on for it; `rg-dbhubup-demo` keeps the record that shows it.

**Risks.** R833 new.

### The nightly stop waits for a running `deploy.ps1` (2026-11-14)

**Why.** Coordinator decision, 2026-11-14, for the user, who reviews it before anything merges: "The nightly stop must not cut off a running deploy or session", first in the notebook orchestration's stack, in its own commits. Live on 2026-11-13 in `rg-dbhubha-demo`, the 19:00 `DbHub-Stop -Scope Nightly` stopped T4 and deallocated `archost01` in the middle of `deploy.ps1`, `sqlvm01`'s own auto-shutdown deallocated it, and the 19:30 T3 check stopped T4 and its replica right after the next run's checks. A first deployment takes about 91 minutes, so a new user who starts after about 17:30 meets it; `main` has the same behavior.

**Work summary.**

1. **The runbook** (`automation/runbooks/DbHubControl.Common.ps1`, `Get-DbHubBusyMarker`, `Get-DbHubBusyDeferral`): `Nightly`, `T3Check`, and `T4` return `Deferred` and change nothing while the group's `DbHubBusyUntilUtc` is ahead by at most `busyMarkerMaximumMinutes` (180), read at the job's start; an expired, too-far, or unreadable marker is ignored, with a log line for the last two. `All` is never deferred. `DbHub-Stop.ps1` fails a job only for `Error`, `Partial`, and `NotGranted`, so a `Deferred` job completes. Both runbook settings (the safety stop's and the control's) carry the maximum.
2. **The marker and its refresher** (`scripts/modules/DbHubDemo/Private/BusyMarkerHelpers.ps1`, new): `DbHubBusyUntilUtc` and `DbHubBusyBy` in `Get-DemoDeploymentStateTagName`, written with `az tag update --operation Merge`. `Start-DemoDeploymentRun -BusyMarker` (only `deploy.ps1` passes it) starts `dbhub-busy-marker`, a job with its own subscription guard, which refreshes every 10 minutes (every 2 until the first write), checks the auto-shutdown every 2 minutes in the 16 minutes before its time, and ends when `deploy.ps1`'s process is gone. The tracks' wait loop relays its lines to the console.
3. **One refresh** (`Update-DemoBusyMarker`): the marker 60 minutes ahead; the VMs' auto-shutdown moved to a quarter hour about an hour after the marker when it would come before the marker plus 15 minutes (Global Schedules - Get, then Create Or Update with every property kept); and, once the marker is written and one of the night's passes falls inside the run, `dbhub-safety-deferred` (hourly, Scope `Nightly`, from the marker's end plus 5 minutes until 12 hours after that pass), unless one runs tonight already. The status page's new **Nightly stop** row says so.
4. **The end** (`Complete-DemoBusyMarkerRun`, from `Complete-DemoDeploymentRun`, whose outcome's `Added` `deploy.ps1` adds to its report): a run the stop waited for, or one that started during an earlier run's grace, gets `deploy-grace` for 60 minutes, the deferred pass and the auto-shutdown at its end plus 5 minutes, and `DEPLOY.NIGHTLYSTOP` (**Warning**) that **DONE**, **NOT DONE** (`Get-DemoBusyMarkerNote`), and the row repeat. Otherwise everything is put back and the marker cleared. Ctrl+C writes the marker expired as `ended`, with no read. A step that fails leaves `ended`, which the next run settles.
5. **`start-demo.ps1` and `stop-demo.ps1`** (`Resolve-DemoBusyNightlyStop`, `START.NIGHTLYSTOP`, `STOP.NIGHTLYSTOP`): only when the marker's tag holds anything; `start-demo.ps1` leaves a live `deploy` or `session` marker alone. **`status.ps1`:** `STATUS.NIGHTLYSTOP` (`Get-DemoBusyMarkerStatus`). `Get-DemoSafetyStopStatus` and `Get-DemoT4RestartCoverage` count `Deferred` as no failure.

**Changed files.** `automation/runbooks/DbHubControl.Common.ps1` and `DbHub-Stop.ps1`; in `scripts/modules/DbHubDemo/`: `Private/BusyMarkerHelpers.ps1` (new), `DeployHelpers.ps1`, `SafetyStopHelpers.ps1`, `ActivityControlHelpers.ps1`, `T4Helpers.ps1`, `DeployExperience.ps1`, `ProgressHelpers.ps1`, `ParallelDeployment.ps1`, and `Public/Start-DemoDeploymentRun.ps1`, `Complete-DemoDeploymentRun.ps1`, `Get-DemoDeploymentState.ps1`, `Set-DemoDeploymentState.ps1`, `Start-DemoEnvironment.ps1`, `Stop-DemoEnvironment.ps1`, `Get-DemoEnvironmentStatus.ps1`; `scripts/deploy.ps1`; tests `Automation.Runbooks.Tests.ps1`, `DbHubDemo.SafetyStop.Tests.ps1`, `DbHubDemo.OneCommand.Tests.ps1`, `DbHubDemo.Progress.Tests.ps1`; ADR 0024, the README, `AGENTS.md`, deployment, troubleshooting, `CHANGELOG.md`, and this report.

**Validation.** `Invoke-Pester` on the runbook, safety stop, one-command, progress, lifecycle, tracks, activity control, and the other files that call the changed functions: 1,352 passed, 0 failed. The new runbook and module tests fail on the code before this change (no `Deferred`, no marker). **Live (2026-11-14, `rg-dbhubha-demo`, stopped; nothing started):** the new `DbHub-Stop` published; `Nightly` and `T3Check` jobs completed `Deferred` with a marker ahead, and `Nightly` did the usual stop with it expired; a refresh scheduled `dbhub-safety-deferred` (hourly, Scope `Nightly`, start and expiry as designed); the run's end set the grace, the pass, and both VMs' auto-shutdown to 00:50 with `DEPLOY.NIGHTLYSTOP` and DONE's note; `STATUS.NIGHTLYSTOP` showed it; `stop-demo.ps1`'s settlement put everything back (ADR 0024's [validation](adr/0024-nightly-safety-stop.md#validation)). Still to do live: a `deploy.ps1` across the stop's time with its refresher. Run all and the capacity-dependent checks wait for the user's resume of the capacity.

8. **A Failed SQL IaaS Agent extension is repaired** (the coordinator's decision, 2026-11-16: a new user who needs the portal breaks the one-click rule). Live, the new-user test environment's first run ended **NOT DONE** on `T1.SQLVM.MONITORING`: "The SqlIaasExtension on sqlvm01 is Failed, not Succeeded", from "Login failed for user 'NT Service\MSSQLSERVER'. Reason: Server is in single user mode". `Invoke-DemoSqlVmMonitoringWait`, which the Monitoring step, `-Sequential`'s stage, and `start-demo.ps1` after it recreates T3 run, now calls `Repair-DemoSqlIaasExtension` when that result's extension is Failed:
   - **Only when it's safe,** read again first: the extension is Failed now; `sqlvm01` is running; T1's bootstrap is Ready, the SQL Server service runs, and `SERVERPROPERTY('IsSingleUser')` is 0 over a Windows-authentication connection, which a server in single-user mode refuses with error 18461 (`Get-DemoSqlVmSqlMode`, one read-only Run Command); and this process hasn't repaired it already.
   - **The documented repair:** [Sql Virtual Machines - Redeploy](https://learn.microsoft.com/rest/api/sqlvm/sql-virtual-machines/redeploy) (api-version 2023-10-01, "Uninstalls and reinstalls the SQL IaaS Extension"), the API behind the portal's Repair. The Contributor role allows it: `Microsoft.SqlVirtualMachine/sqlVirtualMachines/redeploy/action` is within its `*`, and none of its `notActions` names it (read with `az role definition list --name Contributor` and `az provider operation show`, 2026-11-16). Then at most 15 minutes for the extension to report Succeeded; a Failed counts only after a state of the reinstall, since the old Failed shows first.
   - **What a repair drops:** "If you repair or reinstall the SQL IaaS Agent extension, your settings aren't preserved, other than licensing changes" ([Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-sql/virtual-machines/windows/sql-agent-extension-troubleshoot-known-issues#repair-extension)). The SQL virtual machine's own PUT, as `infra/modules/sqlvm01.bicep` sends it (LOCAL connectivity on port 1433, automatic upgrade, with the resource's location, tags, VM, and license type, which the repair keeps), then a read with `$expand=*` that verifies each one; then `Enable-DemoSqlVmMonitoring` merges the monitoring flag again. A test compares the settings with the template's, so a setting the template adds later fails it until the repair sends it too.
   - **What it shows:** `DEPLOY.T1.SQLIAAS.REPAIR` (or `START.`), first in the step's results, so the Monitoring row shows it. A repair is a **Warning** on the console, the row, and **DONE** (`Get-DemoSqlIaasRepairNote`), with the reason, the minutes, and what was re-applied and verified. A repair that can't run (the VM, the bootstrap, single-user mode, a read that fails) or that fails (refused, failed again, still Failed after 15 minutes) is a **Fail** with the reason and the portal's Repair; settings that couldn't be re-applied or verified are a **Fail** with `./scripts/deploy.ps1 -FromStage Infrastructure`, whose template sends them again.
   - **The template's order stays,** since existing demos redeploy it.
9. **Stale Fabric items after a resumed upgrade** (R853; found live at 13:49, the coordinator: fix it now). main's environment had finished its Fabric step in an unfinished run, so the resumed upgrade skipped it and kept main's notebook, history model, and app. Run all's history job would have passed T4's metrics and the session's window to a notebook that ignores them, losing them with no word.
   - **The stamp:** `Get-DemoFabricContentSha256`, one SHA-256 over what the Fabric step publishes from this copy: the notebooks, the dashboard, the history model and report, and the Insights app's source, without dependencies, build output, Markdown, or deploy-time files, with LF line endings (235 ms on a checkout whose `fabric/app` has a local `node_modules` of 52,886 files, which the walk never enters; the same value on a clean checkout). The Fabric step records it (`DbHubFabricSha256`) with the step once the app's summary is Done too, so a workspace with the new notebook but an older app or model is published again.
   - **The comparison:** `Get-DemoFabricContentReopen`, on a resume whose record says the Fabric step finished, before any Fabric read; on `-Sequential -Resume` after its Fabric stage too. Different or missing: the step runs again, and the console and the Fabric rows say why.
   - **Why the resource group and not the items:** a description stamped on each Fabric item would need a Fabric read per item on every resume, which a paused capacity refuses, and the Insights app's item has no documented definition API to read it from. People can also edit an item's description in Fabric. The resource group's tag needs no Fabric call, can't drift from what the step wrote, and is written only after all of it, the app included, was published.
   - **`"importNotebooks": false`:** `deploy.ps1` keeps the workspace's notebooks as they are, by design (Phase 26a); the history's fix text names `./scripts/configure-fabric.ps1` then, not `deploy.ps1`.
10. **The lag finding after a stopped replica restarts** (R854; found live on 2026-11-13, the user through the coordinator: no known bug ships unfixed). Azure Monitor's Read replica lag is "the time since the last replayed transaction" when the primary has no transactions, so a replica that was stopped reads at least the time since then until T4 writes again: 1,380 seconds at 01:00 on 2026-11-13, before the `replica-lag` beat's 219. The notebook's `_pg_lag_catch_up` and the app's `replicaCatchUp` apply one rule: after a gap of 10 minutes (and two intervals) or more in the replica's series, or after the window's start, the leading points that reach half the time since the last point before the gap are the replica's catch-up. The lag finding's peak, and the app's insight and marked peak, leave them out and say so ("Left out: 1 point from 01:00 UTC, up to 1380.0 s, the replica's catch-up after its restart ..."); a capture with only catch-up is a **Pass** that says that. The rows keep every point. Tests with the Nov 13 data: `Fabric.Notebooks.Tests.ps1` (Python) and the app's `insights.test.ts`; a fresh replica's small first points and a 300-second beat right after a short gap stay lag.
11. **A stopped replica's start-first shows on T4's start record** (R855; found on 2026-11-13). `start-demo.ps1` and `deploy.ps1` start a stopped replica before T4, because Azure starts T4 only after its replicas, and that record (`START.T4.REPLICA.START`) lived only in `START.T4.START`'s evidence: T4's message said "is now running (Ready)", and a start-first **Warning** (the replica not Ready within its wait) showed nowhere unless T4's own start then failed. `Invoke-DemoT4PowerAction` now adds the start-first record's message to T4's, and takes its status, with its fix, when that's worse. A test in `DbHubDemo.T4Replica.Tests.ps1` fails on the code before it.

**The monitoring flag before T1's loader** (first a follow-up; built the same day, the user through the coordinator: no known bug ships unfixed). The race isn't the template's: on the new-user test environment the template finished at 16:55, before any bootstrap ran. T1's Bootstraps step started the loader at 17:16:28 and merged the monitoring flag right after it (ADR 0018), and that update of the SqlIaasExtension failed at 17:20:36, while the bootstrap's lockout recovery had SQL Server in single-user mode. The step now waits for `sqlvm01`'s extensions to settle (the loader's own settle, once per step), merges the flag, and then runs the loader: VM extension operations run one at a time, so the update ends before the bootstrap starts. It costs about 4 minutes on T1's track, which isn't the critical path (T2's build is longer), and changes only runs that write the flag, that is, first deployments; in an existing environment the flag is set, so nothing is written. Its live test is the fresh first deployment on the final head.

**"The Run Commands on the VM could not be listed"** (R856; found 2026-11-16 in the window's logs, the coordinator's decision: fix it, as the last separate commit, cause first). The Warning showed for T1 or T2 in nearly every deploy, `main`'s own build included, while the list it named had worked:

- **The capture:** a watcher kept the Azure CLI's own command logs (`~/.azure/commands`, which keep the last 25) during the window, and a reproduction on the stopped new-user test VM ran the real sequence: start, extensions settled, then `Send-DemoChunkSet` with the 48fafeb module. The list exited 0 at 15:30:59, and the Warning followed at 15:31:01; it showed again at the send's end. Throttling (16 parallel lists on one VM), concurrency (8 across VMs), a VM's start (81 lists during it), and a `Start-Job` process like a track's all passed.
- **The cause, in our code:** `Get-DemoChunkRunCommandName` returned `@(...)`, which PowerShell unrolls; with no chunk Run Command on the VM, the usual case, the callers got `$null`, which they read as "couldn't be listed". The same unrolling made `Wait-DemoChunkRunCommandGone` return every name it had asked to delete once Azure had deleted them all, so `DEPLOY.ARTIFACTS.CLEANUP_<VM>` ("Azure is still deleting ...") was a **Warning** whether or not anything was left.
- **The fix:** the function returns its list with the unary comma, so an empty list stays a list. A failed list is tried again, up to 3 times 5 seconds apart, with nothing added when the first try works; a try that a later one makes up for is logged with az's error, and after 3 failed tries the **Warning** keeps az's error, redacted (`Protect-DemoText`), with what to do: nothing, the next cleanup checks again, and `./scripts/status.ps1` lists any Run Command that stays.
- **Tests:** four in `DbHubDemo.Bundle.Tests.ps1` fail on 48fafeb: no **Warning** when the VM has no chunk Run Commands; no leftover when the deletes are done by the first look; a failed list tried again, with the leftover still deleted first; and three failed lists, with the redacted error in the **Warning**.
- **Live:** the deploy rows stay on 48fafeb; this commit changes only the list's path, and its live proof is the smallest real call, `Clear-DemoChunkRunCommand` and `Wait-DemoChunkRunCommandGone` on a running test VM, with the old and the new module.

**Every Azure call that waits on a VM, bounded** (R857; live on 2026-11-16, the coordinator's decision: fix the whole class). The upgrade test's T2 track sent its chunks to `archost01`; one stayed Pending for 900 seconds, so the watchdog ran `az vm restart` at 15:06. Azure accepted it at 15:06:36 and hadn't finished it 40 minutes later (provisioning Updating, no power state, agent Not Ready), and the call had no limit. The restart now goes with `--no-wait` and a 15-minute wait for its end, then one deallocate and start, bounded, with the T2 guest shut down cleanly first when the host's agent is Ready ([ADR 0003](adr/0003-t2-host-size-security-type-bootstrap.md#2026-11-16-amendment-a-restart-azure-doesnt-finish)). The audit, of every call `deploy.ps1` and the lifecycle scripts make that can wait on a VM:

| Call | Where | Bound |
|---|---|---|
| `az vm restart` (the watchdog) | `Restart-DemoVmOnce` | **Now** `--no-wait`, 15 minutes for Azure to finish it and the agent to be Ready, then one deallocate and start in 20 minutes; else a **Fail** |
| `az vm start`, `az vm deallocate` | `Invoke-DemoVmPowerAction`, `Request-DemoVmStart` (deploy, start, stop, and the recovery) | Already: `--no-wait`, then the power state polled for 900 seconds at most (a **Warning** when it's still moving) |
| The T2 guest's clean shutdown | `Stop-DemoGuestVm` (`STOP.GUEST`) | Already: 180 seconds, then the host's deallocation stops the guest anyway |
| `az vm extension set` (T1's monitoring flag) | `Enable-DemoSqlVmMonitoring`, through `Invoke-DemoAzWithConflictRetry` | **Now** 20 minutes a try (the function's new `-TimeoutSeconds`); a time-out is the step's existing **Fail** |
| `az vm run-command invoke` (action Run Command), T1's SQL for T3 | `Invoke-DemoT3SqlFromT1` | **Now** its batches' time limit plus 15 minutes, 90 at most; Azure's own limit is 90 minutes |
| `az vm run-command invoke`, the workload actions (`EnableT3`, `EnableT4`, `Runner`, `StopGuest`) | `Invoke-DemoWorkloadAction` | **Now** by default: the runner's own limit plus its ready wait and 10 minutes, otherwise 30 minutes; `StopGuest` passes its own |
| Managed Run Command create (`PUT`) and its wait | `Invoke-DemoVmRunCommand`, `Send-DemoChunkSet` | Already: `az rest` returns at once; the wait is bounded (each chunk 600 seconds, a Run Command 1,800 by default, with a start time limit) |
| Managed Run Command delete | `Remove-DemoRunCommand`, the chunk cleanups | Already: `az rest` returns at once; the waits are bounded (120 seconds at a send's end, 30 seconds or a fresh name for a name in Deleting) |
| T4's and the replica's start, stop, and restart; the SQL IaaS Agent's repair | `Invoke-DemoT4PowerAction`, the replica helpers, `Repair-DemoSqlIaasExtension` | Already: `az rest` `POST` returns at once; the waits are bounded |
| Template deployments | the control's, the safety stop's, and the replica's templates | Already: 900 to 1,800 seconds, or the replica's own creation time limit. The main template has no client bound: Azure Resource Manager fails each resource at its own limit (a VM's provisioning, an extension, a Run Command's `timeoutInSeconds`) |
| **Each `az rest` call** (R862, added the same day: a status read got no answer for over 2 hours) | `Invoke-DemoAz`, for every caller that sets no limit | **Now** 300 seconds; a stopped call is a failed call, so the waits above reach their own limits. Other commands go through the Azure SDK's transport, which has a read time limit of its own |
| Fabric, Power BI, Resource Manager, Graph, telemetry, and price requests (`Invoke-WebRequest`, `Invoke-RestMethod`) | the module's request helpers, `Test-DemoFabricApp`, `Invoke-DemoRetailPriceRequest` | Already: `-TimeoutSec` (60 to 120 seconds), which on PowerShell 7.4 ends at the answer's headers; **now** `-OperationTimeoutSeconds` bounds each read of the body too. The runbooks run Windows PowerShell 5.1, whose reads are bounded on their own, with `-TimeoutSec` 60 or 100 |
| The notebooks' `requests` calls | the control, deployment, and live-activity notebooks | Already: `timeout=` 60 or 180 seconds on every call |
| The busy marker's refresher | `Invoke-DemoBusyMarkerLoop` | **Now** stops renewing after 60 minutes with no step change, or after 6 hours, so a stuck run doesn't keep the demo awake overnight |

The tests in `DbHubDemo.OneCommand.Tests.ps1` fail on 2916abd: the restart asked with `--no-wait` and a bounded wait; a view from before the restart never counts as its end; a restart Azure doesn't finish gets one deallocate and start, named in the **Warning**; the guest shut down first when the host can run commands; a refused deallocate fails the step with the next step and no further wait; and the other calls' bounds. **Live:** stopping the upgrade that this held, then `deploy.ps1` again on `rg-dbhubmn-demo`, by self-update to this commit.

**The replica's line on a run that stopped early** (R858; live, 2026-11-16). The held upgrade ended **NOT DONE** on T2 at 16:06, after Azure finished the restart at 15:55 and the resent chunks stuck again, and `DEPLOY.T4.REPLICA.END` said the replica was deleted "once DONE's checks and the history snapshot had read it", though they hadn't run. Both deploy paths now pass whether DONE's checks ran (`-ChecksRan`), and the line says when they didn't; the deletion is the same, decided earlier for every run, a **NOT DONE** one included.

**The unit tests and the real Azure CLI** (R859; tests only, the coordinator's decision). A watcher of the Azure CLI's own command logs during the window showed 206 calls from the unit tests for the made-up subscription `11111111-...`. A hunt that ran each test file in its own process, with a stand-in `az` first on `PATH`, found 412 calls in five files: `DbHubDemo.Lifecycle.Tests.ps1` 372 (the session control's setup inside deploy runs: policy assignments, the Automation provider, and the control's resource group), `DbHubDemo.FirstRun.Tests.ps1` 16, `DbHubDemo.Cost.Tests.ps1` 10, and `DbHubDemo.T4Fallback.Tests.ps1` 10 (the safety stop's and the control's schedules), and `DbHubDemo.T4Replica.Tests.ps1` 4 (`az tag update` on the resource group, a write). Each of those files now has a default mock of `Invoke-DemoAzCli` that gives what the real CLI answered for that subscription, which the tests relied on, so their behavior is unchanged; the hunt found no call in the other 82 files, and none in these five after the change. The guard is test-wide: `tests/Invoke-StaticValidation.ps1` turns `tests/TestAzGuard.ps1` on around Pester (the stand-in `az` records each call and ends with exit code 97, and `AZURE_CONFIG_DIR` is an empty folder), and any call it lists is `STATIC.PESTER.AZURECLI` **Fail**; `Repo.TestAzGuard.Tests.ps1` proves a call fails at once, is listed, and uses no sign-in. The same hunt timed each file: the Key Vault opt-in's destroy test spent 901 seconds in `Remove-DemoT4Replica`'s bounded wait, polling a made-up replica in real time, until its 15-minute limit; it now mocks that deletion, which has its own tests, and its file takes 9 seconds instead of 910.

**Chunk names Azure keeps marked for deletion** (R860; live on 2026-11-16, the coordinator's decision: fix it now, reusing the named Run Commands' fresh-name rule). The upgrade test's rerun at 16:26 found 17 chunk Run Commands on `archost01` that Azure had kept in Deleting since 10:21 (each run's cleanup asked again; Azure ended the deletes with an internal error). One was `DbHubDemo-Chunk-cb840b69ea86-001`, the rerun's own bundle chunk, and its `PUT` was refused: "Operation 'PUT Extension' is not allowed on VM extension '...' since it is marked for deletion. You can only retry the Delete operation (or wait for an ongoing one to complete)". `$putChunk` threw, and the Artifacts step sends any such failure to the watchdog, which restarted the VM at 16:30, a restart Azure didn't finish (R857). `main` has the same `$putChunk`, with no fresh-name rule at all.

- **The fix:** `Test-DemoRunCommandHeldError` recognizes the refusal, before the conflict backoff (Azure's answer can read `Conflict`, and a retry doesn't free the name), and the chunk runs at once under `Resolve-DemoRunCommandFreshName -ForChunk`'s fresh name, `<name>-yyyyMMddHHmmss`, once per chunk. `-ForChunk` leaves the set's other chunks alone, since one can have finished without being read back yet, and words the console line and `DEPLOY.RUNCOMMAND.STUCK_<VM>` with what Azure answered, since nothing was waited for; the named path's text is unchanged.
- **What stays:** the chunk's script, so the VM writes the same `chunk-<nnn>.bin`, which the loader reassembles by index; and the cleanups, since a fresh name still matches `DbHubDemo-Chunk-*`.
- **Room first** (the coordinator's addition, from the host at 17:25: 23 of Azure's 25, that is 9 finished chunks of an earlier send, 8 held ones, 5 named ones, and `DbHubDemo-Profile`): `Get-DemoChunkRunCommandName` also returns the VM's total, and when that total plus the set's chunks would pass the fresh-name limit of 24, `Send-DemoChunkSet` waits for the deletes its cleanup just asked for, 5 minutes at most (`-RoomWaitSeconds`), before the first chunk; a VM with room lists once, as before. With still no room, a chunk that needs a fresh name stops with Azure's limit of 25 named and goes to the watchdog, as before; a deallocate and start cleared such a host on 2026-11-14.
- **Tests:** five in `DbHubDemo.Bundle.Tests.ps1` fail on 435676d with the live error: a held chunk runs under a fresh name with the same script and is cleaned up; with four at once, the other chunks are still read back (a mutation without `-ForChunk` fails it); Azure's `Conflict` wording gets no backoff; a crowded VM's leftovers are waited for, so a held chunk finds room (a mutation without the wait fails it); and a VM still at the limit stops with it named. **Live:** the upgrade test's next run, in the next capacity window.

**Tokens held across a long step** (R861; live on 2026-11-16, a new user's first deploy, the coordinator's decision: fix the class in one place). `configure-powerbi.ps1` got its Fabric and Power BI tokens at 20:10Z; the Direct Lake refresh retried for 8 minutes, and the report import at 20:19Z got HTTP 401 `TokenExpired`, so `Fabric.Report` failed and the first deploy would end **NOT DONE**. The Azure CLI hands back its cached token until about 5 minutes before it expires, so a token can come with only that left. `main` gets the tokens the same way, and its request helpers don't renew one.

- **The fix:** `Get-DemoFabricToken` and `Get-DemoPowerBIToken` record each token's source, keyed by the SecureString, never its value (`Register-DemoIssuedToken`). `Invoke-DemoFabricRequest` and `Invoke-DemoPowerBIRequest` send the newest token of its line (`Get-DemoCurrentToken`), renewed first when it expires within 4 minutes, under the Azure CLI's own point so the renewal brings a new token, and renew a refused one once, then send the request again. A token is refused by HTTP 401, or, as Power BI answers it, HTTP 403 with `X-PowerBI-Error-Info` `TokenExpired` or `InvalidToken` and no body (`Test-DemoTokenRefused`); a permission 403 isn't one.
- **Efficiency:** each renewal is recorded for the whole line, so callers that still hold an older token send the newest without asking the Azure CLI; a renewal that brings back the same token isn't sent, or asked again for a minute; a caller's own token is left as it is. No call signature changed.
- **Tests:** six in `DbHubDemo.Fabric.Tests.ps1`, Fabric and Power BI each, fail on 1a41191. **Live** (no capacity needed): an invalid token recorded as issued, then one read-only GET to each service: Fabric 401 and Power BI 403 (`InvalidToken`) each got one renewal, then HTTP 200, and a second GET with the old token sent the renewed one with no second renewal.

**One call that got no answer** (R862; live on 2026-11-16, the coordinator's decision: a single call must never hang a run). On the fresh first deploy, T1's track sent its chunks; at 15:13:05 an `az rest` GET of chunk 8's instance view opened a connection to Resource Manager and got no answer, and at 17:52 it was still open: T1.Artifacts had been running for 2 hours 43 minutes, the chunk's 900-second limit, which is checked between reads, never ran, and the run's busy marker kept renewing, which deferred the nightly stop and moved both VMs' auto-shutdown from 19:00 to 20:00. `Invoke-DemoAzCli` had no default limit, and `az rest` has none of its own; `main` is the same.

- **The fix, the whole class** (the audit table above): `az rest` gets 300 seconds unless its caller sets a limit, through the timed process path that token requests already used, which stops the CLI's process tree; the module's web requests bound each read of an answer (`-OperationTimeoutSeconds`), since PowerShell 7.4's `-TimeoutSec` ends at the headers; and the busy marker's refresher stops renewing when no step's state, status, or message has changed for 60 minutes, its own Nightly stop row aside, or after 6 hours (`Test-DemoBusyRunStalled`, `Get-DemoProgressFingerprint`), and says so on the console and that row. The real runs took at most about 3 hours, and a step that waits says so every few minutes. The notebooks' `requests` calls already had `timeout=`.
- **Tests:** in `DbHubDemo.Guard.Tests.ps1` (the `az rest` default; a caller's limit kept), `DbHubDemo.SafetyStop.Tests.ps1` (the stall and run-time rules, the fingerprint, and the refresher stopping), and two static tests in `Repo.Conventions.Tests.ps1` (every web call in the scripts and the runbooks has its limits; every notebook request passes a timeout). They fail on 8954717, except the notebook guard, which keeps what's already true. **Live:** the fresh deploy was stopped at 17:53 and its environment stopped with `stop-demo.ps1`; its rerun in the next window runs on this fix.

**Run all's history on a small capacity** (R863; live on 2026-11-16, the new user's first Run all on the F4, session 1ce548a4; the coordinator's decision: queued, start the job, say so, and end the session; refused, keep it for the next Run all; never wait while holding the session). At the session's end, the reference run of `NB_DatabaseHub_LiveActivity` started at 22:34:41Z and stopped at 22:35:13Z. The driver log shows where: after "15 / 29 cells completed", the 16th cell, section 6's Locks and blocking, the notebook's first chart, ran its queries; Fabric ran its secret redaction on the cell's result (`SecretRedactionUtils`) and then failed to parse it: "Unrecognized token 'REDACTED' ... column: 299381", about the size of a chart's image. The Estate pulse table before it passed. The likely cause: the control notebook had read the session's two vault secrets, which hold `{}` until a first session ends (`deploy.ps1` creates them so), and Fabric's secret redaction replaces "the secret values that are displayed in cell output with [REDACTED]" ([secret redaction](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/data-engineering/author-execute-notebook#secret-redaction)), so an empty JSON object in a chart's result became a bare token. The fallback job, `fbce4100`, was queued (NotStarted), although Learn says queueing doesn't apply to jobs submitted through the public API ([job queueing](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/data-engineering/job-queueing-for-fabric-spark)); `save_history` waited 30 minutes for it while holding the F4's one Spark session, and it started 5.5 minutes after that session ended, at 18:11, and saved the history in 2 minutes. `main` has no Run all.

- **The fix, both halves:** in a reference run (`isReferenceRun`, [NotebookUtils runtime](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/data-engineering/notebookutils/notebookutils-runtime)), the activity notebook prints one line for each table (its rows and columns) and each chart (its panels): no display output, no chart, no table value, no NaN or infinity, and nothing taken from a secret; a job or a run by hand shows them as before. `POSTGRES_METRICS` uses JSON's default separators, so its text is never the runbook's compact text of the same secret. Run all reads the fallback job once (`history_job_state`) and never waits: Completed is a **Pass**, Failed or Cancelled a **Warning** with the fix, and queued says that Fabric starts it once this notebook's Spark session ends and where its result shows (the Monitor hub, then the report and the Insights app). Its last step, `end_session_for_history`, ends an interactive Run all's Spark session (`notebookutils.session.stop()`; "Code after session.stop() doesn't execute", [session management](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/data-engineering/notebookutils/notebookutils-session-management)) only after a session's end here, while a history job it started still reads NotStarted; a scheduled or pipeline run's session ends by itself (`isForInteractive`). A refused job (HTTP 430: a full capacity, a Trial, a throttled capacity, or a full queue, 4 jobs on F2 and F4) stays a **Warning**, and the next Run all saves the history first, as before.
- **Tests:** `Fabric.ControlNotebook.Tests.ps1` simulates the live case (the reference run fails with the live error, the job stays NotStarted): one job read, the queued line, the session ended as the run's last action, and `POSTGRES_METRICS` the same document as the vault's but not its text; a scheduled run and a finished job leave the session alone; the end step is the last statement. `Fabric.Notebooks.Tests.ps1` runs `display_frame` and `plot_panels` as a reference run with NaN, infinity, and a secret-like value in the table: one line each, none of the values. Four of them fail on 1bae3f1; the finished-job case keeps what's already true. **Live:** the next window, through Run all's real first-session path: rg-dbhubfd-demo's first session after its rerun's **DONE**, whose two secrets are still `{}` as a new user's are, with the history saved in the session (`SAVE_RESULTS` true, so the save cell's Delta writes run in the reference run too), in the same short session as R864's proof.
- **Live, 2026-11-17 (passed):** rg-dbhubfd-demo's first session, 3293c7ae: Run all as a RunNotebook job with its defaults and a 30-minute session, with both session secrets still `{}`, as a new user's are, and `SAVE_RESULTS` true. After the session's stop (02:38) and the wait for the last telemetry (until 02:47), the notebook printed "NB_DatabaseHub_LiveActivity runs in this notebook's Spark session to save session 3293c7ae's history." and "Pass: the history is saved; the report and the Insights app show it after their next refresh." The reference run's own Delta writes saved 1,546 rows to `telemetry_snapshots`, 17 to `analysis_findings`, and 12 to `scenario_runs`, with T4's and its replica's metrics (8 series, 211 points; Read replica lag peaked at 8.0 s). No job fell back, and the Spark session ended with the run, at 02:48:31, 50 minutes after the job's start. One printed line read `"backfilled": [REDACTED]`: Fabric's redaction still masks an empty JSON object once the notebook has read a secret that holds `{}`, which confirms the cause above, and a reference run's printed lines carry it harmlessly.

**A host that stops during a session** (R864; live on 2026-11-16, the same session; the coordinator's decision: surface it as soon as the runbook knows it, with Azure Resource Manager reads only, no new Spark time, and no new polling loop; then the guard against a newer status). archost01's start ended `VMStartTimedOut` at 16:41:48, 53 minutes into the session, and the T2 profile's Run Command failed at 16:41:50. archost01's power state had said running, so T2's activity had gone out and the session's status said so, until its end: the session's job had ended, and `DbHub-Monitor` looked only at T1's plugin. `main` has no session; a run, which has no status for a notebook to follow, is unchanged.

- **The fix:** the session's start checks its hosts before its last write (`Get-DbHubSessionHealth`): each VM its activity went out to, one instance-view read, and each dispatch Run Command, one read with its instance view. A VM that's deallocated or stopped, a provisioning failure since the session's start (an older one isn't blamed on it), or a Run Command that ended Failed, TimedOut, or Canceled is a **Warning** step, `Host`, with the fix, in words that stay the same while the problem does, so it's added once. The status records the dispatch Run Commands (`runCommands`). `DbHub-Monitor`'s 30-minute re-checks make the same reads while the session runs. The identity can't read the vault's value through Azure Resource Manager, so the runbooks keep a copy of each status they write in the control account's variable `DbHubSessionStatus` (`infra/control/control.bicep`; the sandbox's internal `Set-AutomationVariable` and `Get-AutomationVariable`, no role), and the monitor writes the vault and the copy only for a new problem, and only while the copy is still the one it read (`updatedUtc`), of a session that still runs. A missing variable, or a sandbox without the cmdlets, is skipped with one log line. Run all's live view reads the session's status every 5 minutes in its existing loop and prints each new step: the same vault read and identity as before.
- **Tests:** in `Automation.Runbooks.Tests.ps1`, the session's start with a host whose start failed (the live `VMStartTimedOut`), with a failed dispatch Run Command, and with a failure from before the session (not blamed); the monitor adding a host that stopped once, keeping every step, and starting or stopping nothing; the guard, with the session's end or another job's write between its read and its write; a missing variable and a sandbox without the cmdlets; and a status without `runCommands`. In `Fabric.ControlNotebook.Tests.ps1`, the live view printing the monitor's Warning with its fix, at most one status read per 5 minutes (a 90-minute session: at most 19 more reads than before); the live view from 76cdb12 beside the new runbooks, which runs as before and doesn't show it; and a status from runbooks before, which shows nothing new. Eight of them fail on 76cdb12; the other two keep what's already true. **Live:** the next window's short session on rg-dbhubfd-demo, with archost01 deallocated mid-session and `DbHub-Monitor` started on demand.
- **Live, 2026-11-17 (passed):** the same session, 3293c7ae. Once its phase read running (02:11:17), sqlvm01 was deallocated (02:12:24, a healthy host, so the Warning comes at once), and `DbHub-Monitor`, started on demand, ended a minute later with `"session":"Warned"`: "The session's status now says: T1, T3, and T4: sqlvm01 is deallocated, so T1, T3, and T4 has no activity now." The variable `DbHubSessionStatus` held the Host step with its fix, and Run all's live view printed both at its next status read, 3 to 4 minutes later, then again in the session's end summary; the other targets went on. The verb now agrees ("have" for a host that drives several targets: a test in `Automation.Runbooks.Tests.ps1` fails on 1d2e3ce).
- **What it doesn't see in a short session:** the same session's T2 host had the dead VM agent (below). The runbook's start left archost01 running with no agent, T2's Run Command never ran, and the status said "Activity: T2: showcase for 30 minutes" to the end, while the live view showed T2's CPU at 0 to 3% and the history recorded T2's CPU and memory beats as not observed. The check saw it only once Azure ended the start (`VMStartTimedOut`, about 58 minutes) or the Run Command (about 46 minutes).
- **R870, the agent (2026-11-17):** `Get-DbHubSessionHealth` now reads the agent's status from the same instance view: a VM that runs with its agent not **Ready** 15 minutes or more after the earliest dispatch of its targets (`dispatchUtc`) is a `Host` **Warning**, "T2: archost01's VM agent wasn't Ready 15 minutes after T2's activity went out, so the Run Command that sets it can't run, and T2 may have no activity this session", with the fix and the troubleshooting entry. No new read; the words don't change while the problem lasts, so it's added once; the agent's own text goes to the job's log. The session's own check comes right after the dispatch, inside the 15 minutes, so the re-checks find it: 30 minutes into a session of 40 minutes or more. Tests in `Automation.Runbooks.Tests.ps1`: the live case through `DbHub-Monitor` (no Warning at the session's start, one at the re-check, none added at the next) fails on 2e3bc9b; an agent that's **Ready**, and a status without a dispatch time, are never blamed.

**A stop that left a failed VM running** (R868; live on 2026-11-16, the new user's environment at 23:46, after its T2 host's start had ended `VMStartTimedOut` at 22:49). `stop-demo.ps1` read archost01's power state as empty and waited: "archost01 reports no power state yet; waiting", every 22 seconds for 900 seconds. Then it returned `STOP.VM_ARCHOST01` **Warning** "archost01 reported no power state for 900 seconds", with the fix "Check the VM in the portal; run the script again", sent no deallocate, and ended with exit 0. The VM's console showed Windows at its lock screen: it ran and billed, the profile line said it "isn't running", and only the next evening's auto-shutdown would have stopped it. A deallocate by hand was accepted at once (00:04:54, deallocated at 00:07:06). The same happened on the upgrade test environment on 2026-11-13. `main` has the same wait. The nightly safety stop isn't affected: its runbook sends the deallocate whatever the power state.

- **The fix:** in `Invoke-DemoVmPowerAction`, a deallocate of a VM that shows no power state reads the instance view's status codes once (`Get-DemoVmStatusCode`; `Test-DemoVmOperationInProgress` now uses it too). A provisioning state that's failed means the power state won't appear by itself, so the deallocate goes out at once, and the result says why ("Its last operation had failed (ProvisioningState/failed/VMStartTimedOut), so it showed no power state before"). One that's Updating is waited for, as before, so a VM is never deallocated in the middle of an operation. `stop-demo.ps1`'s profile step says such a VM "shows no power state (its last operation failed, or one is still running)" instead of "isn't running".
- **Tests:** in `DbHubDemo.Lifecycle.Tests.ps1`, the live case, with a power state that stays empty until a deallocate goes out, is deallocated after one read and passes (fails on 61ad5e0, which waits the whole bound and reports a **Warning**); a VM that shows no power state while Azure works on it is still waited for, and deallocated once it settles, which keeps what's already true.

**A refused sign-in, read as a missing group** (R867; live on 2026-11-16, the new user's rerun at 23:18). Preflight stopped at `PREFLIGHT.P6.GROUP`: "The T3 admin group ... could not be read from Microsoft Graph (HTTP 401 ... InvalidAuthenticationToken ...)", with the fix "Create an Entra security group you own in the demo tenant and set t3AdminGroupObjectId (prerequisite P6)." One read-only Graph call confirmed the cause: "Continuous access evaluation resulted in challenge with result: InteractionRequired and code: TokenCreatedWithOutdatedPolicies"; the tenant's sign-in policies had changed, and one fresh token from the Azure CLI was refused too (`PREFLIGHT.GUARD.CONTEXT`'s **Warning** had said so in every run since about 22:30). The group existed; following the fix would have changed a working configuration. `main` gives every non-404 failure the same fix.

- **The fix:** a 404 keeps that fix. A 401, or an answer after a claims challenge (`Invoke-DemoRestRequest`'s `Challenge`), says Graph refused the Azure CLI's sign-in and asks for a new one, with the fix "Sign in again yourself: az login (az login --use-device-code in a codespace), for the demo's tenant. Then run the script again; nothing in the configuration changes." Any other error asks the user to check that the group can be read, and to create one only if it doesn't exist. It stays a **Fail**: the template records the group's name as T3's administrator login, and without it a redeploy would put the template's placeholder there. Troubleshooting's claims-challenge row said "Nothing stops"; it now names this exception.
- **Tests:** in `DbHubDemo.Preflight.Tests.ps1`, the live 401 with its challenge asks for a new sign-in and never for a new group (fails on a7f6771); the 404 test also checks its fix.

**A start in progress, and a VM left deallocating** (R866; live on 2026-11-16, mn's upgrade and its retry; the coordinator's decision: fix both, with tests). The retry asked Azure to start the deallocated archost01 at 21:59:43 (`Request-DemoStoppedStart`), and 19 seconds later `Invoke-DemoVmPowerAction` sent a second start: the VM read stopped, with its provisioning state Updating, while Azure worked on the first, and it read that way for 12 minutes. Every start in the activity log since Phase 28 shows twice (13:24 and 13:25, 20:12 and 20:13, 21:59 and 22:00). And at 21:28 the run's NOT DONE said "Running and billing, because this run started or created them: sqlvm01, archost01, and T4", although the watchdog's recovery had asked Azure to deallocate archost01 at 21:03, which then read deallocating and deallocated at 21:25.

- **The fix:** with `-StartRequested`, a VM that reads stopped or deallocated while its instance view says Updating (`Test-DemoVmOperationInProgress`, one read) gets no second start: the wait polls the power state as before, and sends one start only if Azure's start ends without the VM running. `Invoke-DemoVmRestartRecovery` returns where it left the VM (`Left`: deallocating, deallocated, starting, or running), `Restart-DemoVmOnce` passes it on, and `DEPLOY.WATCHDOG_<VM>`'s evidence keeps it as `left`. The ending, which makes no Azure call, reads it (`Get-DemoWatchdogLeftVm`): a VM left deallocating or deallocated leaves the billing line, and the line names it apart ("archost01 is deallocating: the watchdog asked Azure to deallocate it, Azure finishes that on its own, and a deallocated VM doesn't bill for compute").
- **Tests:** in `DbHubDemo.Lifecycle.Tests.ps1`, the live case (the start in progress is waited for, no second start) fails on e45d087; a start Azure ends without the VM running still gets exactly one start, which keeps what's already true. In `DbHubDemo.OneCommand.Tests.ps1`, the live NOT DONE names archost01 apart (fails on e45d087), and a later watchdog result that left the VM running takes it back.

**A managed private endpoint that Fabric failed to provision** (R865; live on 2026-11-16, the new user's rerun on fddbd8d, which ended **DONE**). The control's Fabric part created the workspace "DBHub MR Fresh Control" and its managed private endpoint to the vault at 22:10, with the capacity Active. At 22:10:06 the vault's activity log shows Fabric's write of the connection (`privateEndpointConnectionProxies/write`, Fabric's service principal) ending BadRequest: "remotePrivateEndpoint.connectionDetails[0].linkIdentifier cannot be null." The endpoint read `provisioningState` Failed, with no connection state, and the vault had no connection at all. The step waited its 10 minutes, and **DONE** said "1 item(s) need attention: ... isn't approved yet (Fabric creates it in a few minutes). Run ./scripts/deploy.ps1 again in a few minutes, or approve the pending connection". Neither could work: a rerun found the endpoint by name, created nothing, and waited again, and there was no connection to approve. Run all needs the endpoint to read the session's secrets. The new user's endpoint from the afternoon was Succeeded and Approved with the same code, so the failure is Fabric's, and transient. `main`'s `setup-activity-control.ps1` finds the endpoint by name the same way.

- **The fix:** `New-DemoActivityControlEndpoint` deletes a Failed endpoint ([Managed Private Endpoints - Delete](https://learn.microsoft.com/rest/api/fabric/core/managed-private-endpoints/delete-workspace-managed-private-endpoint), HTTP 200, the workspace's Admin role, which its creator has), waits until Fabric no longer lists it, 5 minutes at most, and creates it again. `Set-DemoActivityControlFabric` does that for an endpoint that reads Failed before the wait, and, since the vault gets the connection only once Fabric has provisioned the endpoint, reads the endpoint again in each of the wait's 30-second rounds and replaces one that fails then, with a new 10-minute wait. A run replaces an endpoint once, so it never loops; a second failure ends the wait at once and says so ("Fabric failed to provision the managed private endpoint ..."), with the next run, which replaces it again, as the fix, and no pending connection to approve. The states are [documented](https://learn.microsoft.com/rest/api/fabric/core/managed-private-endpoints/get-workspace-managed-private-endpoint): Provisioning, Succeeded, Updating, Deleting, and Failed.
- **Tests:** two in `DbHubDemo.ActivityControl.Tests.ps1` fail on fddbd8d: a Failed endpoint is deleted, created again, and its new connection approved (one delete, one create, a **Pass** that says so); and one that Fabric fails again is replaced only once, with the message and fix above, while the notebook is still imported. **Live:** the new user's environment keeps the failed endpoint, so its next `deploy.ps1` run, on this fix, is the proof.
- **Live, 2026-11-17, and R869:** the new user's `setup-activity-control.ps1` on e45d087 (01:14, capacity Active) found the endpoint Failed, deleted it (HTTP 200; Fabric's cleanup on the vault at 06:17:00 UTC), and stopped listing it within seconds; its creation then got "HTTP 500 InternalServerError An error occured", and the step ended **Manual action required** with that error and the documented fix. The vault's activity log shows no write after the cleanup, so the creation never reached it. The fix's next run (01:20, the same code) found no endpoint, created it, and approved its connection: `CONTROL.FABRIC.ENDPOINT` **Pass**. So the delete and the plain creation work live; a creation sent seconds after the delete can fail. R869: `New-DemoActivityControlEndpoint` reads the list back after a 5xx and, if the endpoint isn't there, creates it again, at most twice, after 60 and 120 seconds; a 4xx still ends at once. The POST isn't idempotent, so the list comes first. Three tests in `DbHubDemo.ActivityControl.Tests.ps1` fail on 83a52aa: a 500 and then a success is one **Pass** with two creations; a 500 after which Fabric lists the endpoint makes no second creation; and a 5xx every time stops after three tries and says so.

**The T2 host's dead VM agent** (R871, fixed 2026-11-17). On four of the five test environments, a start of archost01 ended `VMStartTimedOut` after 48 to 88 minutes with its VM agent Not Ready: mn's since `main`'s own build on 2026-11-16 at 10:14, up's on 2026-11-13, nu's at its session's start (15:49), and the new user's at its first start after a stop (20:12, found after its **DONE**, whose T2 checks don't need the host's agent). No sqlvm01 did.

- **The agent's logs** (read from a copy of fd's OS disk, attached as a data disk to another VM and deleted afterwards): Windows ran and was idle, and the agent asked Azure's WireServer for its goal state 1,762 times over 3.7 hours, each answered HTTP 410 "Goal State not yet available", and logged "escalate to ICM - 'OneFleet Node/AzureHost-Agent'". The start stalls on Azure's side.
- **The cause: chunk Run Commands left on the host.** With 8 of them at once (up to 711 KB of inline script each), Azure ended their deletes on the T2 host with `InternalExecutionError`. Each one then stays listed as Succeeded but marked for deletion: Azure refuses a new PUT of its name ("Operation 'PUT Extension' is not allowed ... marked for deletion. You can only retry the Delete"), and any delete while the VM is deallocated ("Cannot modify extensions in the VM when the VM is not running"). sqlvm01 got the same chunks in the same minute; its deletes finished, and it keeps none.
- **The record:** every start of a T2 host from 2026-10-21 to 2026-11-11 worked (30 of 30, the user's own environment included), with the same transfer. From 2026-11-13, every start or restart of a host that listed chunks failed (13 of 13 in the activity logs, then up's at 03:42 and 05:12 today, as predicted), and ha's start without them took 2 minutes. So Azure most likely changed around 2026-11-12, and a demo deployed from `main` since then has the same exposure. One thing stays unexplained: the record counts 8 chunks at up's four 1-minute starts from 2026-11-14 to 16, and it can't tell whether Azure had removed them by then.
- **What brings a host back** (experiments on our own hosts, 2026-11-17): deletes sent while a dead start runs are accepted and stay pending, then end Failed with the start (up: sent at 03:48, Failed at 05:09 with `VMStartTimedOut`, and a deallocate after that left all 9). A deallocate sent a minute after the deletes completes them: nu's 9 were gone after it, and its next start had the agent Ready in 1.7 minutes.
- **The fix** ([troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md#a-hosts-vm-agent-that-isnt-ready), [ADR 0018](adr/0018-fast-redeploy-parallel-tracks-golden-snapshot.md)):
  - fcc2543: `Send-DemoChunkSet -DeleteWaitSeconds`, 300 by default on the T2 host and 0 elsewhere. The host's chunks go one at a time, and each one's delete is confirmed (`NotFound`) before the next. A delete Azure hasn't finished in 5 minutes is sent once more; after a second, the send stops, and the track's watchdog takes over, then sends one chunk at a time again.
  - 2ac5c9c: the watchdog (`Restart-DemoVmOnce`) doesn't restart a T2 host whose agent isn't Ready or that lists chunks. Their deletes go, then, 60 seconds later, one deallocate and start (`Invoke-DemoVmRestartRecovery`). `DEPLOY.WATCHDOG_ARCHOST01` says "deallocated and started", and its **Fail**'s fix is to run `deploy.ps1` again, never to wait 30 minutes.
  - 170d1ba: the recovery's own deallocate gets no second one (`Invoke-DemoVmPowerAction -DeallocateRequested`, as R866 did for a start), and the **Warning**'s wording fits this cause.
  - be698c0: `stop-demo.ps1` sends a running VM's chunk deletes right before its deallocate.
  - 0523d36: chunks an earlier run left on the host, which Azure still hasn't deleted once the artifacts have arrived and are recorded, go to the watchdog's host path at once: their deletes, then one deallocate and start. A host that mustn't be restarted then keeps them, with a `DEPLOY.ARTIFACTS.CLEANUP_ARCHOST01` **Warning** whose fix is `stop-demo.ps1`. sqlvm01's stay a **Warning**, as before.
  - 8d26496: nothing is sent to a running VM whose agent isn't Ready (`Get-DemoVmExtensionActivity` counts it as Azure's work in progress, so the settle step waits, and after 20 minutes the watchdog steps in). mn showed why, below.
- **Tests:** each new case fails on the commit before it: in `DbHubDemo.Bundle.Tests.ps1`, the host's confirmed one-at-a-time send and a delete Azure never finishes; in `DbHubDemo.OneCommand.Tests.ps1`, the three host cases, the **Fail**'s fix, the agent that isn't Ready, and a dead host's settle reaching the watchdog; in `DbHubDemo.Lifecycle.Tests.ps1`, the stop's deletes before each deallocate and the requested deallocate; and in `DbHubDemo.Tracks.Tests.ps1`, the leftovers cleared once the artifacts arrive. `DbHubDemo.Tracks.Tests.ps1` also pins the track's path for a stuck delete: the watchdog, then one chunk at a time, in the same run.
- **Live (2026-11-17, our own hosts; the capacity wasn't needed):**
  - ha (healthy): `Send-DemoChunkSet` with the bundle's and runner's 9 chunks (4.2 MB) took 8.3 minutes, every delete confirmed at its first try, and left no chunk; a deallocate and a start then had the agent Ready in 1.7 minutes. The same host size took 7.2 to 7.4 minutes 8 at once in three earlier deploys, so one at a time costs about a minute.
  - up and fd (dead, 9 chunks each): `Invoke-DemoVmWatchdog` sent the 9 deletes, deallocated and started the host once, with no restart, and found the agent Ready, with no chunk left, in 9.2 and 9.4 minutes (`DEPLOY.WATCHDOG_ARCHOST01` **Warning**; the deletes ended Succeeded at the deallocation). up's run showed the double deallocate and the wording that 170d1ba fixed.
  - mn (dead, 16 chunks): the watchdog ended in its **Fail** after 23 minutes, with "run deploy.ps1 again" as the fix. Its chunks had been sent by the earlier code while the host's agent wasn't Ready (2026-11-17 03:25 UTC, during a dead start): 8 fresh-named ones stuck in Creating, and 8 older ones in Deleting since 2026-11-16. A deallocate canceled their deletes instead of completing them, twice (05:44 and, after one more round of deletes, 06:05). That's why nothing is sent to a host whose agent isn't Ready now. mn needs the T2 rebuild the coordinator planned; it's deallocated.
- **What an existing user sees:** a demo deployed since about 2026-11-13, from `main` or this branch, may list chunks on its T2 host, and the host's next start after a stop fails. Its upgrade, `./scripts/deploy.ps1`, starts the host, the settle step finds the agent not Ready, and after 20 minutes the watchdog brings the host back as above, and the run goes on: that one run takes about 30 to 60 minutes longer. An upgrade that runs while the host is up but still lists chunks clears them once its artifacts have arrived, with one deallocate and start. `main` doesn't give a chunk a fresh name, so a host deployed from `main` has chunks marked for deletion, like up's and fd's, not stuck ones like mn's. The user's own environment lists no chunk today.
- **Not covered, and accepted (the coordinator, 2026-11-17):** the nightly safety stop and the session's end deallocate from Azure Automation without deletes; after this fix, no chunk stays on the host for them to keep.

**The T2 host's rebuild** (R872, 2026-11-17). The user's decision on mn's dead host: "Automatically: deploy.ps1 deletes and recreates only the T2 host, once, when its agent stays dead". No switch. It's the last resort, after R871's recovery.

- **The cue:** the watchdog's Fail for archost01 whose evidence says `agentDead`: its agent stayed down after the deallocate and start, or it was down when the watchdog stepped in and the deallocate and start didn't finish (8155431; mn's run at 01:11 UTC showed its deallocate during a hung start with no power state for 1,193 seconds). A host whose agent was Ready (a refused deallocate, for example) isn't rebuilt. The T2 step now checks the host's agent before its Run Commands too.
- **The rebuild** (`Invoke-DemoT2HostRebuild`, 001803d): it reads archost01's own nested template from `azuredeploy.json` and the values its last deployment recorded before it changes anything; clears what the state records for the old host; deletes the VM, then its disks and network interface, each bounded; creates it again as the deployment `archost01-rebuild`, with a new password only in a private file; moves its auto-shutdown out of a busy run's way; waits for its agent; and runs T2's steps again from Artifacts. Once per run: a second dead agent ends the run **NOT DONE**. The rest of the template isn't deployed mid-run, so T1, T3, T4, Fabric, and the golden snapshot aren't touched; Arc onboarding replaces the old `arcsql01` machine, as on a first deployment. The failed attempt's **Fail** results become **Warnings** that name the rebuild, and **DONE** has a note; the status page has a "Rebuild of archost01" row.
- **A rebuild that stopped:** a host the state records but Azure doesn't have is `DEPLOY.T2.HOSTMISSING`; its records are cleared and a resume starts from preflight, so the template creates it.
- **`status.ps1`** (86e2e7d): `STATUS.RUNCOMMANDS` names the T2 host's Run Commands that Azure is still deleting, first, with `./scripts/deploy.ps1` as the fix, and says when the busy marker shows a run in progress, whose own deletes show for a few minutes.
- **Tests:** 82 new or changed tests fail on 588c323 (`DbHubDemo.T2HostRebuild.Tests.ps1`, and in Tracks, OneCommand, and Progress), the cue's two on 86e2e7d, and `STATUS.RUNCOMMANDS`'s three on 001803d.
- **Live (2026-11-17), mn, `deploy.ps1` on 8155431, from its dead host with 16 Run Commands in Deleting: DONE in 156 minutes** (14:04 to 16:41 UTC).
  - The start left the host's agent Not Ready. After the 20-minute settle, the watchdog sent the 16 deletes and one deallocate at 14:47, which Azure hadn't finished 20 minutes later (no second deallocate).
  - At 15:09:08 the T2 track rebuilt the host: archost01, its OS disk, and its network interface were deleted in 1 minute 55 seconds, and the new host's agent was Ready at 15:13:21.
  - T2's steps then ran again on it: the artifacts in 12 minutes 26 seconds, the loader in 2, the guest from Arc Jumpstart's image in 32, and the sign-in cleanup, Arc onboarding (the old `arcsql01` machine deleted first, `CleanupStaleThenOnboard`), and monitoring in 16.5. T2 was done at 16:21:00, 72 minutes after the rebuild began, with `TELEMETRY.T2` and `HUB.ESTATE.T2` **Pass**. The T4 track had finished in an earlier run, so validation created the read replica DONE needs (594 seconds, lag 0 seconds), and the run deleted it at its end.
  - Two corrections from it: the host build's "minutes so far" counted from the old host's track start ("71 minutes so far" for a 20-minute-old host), now from the rebuild (a79d58e); and the rebuild's start said "about 90 minutes in all", now "about 70 minutes" for the Jumpstart image, as measured, and "longer than an hour" in the build modes.

**T1's T4 step during the replica's creation** (R873, 2026-11-17). fd's rerun on 588c323 ended **NOT DONE**: T4's track started the replica's creation at 13:16 UTC (519 seconds), and T1's T4 step, which a rerun reaches quickly, found T4 Updating at 13:22. `Enable-DemoT4Workload` read every state but Ready as a stopped server. Now T1's T4 step, before T4's restart and its setup, and `Enable-DemoT4Workload` wait while T4 is Updating, Starting, Restarting, or Provisioning ([the server's states](https://learn.microsoft.com/rest/api/postgresql/servers/get)), at most 20 minutes, counted in polls; still changing after that is **Manual action required** with "Azure is still working on it". A first deployment hides it, since T1's bootstraps outlast the creation. Four tests fail on 86e2e7d. Live proof: fd's rerun on 8155431 ended **DONE** in 35 minutes (14:04 to 14:39 UTC): at 14:22:54 T1's T4 step found T4 Updating ("its read replica's creation keeps it Updating for about 9 minutes, so T1 waits for it to be Ready, at most 20 minutes"), and `WORKLOAD.T4.ENABLE` passed once the replica was created (564 seconds); `METRICS.T4.REPLICA` read a lag of 7 seconds, and the run deleted the replica at its end in 105 seconds.

**Deleting everything** (R874, 2026-11-17). The coordinator's decision, from the user's standing preferences: one command deletes everything `deploy.ps1` created. `destroy.ps1` reads, before it asks, what else is this environment's (`Get-DemoDestroyExtraPlan`), lists what goes and what stays in its confirmation, and deletes each part only when it can tell (79a35ac):

- the session control, when its published runbooks' settings name this environment's resource group, as `setup-activity-control.ps1 -Remove` deletes it; the Automation account, whose runbooks prove whose it is, now goes last, so a rerun after an interruption can still tell;
- the demo's Fabric workspace, when every item in it is one the demo creates (the lakehouse and its SQL analytics endpoint, the notebooks, the dashboard, the model, the report, and the Insights app's two items), and the control's, when its control notebook's `RESOURCE_GROUP` is this environment's, with its managed private endpoint; a workspace with anyone else's item stays, named, and `-KeepFabric` keeps both;
- the T3 group, when init.ps1 created it for this environment: its description ends "Created by init.ps1." and it has this environment's name; a group you supplied stays;
- a custom role definition, once no role assignment holds it, so another environment's, the owner's among them, stay.

Each part reports its own `DESTROY.*` result, and one that fails is a **Warning** with its fix while the others go on; the Fabric capacity is never resumed for it. Sixteen tests in `DbHubDemo.Destroy.Tests.ps1` fail on 8155431.

- **Live (2026-11-17), on up and ha, whose groups `destroy.ps1` on 588c323 had deleted at 13:02 to 13:18 UTC (16 minutes each, 10.5 of them for the group's delete), leaving the rest:**
  - ha, on 79a35ac: exit 0 in 2 minutes 48 seconds. It deleted the workspace "DBHub HA NewUser Test" (9 items, all the demo's) and the group `dbhubha-demo-sql-admins`. ha had no control of its own (`DESTROY.CONTROL` **Pass**), and the owner's "DBHub Control" workspace, under the configured shared name, was left alone.
  - up, on 79a35ac: exit 0 in 5 minutes 16 seconds. It deleted the control's workspace with its managed private endpoint, the demo's workspace, the control's 6 role assignments, its roles "(dbhubup)", the identity, the vault (purged), and the Automation account, and the group `dbhubup-demo-sql-admins`. It kept `rg-dbhubup-control` as "holding 3 other resources": the deleted account's runbooks, still listed for a moment (R875). On 17aa4a1, a third run deleted the empty group in 3 minutes 17 seconds, with every other part a **Pass** that found nothing left.
  - Read before and after: the owner's roles ("DbHub Demo Activity Operator", 22 actions, and "DbHub Demo Safety Stop", 7), `rg-dbhub-demo`, `rg-dbhub-control`, the workspaces "Database Hub Demo" and "DBHub Control", and the other test environments' roles, groups, and workspaces were unchanged. "DbHub Demo Safety Stop" stayed, held by 3 assignments (`DESTROY.SAFETYSTOP.ROLE` **Not selected**).
  - Not proven live: Fabric's deletes on a paused capacity. The capacity was Active for fd's and mn's runs at the time; the code reports a paused one as a **Warning** whose fix is to resume it and run `destroy.ps1` again.

**What a deleted account leaves listed for a moment** (R875, 2026-11-17, 17aa4a1). Right after the control's Automation account was deleted, Azure Resource Manager still listed its three runbooks in `rg-dbhubup-control`, so `Remove-DemoActivityControlResource` counted three other resources and kept the group; a minute later it was empty. The leftovers are now read by name, and names equal to the account or under it (`<account>/...`) don't count, there and in `destroy.ps1`'s plan for a rerun. Two tests fail on 79a35ac.

**The opt-in capacity pause, after the Fabric deletes** (R876, 2026-11-17, c2c7349). With `fabric.manageCapacity` true, `destroy.ps1` pauses the capacity that `start-demo.ps1` recorded as resumed (Phase 26b). It did that first, so since 79a35ac the Fabric workspaces' deletes would meet a paused capacity and end in a **Warning** asking to resume it. Now the pause comes after the Fabric workspaces, the session control, and the group, and still before the resource group, whose `DbHubFabricCapacityResumed` tag holds the record. Found while documenting `destroy.ps1`; one test fails on 17aa4a1. The default, `fabric.manageCapacity` false, never calls the capacity.

**A workspace another environment might use** (R877, 2026-11-17). The coordinator's rule: `destroy.ps1` never deletes what another environment might use. R874 deleted a workspace whose items were all the demo's, but two environments can name the same workspace, and the owner's `rg-dbhub-demo`, on `main`'s code, records nothing.

- **The record:** at the end of its Fabric part, `Invoke-DemoControlDeployStep` takes the two workspace IDs from `CONTROL.FABRIC.NOTEBOOK`'s evidence, the demo's and the one the control notebook is in, and merges them into the demo group's tags (`DbHubFabricWorkspaceId`, `DbHubControlWorkspaceId`, through `Set-DemoDeploymentState`). It does that on every run whose Fabric track finished, in this run or an earlier one, so an upgrade records them; `-SkipFabric` records nothing.
- **The check, at deploy and at destroy:** `Get-DemoFabricWorkspaceClaim` runs one Resource Graph query with no subscription list, which Learn documents as every subscription the caller can read, for the configured subscription and for resource groups whose tags hold `deploymentId` or `DbHubDeployStage`. A demo group has both from the template and `deploy.ps1`; the golden group (`environment=golden`) and the control groups (`component=activity-control`) have neither, so they don't count. The answer is its own canary: without the configured subscription's row, it can't tell "nothing else" from "can't read", and it says so.
- **`deploy.ps1`:** `DEPLOY.FABRIC.SHARED` is **Pass** when the IDs are recorded and nobody else records them, and a **Warning** that names the other environment when one does, when the record fails, or when Resource Graph can't be read; never a **Fail**. A **Warning** shows on the status page's Control row too.
- **`destroy.ps1`:** `Get-DemoDestroyFabricPlan` keeps a workspace its own checks found to be this environment's when another environment records it (Claimed), when any demo environment has no record (Untagged), or when Resource Graph can't be read (Unreadable). The confirmation lists it with the reason, and `DESTROY.FABRIC.WORKSPACE` or `DESTROY.FABRIC.CONTROL` is a **Warning** with the fix: run `destroy.ps1` again after the other environment's next `deploy.ps1` or its destroy, or delete the workspace in Fabric once nothing uses it.

Either the host runs with its agent **Not Ready**, or its start ended `VMStartTimedOut` (about an hour after it began in R871's cases), which leaves it with no power state, so the start step leaves it alone. - **Why the start step doesn't rebuild:**
  - The agent can't be read before the VM runs, so at that step a slow start can't be told from a dead one, and a rebuild deletes a T2 build that takes about 70 minutes to make again.
