### The runner's profile file replace, and the replica's lag seen in Database Hub (2026-11-17)

**Why.** The user: "Did we verify the replica lag shows in the database hub and everything works appropriately?" A session on fd, at aba211f, ran the replica-lag scenario so the owner could look. The scenario's first send was refused (R882), and the coordinator approved its fix as a follow-up to #58, on its own branch off `main`.

**Work summary.**

- **The replica's lag in Database Hub (R824, closed):**
  - `./scripts/start-demo.ps1` (17:48 to 18:08 ET) created pgreplica01-54cci4: `START.T4.REPLICA` **Pass** in 549 s.
  - `./scripts/demo-control.ps1 -Target T4 -Scenario incident:replica-lag -Duration 15` ran from 18:11, and again from 18:27.
  - Azure Monitor's `physical_replication_delay_in_seconds` climbed to 213, 214, 216, and 218 s in the full cycles, and dropped between them.
  - The owner saw the lag climbing in Database Hub (**Performance**, then **PostgreSQL**) at about 18:35 ET, with a screenshot.
  - `./scripts/stop-demo.ps1` (18:38 to 18:44) then deleted the replica, deallocated both VMs, and stopped T4. The capacity stayed paused throughout.
- **The refusal (R882):** the first send ended `CONTROL.T4` **Fail**: "runner profile set --target T4 failed with exit code 1: ... Access to the path is denied". The same command passed a minute later.
  - **The cause:** `FileProfileStore.SetAsync` writes the new profile to a temporary file, then moves it over the old one. On Windows, that move is refused with `UnauthorizedAccessException` while any other handle has the old file open, whatever its share mode (reproduced with Read, ReadWrite, and Read plus Delete).
  - **Why then:** the profile host reads the file every 10 seconds, without the lock. At the refusal, it was in T4's business-day connection-surge incident, so its read probably took longer.
  - **Read-only on sqlvm01** (one managed Run Command, deleted afterward): the file isn't read-only, SYSTEM and Administrators have FullControl, and the host was the only process that had it open. No log on the VM records the refusal.
- **The fix:**
  - `FileReplace` tries the move again after 50, 100, 200, 400, 800, and 1,600 ms (about 3 seconds), only while the file is in use: access denied, or a sharing or lock violation.
  - `FileProfileStore.SetAsync` uses it under its lock. So does `HostLanesFile.Write`, the host's heartbeat, which `status` reads.
  - The heartbeat reader's comment said that sharing for delete lets the host replace the file; it now says that holds on Linux and macOS only.
- **demo-control's message:** demo-control sends runner commands without `--json`, so they write no records, and its **Pass** read "(0 check(s) passed)". `Get-DemoVmRunnerOutcome` now gives the count only when there are records.
- **Also:** in this report, the README optimization paragraph and the next one had no blank line between them, so they rendered as one.
- **The docs:** the limitations, the Database Hub visuals page, and ADR 0025 no longer call the replica's own row an inference, or its lag chart not proven live; the showcase's climb and the replica's size fallback stay not proven live.

**Changed files.**

- `workload-generator/src/ContosoCare.Workload/Profiles/FileReplace.cs` (new), `ProfileHost.cs`, and `HostLanes.cs`;
- `workload-generator/tests/ContosoCare.Workload.Tests/ProfileStoreTests.cs` and `HostLaneStatusTests.cs`;
- `vm/bootstrap/lib/Workload.ps1` and `tests/unit/Vm.Workload.Tests.ps1`;
- `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/limitations.md`, `docs/database-hub-visuals.md`, `docs/adr/0025-t4-read-replica.md`, and this report.

### The T2 host that Azure keeps with no power state (#63, 2026-11-18)

**Why.** The user: "Continue the clean up and ensure users are safe to pull all the new DR and bug fixes." An existing user's update, checked live on vu (deployed with 3881ea1's scripts, then a plain `./scripts/deploy.ps1`, which updated itself to `main` b27f0c1), ended **NOT DONE**. The coordinator filed [#63](https://github.com/MarcBushong/fabric-database-hub-demo/issues/63) with the workaround (deallocate and start the host, then run `./scripts/deploy.ps1` again) and approved the fix with a condition: "count a host with no power state and an agent that isn't Ready as agent-down only once it has stayed that way for the same time the running-host case requires, never on a single read. A VM that Azure is still starting or updating for a few minutes must not be deallocated." The repair must stay one-click. The owner's `rg-dbhub-demo` has `DbHubT2BuildUtc` empty, so the owner's demo isn't in this state.

**Work summary.**

- **What happened on vu (ET):**
  - Its first deploy, on 3881ea1 from 22:30, started T2's bootstrap generation at 23:06 (`DbHubT2BuildUtc` 2026-11-18T04:06:32Z). A tenant governance job then stopped T4 at 00:06 and deallocated both VMs at 00:48, and the run ended **NOT DONE** at 01:24, so nothing cleared the record.
  - The rerun at 01:27 started the VMs. From then on, archost01 stayed "updating", with no power state and its VM agent Not Ready.
  - The update (03:30 to 04:24): `Get-DemoVmExtensionActivity` counted only a running VM whose agent isn't Ready as busy, so the settle found the host idle and sent its artifacts, and the chunk stayed **Pending** for 900 seconds. The watchdog then stood down: "its loader started a bootstrap generation at 2026-11-18T04:06:32Z that hasn't been seen to finish", with `agentDown` and `agentDead` false, so the rebuild's cue never came. `DEPLOY.EXTENSIONS_ARCHOST01` was a **Fail**, and every later run would have ended the same way.
- **The fix, in `VmExtensionHelpers.ps1`:**
  - `Get-DemoVmExtensionActivity` counts a VM with a provisioning state, no power state, and its agent not Ready as busy, "the VM's start or update (no power state, and its agent isn't Ready)", so nothing is sent to it. It returns that as `NoPower`.
  - `Wait-DemoVmExtensionSettled` returns `NoPowerMinutes`, how long every read has shown it, and `Invoke-DemoVmSettle` passes that through `Invoke-DemoVmWatchdog` to `Restart-DemoVmOnce`.
  - `Restart-DemoVmOnce`, for the T2 host: a first read with no power state and the agent not Ready starts `Wait-DemoVmAgentDown`, which reads the instance view again every 15 seconds for the rest of the 20 minutes, and at least once. The host stays down while its agent isn't Ready and it shows no power state, starting, or running; a Ready agent, or another power state, ends it.
    - **Down:** R871's path. No restart, the chunks' deletes, one deallocate and start, and `AgentDead`, R872's cue to rebuild the host, when that doesn't bring it back.
    - **Not down, with no chunks:** no restart and no deallocate, and the watchdog stays available for a later stall in the run.
  - `Get-DemoHostRestartBlocker`: a recorded generation older than 180 minutes (`$script:T2BuildRecordMaxMinutes`, the default of `deploy.ps1 -T2WaitMinutes`) doesn't block. A newer one, or one that can't be read, still does. Each generation's start records its own time.
  - **Why 20 minutes:** the settle gives a running VM's agent 20 minutes (`-FirstMinutes`) before the watchdog counts it down. The settle's own reads count toward the same 20, so a stuck host waits about as long as in R871, not twice as long.
- **Tests** (`DbHubDemo.OneCommand.Tests.ps1`, 10 new):
  - the activity with no power state (3 cases) and the generation's age;
  - 20 minutes, read by read, before the deallocate and start: no power state throughout, and a start whose agent never comes Ready;
  - no restart and no deallocate when it's brief: a start that ends with the agent Ready, and a deallocate meanwhile;
  - the settle's minutes counted, through the watchdog, and at least one read again.
  - Two fixtures changed: the blocker tests' recorded generation is 30 minutes old instead of a fixed 2026-10-29 time, and the restart test's host runs with its agent Ready before its restart.

**Changed files.** `scripts/modules/DbHubDemo/Private/VmExtensionHelpers.ps1`, `tests/unit/DbHubDemo.OneCommand.Tests.ps1`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/troubleshooting.md`, and this report.

### PowerShell Direct into T2's guest after an update (#65, 2026-11-18)

**Why.** The user hit a T2 failure while upgrading their own demo with `./scripts/deploy.ps1` and asked: "Is this a me problem or an unexpected bug", then "Do we need to put a bug fix to correct it". The coordinator confirmed a bug, filed [#65](https://github.com/MarcBushong/fabric-database-hub-demo/issues/65), and set the requirements: one click every time, upgrades included; failures and automatic recoveries on the status page and in the run summary; nothing existing broken; docs current. The user then decided: "Push the bug fix now no need to wait for that" (the live reproduction), with the coordinator's scope: a short bounded retry for a break like the user's, the restart-once fallback for one that stays, and anything else deferred.

**What happened.**

- **The user's demo (UTC):** the update's bundle started a new bootstrap generation at 18:46:43, and every step was checked again. `GuestSignInCleanup`'s check ran from 18:48:06 to 18:50:36; its in-guest scan was one PowerShell Direct session from 18:48:06.75 to 18:49:24.84 (the guest's Windows PowerShell 400 and 403 events). Arc onboarding ran during it, because a guest restored from the golden snapshot gets `-Force` (`TrackHelpers.ps1`): two probe sessions at 18:48:37 worked, but no session started in the guest from 18:48:39.86 until the scan's ended, although the marker's Run Command was created at 18:49:01. The marker's session got its server at 18:49:25.12, 0.3 seconds after the scan's ended; that process ended 0.15 seconds later, and `archost01` logged "Arc WriteMarker failed: ... The Hyper-V socket target process has ended" at 18:49:25.97. Sessions worked again from 18:49:26, and the rest of the pass passed. No crash, memory pressure, or Defender detection in the guest: 5.7 GB of 8 GB free, SQL Server at 520 MB.
- **vu (an existing user's update from 3881ea1):** the same check ran from 13:45:58 to 13:49:10, and T2's activity profile (`DEPLOY.PROFILE_T2`) ran alongside; PowerShell Direct then stayed broken for more than 20 minutes ("PSSessionStateBroken", the guest Running with its heartbeat OK) until the guest restarted. A later update whose bundle didn't change didn't break, and neither did a new deployment.
- **Why `deploy.ps1` ran alongside:** a pass whose every step is already in the desired state writes `health.json` only at its end, so for the 5 minutes of the check `deploy.ps1` reads the last generation's Ready, and the golden path's `-Force` skips the host-state gate.
- **The error:** PowerShell's client raises "The Hyper-V socket target process has ended" when the guest's end of an established session closes its stream ([RemoteSessionHyperVSocket.cs, OutOfProcTransportManager.cs](https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/tree/master/src/System.Management.Automation/engine/remoting)), so a step that meets it sees the guest's PowerShell process end; Windows doesn't log why. Avoiding the overlap (T2's PowerShell Direct steps waiting for the host's check, or sharing its lock) is left for a follow-up.

**Work summary.**

- **The guest side** (`vm/hyperv-guest/GuestVm.ps1`): `Test-DemoGuestChannelBroken` (the error, or `PSSessionStateBroken`), `Test-DemoGuestChannel` (probes; Broken only while the guest runs with a healthy heartbeat), `Get-DemoGuestRecoveryDecision` (None, Wait for a guest up less than 5 minutes, Exhausted when the run's key already restarted it, or Restart; nothing during a golden capture), and `Invoke-DemoGuestRecovery`: under a host-wide mutex, three probes 10 seconds apart (Healed: the caller runs its step again), else the decision; a restart is recorded in `guest-recovery.json` first, then `Stop-VM -Force` (a clean shutdown; `-TurnOff` only after 6 minutes) and `Start-VM`, and `Wait-DemoGuestOnline`. It never throws.
- **Who calls it:** Arc onboarding (`Invoke-DemoArcOnboardWithRecovery`: an action that failed with the error, or a probe that found the guest unreachable with a broken channel, runs again once); T2's relay (`Invoke-DemoWorkloadControl.ps1`: a probe before an activity command, and after any command that failed with it, which then runs again once; `Wait-GoldenGuest -BrokenChannelSeconds 30` ends its wait early on a channel that stays broken); and the host's bootstrap (`Test-DemoHostGuestReachable`, once per generation, only for an onboarded guest).
- **Run keys:** `deploy.ps1` gives each run its own (`deploy-` and 12 characters of the status page's run ID), passed to the host's Run Commands and to T2's relay requests; the session control has one an hour; the bootstrap one per generation.
- **What the user sees** (`GuestRecoveryHelpers.ps1`): `DEPLOY.T2.GUESTRETRY`, a **Warning**, for a break that was over; `DEPLOY.T2.GUESTRESTART`, a **Warning** that says what broke and that the restart cleared it, or a **Fail** when the guest still didn't answer; each recovery once, from the step's evidence or the host's health (`guestRecovery`). The status page's T2 row "Recovery of PowerShell Direct into arcsql01", and **DONE**'s note. A relay command that ran after a recovery is a **Warning** in the session's results too.
- **Timeouts:** the Arc probe's Run Command 600 to 1,500 seconds, the activity profile's 900 to 1,800, so a restart fits.
- **The review of 962c107 (PR #66), two Medium findings:**
  - **A restart cut short left the guest off:** Stop-VM and Start-VM run in the caller's process, so Ctrl+C during a restart, a rerun's delete of the leftover Arc probe Run Command, or a Run Command's timeout between them left `arcsql01` Off, and nothing started it again. `Complete-DemoGuestRecoveryInterrupted` now finishes such a restart: only when `guest-recovery.json`'s latest entry has no `endedUtc`, under the recovery lock, for the same guest (its VM ID, now in each entry), and never while a golden capture runs or a capture record isn't released. It starts the guest, waits until it answers, and ends the entry with `stoppedBy` Interrupted. The host's bootstrap runs it every 5 minutes, and `Invoke-DemoGuestRecovery` and the Arc probe's unreachable path first. The host's own stop (`StopGuest`) ends an unfinished entry (`HostStop`), so nothing starts the guest it stops. deploy.ps1 reports a finished one as `DEPLOY.T2.GUESTRESTART` at the time it was finished.
  - **An older bundle hid the real failure:** the Arc script is sent inline, but the recovery's functions come from the host's installed bundle, so a host whose bundle predates them (`configure-arc.ps1` after a pull, `test-t2-golden.ps1 -Onboard` on an older snapshot) got a CommandNotFoundException. Without them, the failure is thrown as it was, and the Probe's result returned unchanged.
- **The second review of d7950e2 (PR #66), two Medium findings and one Low:**
  - **No restart on a host restored from the golden snapshot, the default path:** the recovery took the mere presence of `golden\capture-in-progress.json` as a capture in progress, but Prepare writes that marker before the snapshot, so every restored copy carries it, and the restore's Release leaves it. Every recovery there decided None, and the repair never started a guest. `Test-DemoGuestCaptureInProgress` now reads the marker as the golden script's `Get-GoldenCaptureProgress` does: it counts only on the host it names (`sourceAzureVmId`, against this host's VM ID from the Instance Metadata Service), for 6 hours, and fails closed when the marker or the VM ID can't be read.
  - **A restart cut short while the guest was still shutting down left it off:** Hyper-V reports a guest Running until its operating system powers off, so the repair took it for running and closed the entry once the guest was off. Now a guest that still runs the boot the restart began on (its uptime is longer than the time since the entry) is restarted (`Restart-DemoGuestVm`: up to 6 minutes for its shutdown, then turned off, then started); one that booted since only gets its entry completed; an entry is never closed while the guest is still off. The bootstrap's call is bounded: 6 minutes for a shutdown and 5 for the guest to answer.
  - **The profile Run Command's short line** kept a recovery only when it restarted the guest, without its action or time, so a retry wasn't reported and a restart could be reported twice. It keeps both now, read field by field for any relay's version.

**Changed files.** `vm/hyperv-guest/GuestVm.ps1`, `vm/bootstrap/HostSteps.ps1`, `vm/bootstrap/Invoke-HostBootstrap.ps1`, `vm/bootstrap/Invoke-DemoArcOnboard.ps1`, `vm/bootstrap/Invoke-DemoGoldenGuest.ps1`, `vm/bootstrap/Invoke-DemoWorkloadControl.ps1`, `vm/health/Get-DemoHealth.ps1`, `vm/health/health.schema.json`, `vm/health/README.md`, `vm/bootstrap/README.md`; `scripts/modules/DbHubDemo/DbHubDemo.psm1`, `Private/GuestRecoveryHelpers.ps1` (new), `Private/ParallelDeployment.ps1`, `Private/TrackHelpers.ps1`, `Private/ProgressHelpers.ps1`, `Private/DeployExperience.ps1`, `Private/ActivityProfileHelpers.ps1`, `Private/LifecycleHelpers.ps1`, `Public/Invoke-DemoArcOnboarding.ps1`, `Public/Invoke-DemoWorkloadCommand.ps1`; tests `Vm.ArcOnboard.Tests.ps1`, `Vm.WorkloadSteps.Tests.ps1`, `Vm.GoldenGuest.Tests.ps1`, `DbHubDemo.GuestRestart.Tests.ps1` (new), `DbHubDemo.Arc.Tests.ps1`, `DbHubDemo.Progress.Tests.ps1`; `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/deployment.md`, `docs/troubleshooting.md`, and this report.

### The Database Hub GA updates: the Database Agent loop, T2's migration assessment, and the GA wording (2026-11-18)

**Why.** Microsoft Ignite made Database Hub generally available on 2026-11-17, with real-time dashboards for SQL, PostgreSQL, and Cosmos DB, Optimization insights, and Database Agents (preview) for Azure SQL Database. The coordinator reviewed the three announcements and recommended six changes, and the user said "Create a new branch and do them all". This entry covers items 3 to 6, on `ignite-updates`. On 2026-11-18 the owner, answering the coordinator, set T3's lowest-cost maximum to 2 vCores and the session ceiling to $20, because Database Agents doesn't support one-vCore serverless databases. The user then directed, the same day: "Make sure to account for users signing in and demoing this themselves and repeatable. Simple and one click as possible".

**Decisions.**

- **The response runs inside Run all** (one notebook, one action). At 85% of its window, T3's agent beat makes Database Agents' documented manual response itself, so the presenter needs no second action ([ADR 0013](adr/0013-agent-experience.md#amendment-general-availability-and-the-database-agent-loop-on-t3-2026-11-18)).
- **`FORCE_LAST_GOOD_PLAN` is held off for the beat** (the owner, 2026-11-18), so automatic tuning doesn't fix the regression before the agent raises its issue. Every way a session ends turns it back on:
  - The nightly safety stop can't change anything ([ADR 0024](adr/0024-nightly-safety-stop.md)), so after it the next run on T3 restores the setting. That needs no role change (the coordinator's option A).
  - `stop-demo.ps1` releases the hold through T3 itself, before it stops T1, and `deploy.ps1`'s setup restores it too. Before the review, `stop-demo.ps1` wrote the option through Azure Resource Manager, which could undo an off set outside the demo.
- **The showcase:** the cycle-2 timing, at most two T3 incidents at once, and the cycle-3 recurrence beat, which stays (the coordinator, 2026-11-18; [ADR 0010](adr/0010-workload-generator-technology.md#amendment-the-database-agent-beat-2026-11-18)).
- **The engine dashboards are linked, not rebuilt** (the coordinator's option a): no Log Analytics workspace.
- **T2's assessment stays out of the history:** the notebooks have no Azure Resource Manager token, so it shows on the status page and in Database Hub. Database Hub's own inventory carries it (`properties.migrationAssessment`, read through the Database Hub CLI skill), so the Insights app's live estate can show it too.

### T5: Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL (2026-11-18)

**Why.** User-directed, 2026-11-18: item 2 of the Ignite 2026 review ("Azure Cosmos DB as T5"), in "Create a new branch and do them all", and "Make sure to account for users signing in and demoing this themselves and repeatable. Simple and one click as possible". Database Hub in Microsoft Fabric, generally available since 2026-11-17, covers Azure Cosmos DB in Overview, Estate, Performance (normalized RU consumption, throttled requests, availability), and Security, from Azure Monitor's platform metrics with no setup ([monitor Azure Cosmos DB](https://learn.microsoft.com/fabric/database/hub/monitor-cosmos-db)). The demo had no Cosmos DB. The coordinator's decisions: a private endpoint in both network modes (secure by default, rather than a service endpoint), the free tier when the subscription's one slot is free, and the DBA moment, normalized RU at 100% with 429s and then the recovery, live ([ADR 0027](adr/0027-t5-cosmos-db.md)).

**Work summary.**

1. **The account** (`infra/modules/cosmos01.bicep`, `cosmos01-access.bicep`, `infra/modules/demo.bicep`, `network.bicep`, `config/versions.json` `cosmosdb`): `cosmos01-<deploymentId>`, Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL, one region, Session consistency, `disableLocalAuth`, `disableKeyBasedMetadataWriteAccess`, public network access off, TLS 1.2; the database `contosocare` and the container `patient-events` (`/patientId`, hash v2) at 400 RU/s manual, with the `payload` filler excluded from the index. A private endpoint in `snet-pe` with the `privatelink.documents.azure.com` zone and a zone group in both network modes, and an NSG rule for T1's subnet on 443. T1's system-assigned identity gets Cosmos DB Built-in Data Contributor at the account (`sqlRoleAssignments`, a child resource that Contributor writes; no Azure role assignment, ADR 0008). No availability zones (1.25 times the throughput price) and the default periodic backup: PSRule's two Cosmos DB findings are suppressed with the reason.
2. **The free tier** (`Resolve-DemoT5FreeTier`, `DEPLOY.T5.FREETIER`): resolved before the template through Azure Resource Graph. An existing account keeps what it has (Azure sets it only at creation); a new one gets it when no other account in the subscription has it, and not when Resource Graph can't be read (a **Warning**), or in an internal subscription (`subscriptionPolicies.quotaId` `Internal_*`, a **Warning**; live finding below). A refusal deploys the template again without it, once, with Azure's reason (`Test-DemoT5FreeTierRefusal`, `Get-DemoT5FreeTierRefusalReason`), and replaces the earlier **Pass**. `t5UseFreeTier` false never asks.
3. **Deployment and upgrade** (`Invoke-DemoTemplateDeployment`, `Get-DemoDeploymentParameter`, `ParallelDeployment.ps1`, `Invoke-DemoDeployment.ps1`, `TrackHelpers.ps1`, `ProgressHelpers.ps1`, `DeployExperience.ps1`): the template's `t5Enabled` and `t5FreeTier`; T1's track's `T5` step in stage T4 (`Test-DemoT5`, then `Invoke-DemoT5WarmUp` through T1's runner, retrying transient 401, 403, 408, 429, 449, 503, DNS, and timeouts every 45 seconds for up to 10 minutes); `METRICS.T5` in the run's validation and DONE's gate; **DONE** needs `HUB.ESTATE.T5` and `METRICS.T5` unless T5 is off. An environment without the account: `DEPLOY.T5.MISSING` turns a resume into a run from preflight, so the template creates it. `t5Enabled` false: `DEPLOY.T5.OFF`. The status page's **T5: Azure Cosmos DB** group.
4. **Checks** (`Test-DemoT5`, `T5Helpers.ps1`): `T5.ACCOUNT`, `T5.ENTRAONLY`, `T5.NETWORK` (public access off, the private endpoint approved), `T5.CONTAINER` (database, container, partition key, 400 RU/s), `T5.FREETIER`, `T5.ACCESS` (the data-plane role for T1's identity at the account), and `METRICS.T5` (requests and normalized RU in the last 15 minutes); `HUB.ESTATE.T5` through Resource Graph (`ResourceGraph.Estate.kql`). `validate.ps1 -Area T5`, the Workload area, `status.ps1` (`STATUS.T5`, with the last 15 minutes' peak normalized RU and 429s), `start-demo.ps1` (`START.T5`), `stop-demo.ps1` (`STOP.T5`, **Not supported**: what bills on), preflight (`Microsoft.DocumentDB`).
5. **Cost** (`Get-DemoCostEstimate`, `estimate-cost.ps1`, preflight, the Cost area): idle all month: the throughput (`RUs`, or the Free Tier meters), about 1 GB of storage, the private endpoint, its DNS zone, and Defender for Azure Cosmos DB (`CosmosDbs`, `Standard 100 RU/s`) when that plan is on Standard; Defender CSPM doesn't bill Cosmos DB. `estimate-cost.ps1` reads whether the subscription's free tier is taken when it's signed in (`Get-DemoT5FreeTierStatus`), and prices list otherwise. Dated example (2026-11-18, West US 3): $31.41 a month at list price, $7.80 on the free tier, plus about $3.50 with Defender; the default light-use month goes from $315.82 to $347.23 at list price, within the $375 ceiling.
6. **The runner** (`workload-generator`, by a sub-agent): `--target T5 --server <account>.documents.azure.com`, the documented REST API over HTTPS with an Entra token for T1's managed identity (gateway mode, so only 443 through the private endpoint), acting only in `contosocare`/`patient-events`, with its own run store (`C:\ProgramData\DbHubDemo\t5-runs.json`) and profile (`activity-t5.json`). `healthy-baseline` upserts and point-reads 500 patients' fixed ids (about 10 MB at most). `ru-storm` (T5 only; 600 seconds by default, 1800 at most; 8 writers, waves of `stormSeconds` 150 and `calmSeconds` 90) upserts 100 fixed 2 KB documents in one hot partition and deletes them at its end, paced to 200 RU/s, however it ends; `reset --target T5` deletes any left over. 429s honor `x-ms-retry-after-ms` and count as the scenario's signal, not failures. `business-day` runs it at :25 each hour for 8 minutes; the showcase at minutes 3 (10 minutes) and 18 (8 minutes) of each 30-minute cycle.

### T2's PowerShell Direct steps wait for the host's pass over a new generation (#65 follow-up, 2026-11-19)

**Why.** #65's fix (R892) clears a broken PowerShell Direct channel, but it left the overlap that breaks it: the coordinator asked, after the live validation, that "deploy.ps1's T2 PowerShell Direct steps wait for the host's check pass after a new bundle, or share its bootstrap.lock, so an update no longer races it", with the review's two low-likelihood edges, on `ignite-updates` so that the combined final tests cover it. The user, the same night: "complete all that you can with your current assumptions and recommendations and I can adjust any decision points in the morning and redo".

**What made the overlap.** The loader starts a generation (`<bundle>-<UTC time>`, in `settings.json`) and the bootstrap task at once; the state machine sets every step Pending, saves `state.json` before each step, and writes `health.json` only when a step converges or when the pass ends. A pass whose steps all check out (an update's) therefore leaves the pass before's report in `health.json`, "Ready: Every step is in the desired state", for its 4 to 5 minutes, and `Get-DemoHealth.ps1`, which `deploy.ps1` reads through Run Command, printed that file. vu (2026-11-18): "step starting (1 of 19)" at 13:46:50, `Ready` at 13:48:51, and `DEPLOY.PROFILE_T2` broken within the pass. `Wait-DemoT2HostBuild`'s bundle check (2026-11-09) doesn't catch it when the same bundle is sent again, and a golden copy's Arc onboarding (`-Force`) doesn't read the host's state at all.

**Work summary.**

- **The health read** (`vm/health/Get-DemoHealth.ps1`, `Get-DemoHealthPassFact`): on the T2 host (`settings.json`'s role `ArcHost`), a generation that the loader started in the last 30 minutes and that `health.json` doesn't report is reported as `InProgress` (status **Warning**), in both views, with that generation, `state.json`'s current step once that generation's pass has started, `generationPending`, and the file's own `reportedGeneration` and `reportedState`. The script is sent from the checkout, so it works with any bundle on the host. Chosen over sharing the bootstrap's lock, which would hold Run Commands for a whole pass, a build's included, and keep the bootstrap from running while one waits.
- **The waits:** every wait for the host takes `InProgress` as in progress, so `Wait-DemoT2HostBuild`, `Invoke-DemoArcConfiguration`'s, and the wait before T2's activity profile go on until the pass reports; `Wait-DemoT2HostBuild` reads every minute while `generationPending` (its 5-minute poll would add up to 5 minutes to an update) and says that the host checks every step again for the run's generation. Arc onboarding with `-Force` waits until the pass ends (`-PassWaitMinutes`, 20 by default), then goes ahead with R892's recovery and says so; the review below made it wait through the steps the pass converges.
- **The review's edges** (`vm/hyperv-guest/GuestVm.ps1`): `Complete-DemoGuestRecoveryInterrupted` doesn't restart a guest that still runs its old boot while a golden capture is in progress on the host, and keeps its entry for a later run; `Test-DemoGuestRestartedSince` takes a running guest whose uptime rounds to 0 (under about 3 seconds) as restarted, where it said it couldn't tell.

**Changed files.** `vm/health/Get-DemoHealth.ps1`, `vm/health/README.md`, `vm/hyperv-guest/GuestVm.ps1`, `scripts/modules/DbHubDemo/Public/Invoke-DemoArcOnboarding.ps1`, `scripts/modules/DbHubDemo/Private/GuidedStopHelpers.ps1`; tests `Vm.WorkloadSteps.Tests.ps1`, `Vm.ArcOnboard.Tests.ps1`, `DbHubDemo.Arc.Tests.ps1`, `DbHubDemo.GuestRestart.Tests.ps1`; `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/deployment.md`, `docs/troubleshooting.md`, and this report.

**Validation.** New tests: the health read reports a pending generation as `InProgress` with its pass's step, and "starting" before the pass begins, in both views, and leaves `health.json` as it is once it reports that generation, on T1, and after 30 minutes; `Wait-DemoT2HostBuild` reads every minute while the generation is pending and ends once the pass reports; Arc onboarding with `-Force` waits for the pass before its probe, and goes ahead after `-PassWaitMinutes` with a **Warning** in the log; no restart under a golden capture, with the entry kept and finished after the capture; a running guest whose uptime rounds to 0 counts as restarted. The touched files' tests, on this commit alone and with `Set-StrictMode -Version Latest` as CI runs them (with `Repo.LifecycleScripts.Tests.ps1`): 343 passed. Live proof of the review fixes from #65 (2026-11-19, `dbhubpn` from `main`, no deploy running): an interrupted restart that left `arcsql01` off was finished by the host's bootstrap 2.5 minutes later, and one cut off before the guest was off was restarted by the next pass; both entries closed `Interrupted`, recovered. The full static validation, with #68's fix, is in the next section.

**Risks.** R902 new.

### A first deployment on a busy Fabric capacity (#68, 2026-11-19)

**Why.** The live validation of #65 found it: a new deployment from `main` on the owner's shared F4 ended **NOT DONE** after 82 minutes, and the coordinator filed [#68](https://github.com/MarcBushong/fabric-database-hub-demo/issues/68): "A new user whose capacity is busy gets NOT DONE on their first deployment and needs a second run. That breaks one-click." The coordinator's requirements: while the history run is queued or running, the Fabric track waits for it, with a longer bound that the status page shows, and then refreshes the model; a run still queued at that bound gets the model refreshed again once it completes; otherwise the step is a Warning that says what will fill the model, never a Fail; and an update whose model already has data isn't slowed down.

**What happened** (UTC, `dbhubpn`): the track started `NB_DatabaseHub_LiveActivity` at 02:02:45 to create the lakehouse's history tables; after 10 minutes it was still NotStarted (`FABRIC.NOTEBOOKRUN.NB_DATABASEHUB_LIVEACTIVITY`, a **Warning**), and the history model, imported at 02:13, refreshed with no `scenario_runs` table: "0xC14700C7 We cannot access the source Delta table". The queued run started at 02:18:07 and completed at 02:19:23. `./scripts/deploy.ps1` again ended **DONE** in 24 minutes.

**Work summary.**

- **The wait** (`Wait-DemoFabricNotebookJob`, new in `Private/HistoryFirstRunHelpers.ps1`, which `Invoke-DemoFabricNotebookRun` now uses): the job is read every poll, bounded by elapsed time as before; while it's queued or running, the status page's row says so with the minutes so far and the bound, and the console says so every 5 minutes it stays queued. `Invoke-DemoFabricNotebookRun`'s evidence adds `queuedSeconds`, and, for a job that hasn't finished, `jobLocation`, its job instance, so the track can follow it.
- **The first run's bound:** `configure-fabric.ps1 -HistoryRunWaitMinutes` (45 by default) for the run it starts by itself when it created the notebook or the lakehouse, with `-ProgressPath` for the status page's `Fabric.Items` row; `-RunLiveActivity`'s wait is unchanged. `Invoke-DemoFabricStage` passes both from the track (`HistoryRunWaitMinutes`, `HistoryFollowMinutes`).
- **The track** (`TrackHelpers.ps1`, Fabric): a first run that failed is a **Warning** (`Set-DemoHistoryFirstRunWarning`); a refresh that found no tables after a first run that didn't complete is a **Warning** that says what fills the model (`Set-DemoHistoryRefreshWaiting`, only for 0xC14700C7 or 0xC14700DF and that run; any other refresh failure stays a **Fail**); and a run still queued or running is followed for up to 45 more minutes (`Invoke-DemoHistoryFirstRunFollowUp`, on the `Fabric.Report` row), then the history model's step runs again (`Invoke-DemoPowerBIStage`) before the Insights app, whose checks read the model. The records say what happened in the end, each keeping what it said first (`earlierMessage`).

**Changed files.** `scripts/configure-fabric.ps1`, `scripts/modules/DbHubDemo/Private/HistoryFirstRunHelpers.ps1` (new), `Private/DeployHelpers.ps1`, `Private/TrackHelpers.ps1`, `Public/Invoke-DemoFabricNotebookRun.ps1`; tests `DbHubDemo.FabricTrack.Tests.ps1`, `DbHubDemo.Fabric.Tests.ps1`, `DbHubDemo.Tracks.Tests.ps1`; `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/deployment.md`, `docs/troubleshooting.md`, and this report.

**Validation.** New tests: a first run that starts after 15 minutes of queue passes, with the status page's line and its bound (the notebook run, and `configure-fabric.ps1` end to end); a run still queued at the bound returns its location; followed, it completes, the model's step runs again, and the Warning says so; still queued after the follow-up too, both records are **Warnings** that name the end-of-run snapshot, and nothing more runs; a first run that failed: **Warnings**, never a **Fail**, and nothing waits; an update, with no first run, waits for nothing, and its refresh failure stays a **Fail**, as does one after a first run that completed; and the whole Fabric step on the track: no **Fail**, the order Fabric stage, model, job read, model again, Insights app. The touched files' tests, with `Set-StrictMode -Version Latest` as CI runs them: 233 passed.

**The full static validation** (`./tests/Invoke-StaticValidation.ps1 -CI`, 2026-11-19, with the #65 follow-up before it, over `origin/ignite-updates` at 52df9bd):

- PSScriptAnalyzer: 0 findings in 376 files. Bicep, PSRule (302 rules), .NET, the Fabric app, and markdownlint pass.
- Pester, with `Set-StrictMode -Version Latest` as CI runs it: 4,741 tests; 4,695 passed, 0 failed, and 46 skipped; no unit test reached the Azure CLI.
  - 42 of the skips are the notebook simulations, which need Python 3 with pandas. With Python 3.11 and pandas, their files pass too (`Fabric.ControlNotebook`, `Fabric.Notebooks`, and `Fabric.PowerBI`: 171 passed, 1 skipped).
  - The other 4 need tools this PC doesn't have: gitleaks (3), and the history report generator's npm packages (1).
- The first full run, before the rebase onto 52df9bd, found three failures under strict mode, all from these two commits and fixed in them: two tests read an evidence property that isn't there, and `configure-fabric.ps1`'s new `-ProgressPath` didn't go through `Resolve-DemoUserPath`, as the repo's convention test requires.

### The review of the #65 follow-up and #68 (2026-11-19)

**Why.** The coordinator's independent review of 9d2a28e and 71241ad found one medium issue in the #65 follow-up, and a cosmetic one in #68, to fix "only if it's small"; #68 was otherwise clean.

**Work summary.**

- **Medium: a golden copy's Arc onboarding stopped waiting at the pass's first converging step.** `Invoke-DemoArcOnboarding -Force` waited only while the health read reported `generationPending`, which clears the first time the new generation writes `health.json`: the state machine writes it, `InProgress`, right before a step changes anything (`vm/bootstrap/lib/Runner.ps1`). An existing golden copy keeps its Arc marker, so after an update that step can be `WorkloadRunner`, whose install stops the workload in the guest over PowerShell Direct, and onboarding's probe and marker went into the guest during it; a golden copy has no other wait (`WaitForHostMinutes` stays 0). R892's recovery still caught a break, but the overlap stayed. Now `-Force` enters and keeps its wait while the host reports a pending generation, `InProgress`, `RebootPending`, or `NotStarted`, and stops at any other state, where a pass ends (`WaitingForArcOnboarding`, `Ready`, `ManualActionRequired`, `Failed`, `WaitingForProductKey`, or another wait), still within `-PassWaitMinutes` (20). The console says which state and step it waits for, and the **Warning** after the bound says the same. A new golden copy waits about as before: its Release renames the Arc marker, so its pass stops at `WaitingForArcOnboarding` once the steps before it check out.
- **Low (#68): a stale data check.** When the follow-up refreshed the history model again, the first model step's **Not selected** `FABRIC.SEMANTICMODEL.DATA` ("its measures weren't evaluated"), from before the model had tables, stayed beside the new one. The track now drops it once the follow-up's step has checked the data.

**Changed files.** `scripts/modules/DbHubDemo/Public/Invoke-DemoArcOnboarding.ps1`, `Private/TrackHelpers.ps1`; tests `DbHubDemo.Arc.Tests.ps1`, `DbHubDemo.Tracks.Tests.ps1`; `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/troubleshooting.md`, `vm/health/README.md`, and this report.

**Validation.** New tests: with `-Force`, a pending generation, then `InProgress` at `WorkloadRunner` with no `generationPending`, then `Ready`: four health reads, and the probe only after `Ready`; `RebootPending` and `NotStarted` are waited through, and `WaitingForArcOnboarding`, `ManualActionRequired`, `Failed`, `WaitingForProductKey`, and `WaitingForGuestSql` aren't waited on; at the bound, a pending generation and an `InProgress` pass both give `passPending` and a **Warning** that names them; and the Fabric track's results keep one `FABRIC.SEMANTICMODEL.DATA`, the follow-up's. Without the code changes, the three onboarding tests and the track's fail. The touched files' tests, with `Set-StrictMode -Version Latest` as CI runs them: 293 passed. The full static validation (`./tests/Invoke-StaticValidation.ps1 -CI`, over `origin/ignite-updates` at 7a2e586, with Python 3.11 and pandas for the notebook simulations): PSScriptAnalyzer 0 findings in 383 files; Pester 4,763 tests, 4,759 passed, 0 failed, and 4 skipped (gitleaks isn't on this PC, 3; the history report generator's npm packages, 1), and no unit test reached the Azure CLI; Bicep, PSRule (302 rules), .NET, the Fabric app, and markdownlint pass.

**Risks.** R902 updated.

### Ask: the GitHub Copilot chat in the Insights app (2026-11-18)

**Why.** The user, on the Ignite 2026 announcements (the Database Hub GA and its CLI skill): "Since there is GitHub Copilot support that we can then use to put into the Fabric app as well as a chat interface in the Rayfin app vs going to the GHCP locally", and "The goal would be to get insights from the data and trends and perform conversational analytics directly in the rayfin app"; every demo user has a GitHub Copilot license. Then: "The GitHub Copilot chat interface right in the App is a must and a gamechanger", and "Make sure to account for users signing in and demoing this themselves and repeatable. Simple and one click as possible."

**Decisions** (the coordinator, for the user, 2026-11-18; [ADR 0028](adr/0028-ask-copilot-in-the-insights-app.md)):

- **Sign-in:** one GitHub OAuth App, **Database Hub Insights Ask**, owned by MarcBushong, with the device flow and no client secret; its client ID ships in `config/versions.json`, so a deployer registers nothing.
- **The relay's image:** a public GitHub Container Registry image that the repository's own workflow builds, pinned by digest; users never run GitHub Actions.
- **The live estate:** the app's function as the app's identity, on the GA skill's 8 read-only routes, allowlisted and scoped to the demo's own subscription and resource group, without the skill's telemetry header; a narrow, documented exception to "documented interfaces only" ([ADR 0013's amendment](adr/0013-agent-experience.md#amendment-2026-11-18-the-ga-skill-and-one-narrow-exception)).
- **User steps:** a GitHub sign-in once per browser; an organization that restricts OAuth apps approves the app once; the strict content security policy tenant setting stays off. Nothing for a deployer.

**Work summary.**

- **The dock** (`fabric/app/src/copilot/`, on the redesign session's contract): docked on the right, resizable, full screen; streaming answers with the app's own charts and tables (`ChartView`); **Show the source** (the DAX, or the Database Hub routes), copy, **Export**, **New chat**, suggested follow-ups, and starters from the prompt pack, shown only when the environment can answer them (the live ones with the estate function; T5's once the history holds its metrics, from one `[Has Cosmos DB Bins]` query); **Ask Copilot** and **Ask why** from every visual; the GitHub account in the shell (`useCopilotAccount`), with sign-out and switch account; every state a viewer can meet, in plain words (no relay, waking from zero, sign-in off, no Copilot, an organization's policy, an expired sign-in).
- **The tools, in the page:** `run_dax` (read-only `EVALUATE` through the app's delegated `history` connector, bounded rows), `show_chart` (validated with `validateChartSpec`), and `estate_overview`; Copilot gets a guide to the history model built from its TMDL (`npm run guide:build`), names and not data.
- **The relay** (`ask-relay/`): the GitHub Copilot SDK 2.0.0 behind a WebSocket, holding no credential; the device flow and token renewal (GitHub's endpoints refuse browser calls); exact-origin CORS for HTTP and WebSocket, rate and size limits, session caps, timeouts; a distroless, non-root image from digest-pinned Azure Linux bases.
- **The live estate** (`fabric/app/rayfin/functions/`): `estateOverview` reads inventory (with each SQL Server instance's migration assessment, 31cf1c1), health (SQL and PostgreSQL CPU, storage, and memory; Cosmos DB availability and RU), and security (Entra authentication, auditing, customer-managed keys), filtered to the demo's scope, cached for 60 seconds; the dock's tool calls `readEstate(view)` (`src/copilot/estate.ts`), and the pages' `useLiveEstate(view)` (`src/data/live-estate.ts`, the redesign's) loads it, so they share one call.
- **Deploy:** `configure-fabric-app.ps1`, so `deploy.ps1`, deploys the relay (`infra/ask/ask-relay.bicep`, `Invoke-DemoAskRelaySetup`, registering `Microsoft.App` when it's missing), writes its address into the app, sets the relay's origin to the app's after `rayfin up`, wakes and checks it, and reads the strict-CSP setting (`ASK.RELAY`, `ASK.RELAY.HEALTH`, `ASK.SIGNIN`, `ASK.CSP`; never a **Fail**). The status page has its own non-blocking row, **DONE** a note; `start-demo.ps1` wakes the relay; `-CheckOnly` checks it; `destroy.ps1` deletes it with the resource group. The cost estimate prices it from the Retail Prices API.
- **The image's workflow:** `.github/workflows/ask-relay-image.yml` (on a push to `main` or `ignite-updates` for `ask-relay/**` or the workflow, or by hand; never on a pull request or in a fork; `contents: read`, `packages: write`, actions pinned by SHA), tagged by commit SHA, the digest in the run's summary and annotations. Its first run, on e80210e (2026-11-19), published `ask-relay@sha256:c237ae74fc11`, public from that first publish from this public repository; the owner keeps it public and pinned (2026-11-19), since a public package can't be made private again, only deleted. Its run on dc2642d, with the security review's fixes, published `ask-relay@sha256:8825035c813a`, and its run on 87af20c, with R925's fixes and their review's, published `ask-relay@sha256:85fdef25f31d`, which `config/versions.json` pins now.
- **Lockfiles (2026-11-19):** `ask-relay/package-lock.json` (38 entries) and `fabric/app/rayfin/functions/package-lock.json` (13) had SHA-1 integrity from an npm feed proxy; each now carries the same tarball's SHA-512 (`npm pack`, its SHA-1 checked against the lockfile's), `npm ci` verified them, and `DbHubDemo.FabricApp.Tests.ps1` checks every `package-lock.json` in the repository for npmjs.org and SHA-512, not only the app's.
- **The security review's fixes (2026-11-19):** an independent review of e80210e found no way for a viewer's GitHub token to leak, and five bugs, fixed before the image's pin. (1, high) The relay parsed each request's target with `new URL()` before its origin check, so `GET //x:a` threw and stopped the process: it reads paths as text now, both handlers catch, and `uncaughtException` and `unhandledRejection` are logged, never fatal. (2) A failed start left its socket open, kept alive by the page's pings: the relay and the page close it, the page pings only a started conversation, and an account that can't use Copilot here can't send. (3) One client could hold every place or slip the limits: limits key on the address the ingress appends to `X-Forwarded-For`, a full limiter forgets only ended windows, only started conversations count, a socket must start within 10 seconds, a client holds at most 4 sockets, and Copilot checks run 1 per client and 4 in all. (4) The 6-month refresh token was thrown away, so viewers were signed out daily: the page renews before `/auth/user` and `/auth/copilot`, renews once when GitHub refuses a token, ends a sign-in only when GitHub refuses the refresh token, re-reads storage and renews under `navigator.locks`, and follows other tabs' storage events, reconnecting on a new token. (5) A poll that failed on the way ended the sign-in: it waits longer and goes on until the code expires.
- **The redesign's two notes (2026-11-19):** the chat's tests pass on Node 26, which `config/versions.json` pins, as well as on CI's Node 24, with the redesign's shared `src/test/setup.ts` (Node 25 and later have their own `localStorage`); and the system message, with the model guide, and the page tools load when the first conversation starts rather than with the app, which takes the main chunk from 799 KB to 761 KB (231 KB to 218 KB gzip). ### The Insights app as a DBA console (2026-11-18)

**Why.** The user, on `ignite-updates`: "Adjust the Fabric Rayfin App to really be a DBA's dream app to manage and view their estate with the conversational analytics", "more professional, and functional and clean/modern", and "The GitHub Copilot chat interface right in the App is a must and a gamechanger"; then "Make sure to account for users signing in and demoing this themselves and repeatable. Simple and one click as possible". A separate session builds the Copilot chat; this entry is the app around it ([ADR 0029](adr/0029-insights-app-dba-console.md)).

**Decisions.**

- **Fluent 2** (`@fluentui/react-components` 9.75.2, `@fluentui/react-icons` 2.0.346, MIT): Fabric's own design language, accessible components, light, dark, and high-contrast themes from tokens, and React 19 support. The decorative visuals, Framer Motion, lucide, d3-sankey, d3-hierarchy, d3-interpolate, and the web fonts are gone.
- **A DBA's information architecture:** Overview, Estate (T1 to T5, with T4's read replica), Performance, Incidents, Findings, Readiness, Trends, Manage, and Live views, under a left navigation and a global target and period filter.
- **The Copilot contract first** (`src/copilot/contract.ts`, 935eeed): `AskContext`, `ChartSpec`, and `CopilotApi`, so the chat session and the pages built on it at once. `ChartView` draws every chart, the dock's too.
- **History and live, labeled everywhere:** the live estate comes from the chat session's function (the coordinator's decision 3), loaded through `import.meta.glob`, so the app builds without it and pages say why there's no live data.
- **Manage (the coordinator's decision for the user):** A, the app's Manage function, with C, copying the request for Run all, as the automatic fallback; the conditions are in ADR 0029.

**Work summary.**

- **Shell** (`src/shell/`, `src/App.tsx`, `src/main.tsx`, `src/theme/`): the top bar with the GitHub and Fabric account chips, the left navigation with a rail mode, the global filter with the History, Live, or Sample badge, the dock's region (resizable, full screen), and the Fabric-teal themes.
- **Pages** (`src/pages/`): the nine pages; T5's page from the Cosmos DB session's history contract; the Database Agent loop on Incidents from the agent loop's `database_agent` findings; Security and Optimization read Database Hub live; Overview's **Live now**.
- **Components** (`src/components/`): `VisualCard` (Ask Copilot, the data, the DAX or the Database Hub API calls, CSV, focus), `DataGrid` (sort, filter, CSV), KPI and health tiles, badges, and empty states.
- **Data** (`src/data/`): a `DataSource` behind the query client; the catalog's new queries `scenario-runs`, `daily-trend`, `agent-loop`, `cosmos-series`, and `cosmos-findings` (21 in all), with `mayBeEmpty`; the parsers for sessions, days, agent beats, and T5's captures.
- **Manage** (`src/lib/control.ts`, `src/lib/manage-client.ts`, `src/pages/ManagePage.tsx`): the actions, their bounds, the confirmation, the request's parameters, mode detection, and the copied lines for Run all.
- **The deploy-time check** (`Test-DemoFabricApp.ps1`): queries marked `mayBeEmpty` are said, not warned about; a Pester case.
- **`package-lock.json`:** every package from `registry.npmjs.org` with SHA-512. The Fluent packages had resolved through a mirror, which `DbHubDemo.FabricApp.Tests.ps1` caught; the hashes came from `npm pack`, matched npmjs's in public lock files, and `npm ci` verified them.
- **The preview** (`npm run dev:sample`, `src/preview/`): sample history and live answers, for design work and screenshots.
- **Docs:** the app's guide (Demo it yourself, pages, Copilot, Manage, update and delete), ADR 0029, and the app's parts of the presentation page and the walkthrough.
- **Manage's checks** (`rayfin/functions/src/manage-core.ts`, a6217ab): the caller's Rayfin token verified with the app's own keys from the pinned API, the operators, `REQUESTED_BY`, and only the documented actions within the control's caps; tested with Web Crypto keys, and kept equal to each `scenario.json` and the app's own parameters.
- **Manage's sending mode, built** (the owner's word for the night: "complete all that you can with your current assumptions and recommendations"): `manage.ts` registers `manageAccess`, `manageRequest`, and `manageJob` with `registerManage(udf)`, for the shared functions project's `function_app.ts`; their answers are in `manage-core.ts` and run `NB_DatabaseHub_Control` through the Fabric job API (`jobType=RunNotebook`) with `REQUESTED_BY` from the verified caller. A deployment whose function isn't set up says so, and the app copies each request for Run all instead. `configure-fabric-app.ps1` resolves the operators (`FABRIC.APP.OPERATORS`), writes the function's settings into the stage (`Set-DemoFabricAppManageSetting`, `FABRIC.APP.ACTIONS`: the app's API from the deployment record, the control notebook's IDs, and the operators), and, on an app's first deploy, writes them again with the API that deploy recorded and deploys once more. `NB_DatabaseHub_Control` has a `REQUESTED_BY` parameter, `"notebook"` by default, that every request it builds carries. The app's own answer types come from `manage-core.ts`, one definition for both sides.
- **The review of the server side (2026-11-19):** an independent review found no way for an unverified caller or a non-operator to start a job, and asked for four fixes, all in:
  1. **The token is bound to this app,** with the deployment record's IDs: its tenant (`tid`, or the tenant in Fabric's managed token's subject path) and this app (an audience of the app's ID or API, or Fabric's subject path and `xms_attr` for this app); exact `issuer` and `audience` pins wait for the identity proof, because the record holds neither. A token with an `oid` matches operators on it only; names count only without one.
  2. **Copy mode takes over** whenever the function can't send for anyone: it isn't set up, it can't confirm the caller, or the job API refuses or can't be reached. Read-only is only for a verified viewer who isn't an operator.
  3. **The control's own catalog:** the deploy writes it from the same runbook settings as the notebook's `CATALOG_JSON` (`Get-DemoFabricAppManageCatalog`): its targets (T5 only while it's on), its incidents, and a run's 5 to 120 minutes. healthy-baseline runs as the control's `baseline`, in copy mode too. After a start, the page follows the run's real state through `manageJob`, a failure included.
  4. **One request at a time:** while one of the control's runs is in progress, Manage offers only Stop now, which cancels that run first, so the stop starts on a small capacity; the wording that a new session "replaces" a running one is gone: the control follows it.
- **The second review (2026-11-19, at 1f40879):** findings 2 and 3 were resolved, and with empty pins another tenant or app was still blocked. It asked for four more, all in, each with a test that fails without it:
  1. **The app tie** is the token's audience (the app's ID, `api://<its ID>`, or its API) or Fabric's managed subject path through this app, never a key among its attributes (`xms_attr`), which a token for another app can carry; a pinned audience ties a token only when it names the app's ID. Fabric's sign-in email for the app (`rfn_email`) is read only after that tie, and it's the one name-based match: only without an `oid`, accepted until the identity proof ([ADR 0029](adr/0029-insights-app-dba-console.md)). A token with neither names no one, so copy mode takes over.
  2. **One request at a time, enforced:** `answerRequest` refuses every action but Stop now while one of the control's runs is queued or in progress, with that run in its answer, and sends nothing when it can't list them (copy mode). The page reads the run in progress again when an action opens, holds **Confirm** until it has, and reads it again after each start.
  3. **The cancel-then-stop race:** Fabric's cancel only asks (HTTP 202), so Stop now waits for the run it cancelled to end, reading it no sooner than `Retry-After`, and asks again while the capacity refuses the stop (HTTP 430 or 429), within 150 seconds: a function runs at most 240, and the app waits 200 for a request. If the stop still doesn't start, its answer says it cancelled the run and that nothing is stopping the session now, and the dialog's title says so.
  4. **A cancelled end phase keeps its history:** the function can't see whether the run it cancels is ending a session (the session's phase is in the control vault, which also holds the webhook URL, so the function has no token for it). So `NB_DatabaseHub_Control`'s Stop now finishes what such a run left: a session whose end passed with no stop recorded is stopped as its end would be (`session_unstopped`), and with no session running, the history of the session that last stopped, in the last 7 days, is saved once its telemetry has arrived (`stopped_history`, `save_stopped_history`), the way the pre-check saves an earlier session's. The page no longer suggests "Stop now first, then start a new one". The Database Agent beat and its timing are untouched.
- **ADR 0029:** the Copilot chat session's ADR, created first, is 0028 on its branch, so this one is 0029.
- **After dbhubc5's live look (the coordinator's fixes):** a neutral **Live · unavailable** badge in every state without live data, green only for a live answer; one period per sentence in the live states (c68f70b); and readiness (4bbc067): Overview's tile stays blank for a summary row of zeros and says what fills it, the Readiness page says it too, and `readiness-checks` is `mayBeEmpty`.
- **Readiness in every Run all** (4bbc067, the coordinator's decision): once the session runs, `NB_DatabaseHub_Control` runs `NB_DatabaseHub_Deployment` as a reference run in its own Spark session, read-only (`SAVE_RESULTS` on, `CONFIRM` and `PURGE_DEMO_TABLES` off), within 300 seconds, and says so in one line before the guide. A failure or a slow run is a **Warning** with the fix, and the session, the Database Agent beat, and the history go on. Before 4bbc067, only that notebook run by hand wrote `validation_results`, so a normal flow (deploy, then Run all) left Readiness empty.
- **Wait families by their own category** (09e28f0, found on dbhubc5's data): Incidents measured Tran Log IO, Buffer Latch, Network IO, Memory, and Parallelism incidents against all waits, so a detected log flush window read "peak 142 s, 0.7× its baseline". It now reads each family's category, as the analysis notebook's detector does (`WAIT_FAMILY_CATEGORIES`), from the waits query the page already runs: 20.4 s at 01:53 against 0.4 s, 35×, the detector's own 20.417. A ratio over 100 reads ">100×" with "baseline near zero".
- **T2 ready to migrate** (the coordinator's decision, 2026-11-18): Database Hub doesn't raise a ready migration assessment as an issue, so T2 never shows in its Optimization issues; the agent-loop session read its readiness in the inventory's rows instead. The app's **Ready to migrate** card, on Findings' Optimization tab and T2's page, reads it from the live inventory (the chat session adds `migrationAssessment` to it): readiness per Azure SQL target in Learn's words, when Azure Arc assessed it, **Ask Copilot** ("Which of my servers can move to Azure, and to what?"), and **Ask why** on a target that's not ready. Without the live source, it links T2's SQL Server instance in the Azure portal (Migration, Assessments), a link `Resolve-DemoFabricAppItem` builds at deploy time from the instance's own resource ID (`Get-DemoT2MigrationPortalLink`, one read-only ARM list).
- **One row per resource:** Database Hub's inventory lists a SQL Server on an Azure VM twice, as its SQL virtual machine and as its SQL Server instance from unified inventory, so Live now counted 2 SQL VMs, and the VM row's "Unknown" status read as not up. The app merges them (`uniqueResources`), and "Unknown" isn't "not up". The sample's PAYG license finding on T1 is gone: live, neither T1 nor T2 has one; the flags `hasMigrationAssessmentIssue` and `hasUsageReportingIssue` have their own words.
- **With T5 in `ignite-updates` (78e080a):** Manage's checks keep the catalog's `ru-storm` (T5, 10 minutes, 30 at most) and healthy-baseline on T5, so they still equal each `scenario.json`. Reset accepts T5, as the runbook and the control notebook do since T5 (it deletes what a cut-off RU storm left), and the session's and Stop now's descriptions say they save T5's metrics.
- **With Ask in `ignite-updates` (e80210e):** the chat session's `function_app.ts` registers Manage after the live estate (`registerManage(udf)`), and `rayfin.yml` keeps its one `services.functions` block, its comment naming both. The pages' live types are now the estate function's own (`estate-core.ts`, through `src/copilot/estate.ts`), with no copy in `live-estate.ts`, so the typecheck found where the pages assumed more than the function promises, each fixed: an answer with no data (the function has no scope) now shows the unavailable state with the function's reason instead of tiles stuck on "Reading" (`liveDataOf`); a Cosmos DB answer with RU but no account count still shows T5's tile; and a high-usage count the answer leaves out counts as zero. Each has a test that fails without its fix. T2's card reads its `MigrationAssessment`. The Database Agent panel and its prompts name the GA `databasehub-cli` skill (the `fabric-skills` plugin) and the `microsoft-sql` plugin instead of `microsoft-sql-fdh`.

### The review of T5: four fixes (2026-11-19)

**Why.** An independent code review of T5 (`41a3a1b..78e080a`), relayed by the coordinator: four issues, two of them High because they hit existing users who update; fix them before the follow-up batch, each in its own commit, with tests. The review found nothing significant in security, cost, the storm's cleanup and bounds, teardown, the DNS zone, metrics, strict mode, or the app's numbers.

**Work summary.**

1. **High: Azure refusing T5's free tier moved T3 off the Azure SQL free offer** (28ba289; `Invoke-DemoTemplateDeployment`, `Resolve-DemoT3FreeOfferError`, `Test-DemoT5FreeTierRefusal`, `Get-DemoT5FreeTierRefusalReason`). T3's free-offer check ran first, and its `free tier` matched both of Azure Cosmos DB's refusals, so a run whose Resource Graph read missed the free tier's holder, raced another deployment, or couldn't read the `quotaId` turned `t3UseFreeLimit` off: a new T3 created paid, an existing free T3 moved to paid for good, or a failed update. Now T5's refusal is checked first and counts only in Azure Cosmos DB's own error detail (the text from the error target before "free tier" to the next names Cosmos DB, `Microsoft.DocumentDB`, `Microsoft.Azure.Documents`, or `cosmos01`), so an Azure SQL error that says "free tier" never costs T5 the free tier either; T3's check ignores Cosmos DB's details and no longer takes "free tier" for its offer (Azure SQL's own refusals name a "free limit database", "free database", or "free offer").
2. **High: `t5Enabled` false didn't get past a policy that denies Azure Cosmos DB** (d7e360d; `Get-DemoResourceTypeList`, `Get-DemoPolicyConstraint`, `PolicyHelpers.ps1`, `PolicyCache.ps1`). The policy checks take the configuration's resource types: with T5 off, T5's four `Microsoft.DocumentDB` types aren't checked, a rule for them alone counts as unrelated, and the policy cache is keyed on it. With T5 on, a denial of T5's types alone is a **Fail** whose fix says to set `"t5Enabled": false`; with other types too, the fix says that leaves T5's out.
3. **Medium: a failure in T5 alone ended an update NOT DONE, and a resume couldn't get past it** (0b2eaaf; `Get-DemoT5OnlyFailure`, `Copy-DemoT5OffConfig`, `New-DemoT5LeftOutResult`, `Test-DemoT5LeftOut`, `Resolve-DemoT5LeftOut`, the template, both deploy paths, the tracks' handoff, DONE). When the run creates T5's account and every failed operation is T5's (its Cosmos DB resources, the `cosmos01` deployments, its private endpoint and DNS zone, or a policy's refusal naming only T5's resources), the template is deployed again once without T5; `DEPLOY.T5`, a **Warning**, gives Azure's reason and the fix (`t5Enabled` false, or another region) on the console, the Infrastructure step, and T5's rows; the rest of the run, its tracks, and DONE go on without T5, so it can end **DONE**. The resource group records it (`DbHubT5Refused`), so a resume leaves T5 out instead of starting from preflight (`DEPLOY.T5.MISSING`); a run whose template creates T5 clears it. An account that existed before the run is never left out, and its `DEPLOY.TEMPLATE` fix says how to deploy without T5. The template's attempt limit now counts T5's two retries (8, or up to 10 with `t4SkuName`).
4. **Low: `deploy.ps1 -Sequential` with `t4Enabled` false skipped T5's checks** (c1670f7): the T4 stage's T5 part now runs first.

**Validation.** Each fix's new tests fail on the code before it and pass after (checked in a throwaway worktree): fix 1, 11 of 21 (the other 10 test behavior that didn't change); fix 2, 4 of 4; fix 4, 1 of 1 ("TestT5" not found). The suites they touch, together: 1,119 passed, 0 failed. **Fix 1 is validated by unit tests only:** every subscription the live tests use is internal, where T5 never asks for the free tier (its `quotaId`), and no test environment's T3 has the free offer, which the agent-loop session confirmed read-only. So its tests use Azure's exact texts, "Free tier is not supported for Internal subscriptions" (live, 2026-11-18) and "Free tier has already been applied to another Azure Cosmos DB account in this subscription", and Azure SQL's real refusal, "Provisioning of free limit database is not supported for provided service level objective or region" (Microsoft Q&A), through the real `Resolve-DemoT5FreeTier` and the template's retries: an update with an existing free T3, a new deployment, an unreadable `quotaId`, both refusals in one error, T3's own refusal, and Azure SQL errors that say "free tier" before or after a Cosmos DB failure.

**Risks.** None new.

### T5's container only during a session, the secret scan, and a stopped T4 (2026-11-19)

**Why.** The coordinator's follow-up batch to T5 (2026-11-18 22:50 ET), four items: (1) T5's idle cost when the free tier is refused: most of the demo's users are Microsoft-internal, so T5's $31.41 a month at list price, 400 RU/s around the clock, was the usual case, about +48% on the lowest-cost profile's light-use month, for a target used only during sessions; remove its provisioned throughput while idle if that's reliable, with the bar that the storm stays reliable, nothing is manual, an update migrates by itself, T5's metrics and history stay meaningful, and every path reports on the status page; (2) `validate.ps1`'s Security area scanned `out/fabric-app/node_modules`, 114k files and 37+ minutes; (3) `T4.DATABASE` was a **Fail** on a stopped T4, so `validate.ps1` after any session had 1 **Fail**; (4) R896, T5 idle after its last storm. The owner's condition, relayed by the coordinator (2026-11-19): a session must never run without T5's container. The coordinator approved the two role additions provisionally that night, and the owner approved them on 2026-11-19 ([ADR 0027](adr/0027-t5-cosmos-db.md#the-container-only-during-a-session-2026-11-19)).

**Work summary.**

1. **The container only during a session** (`T5Helpers.ps1`: `New-DemoT5Container`, `Remove-DemoT5Container`, `Invoke-DemoT5ContainerStop`, `Resolve-DemoT5ContainerLifecycle`, `Get-DemoT5LifecycleText`, `Get-DemoT5CostLifecycle`; `Public/Update-DemoT5ContainerLifecycle.ps1`; the runbooks' `New-DbHubT5Container` and `Remove-DbHubT5Container`). A container's provisioned throughput can't be taken away, only deleted with it (manual throughput has a 400 RU/s floor, and dedicated throughput can't become a shared database's), and autoscale's floor still bills every hour, so the container goes between sessions, and the account, its database, private endpoint, DNS zone, and T1's data-plane role (scoped to the account) stay. Its definition is in one place, `config/versions.json` `cosmosdb` (partition key, version, indexing policy, throughput), which `cosmos01.bicep` deploys and the scripts and runbooks send through Azure Resource Manager, with the demo resource group's own tags. Created by `start-demo.ps1` while the VMs boot (`START.T5.CONTAINER`), Run all's session start, `demo-control.ps1` and the control's run action (`CONTROL.T5.CONTAINER`), and `deploy.ps1`'s T5 step (`DEPLOY.T5.CONTAINER`); deleted by `stop-demo.ps1` at its end, after T5's metrics were read for the history (`STOP.T5`), Stop now and the auto-stop, the nightly safety stop and its deferred pass, and the control's daily T4 pass while the VMs are deallocated. `deploy.ps1` leaves it, since the demo runs `business-day` until the nightly stop.
2. **Never a session without it:** the lifecycle is the demo resource group's `DbHubT5Container` tag. `deploy.ps1` sets it right after the session control's setup (`DEPLOY.T5.LIFECYCLE`, the status page's new **T5.Lifecycle** row): **Session** when the control's custom role has the container's actions and its identity holds it at the demo resource group, **AlwaysOn** otherwise; `grant-safety-stop.ps1` turns AlwaysOn into Session once an Owner granted the roles (`GRANT.T5.LIFECYCLE`); `stop-demo.ps1` checks the role again before it deletes anything, and turns Session back into AlwaysOn when the role can't any more. Every stop path deletes only with Session, so with AlwaysOn, or in a demo deployed before (no tag), the container stays, with a **Warning** that says what it bills and the fix (a **Pass** on the free tier).
3. **The roles** (`ActivityControlHelpers.ps1`, `SafetyStopHelpers.ps1`; approved by the owner, 2026-11-19): "DbHub Demo Activity Operator" gains `Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts/sqlDatabases/containers/read`, `/write`, and `/delete`; "DbHub Demo Safety Stop" gains `containers/read` and `/delete`. An Owner's `deploy.ps1` updates both definitions before any session relies on them (`CONTROL.ROLE.DEFINITION` and `SAFETYSTOP.ROLE` name what they added). ADR 0024, ADR 0026's role list, and `docs/permissions.md` name both changes.
4. **Checks and status:** `T5.CONTAINER` is a **Pass** for a missing container between sessions (Session, `sqlvm01` not running), a **Warning** for one missing while `sqlvm01` runs or there while the demo is stopped, and a **Fail** only when nothing creates it; `T5.LIFECYCLE` (`validate.ps1 -Area T5`); `STATUS.T5` says whether the container is there and what bills.

Callers price an existing environment whose tag isn't Session as AlwaysOn. Before and after (Azure Retail Prices API, 2026-11-19, West US 3, list, `lowest-cost`, 10 light-use hours): an internal subscription's T5 month goes from $31.41 to $8.12 ($7.80 plus $0.0323 an hour), its whole light-use month from $96.16 to $72.87; on the free tier, $7.80 and $72.55 both before and after. A 5-hour session goes from $15.03 to $15.19.
6. **The runner** (by a sub-agent): an activity on T5 with no container is refused with the reason and retried by the profile host every 30 seconds within its window (`RefusalPasses`); `reset` and every storm cleanup with no container are a **Pass** with nothing to clean; `status` says the container doesn't exist now, without an error; `warmup` and `setup` say it exists only during a session.

### A session's history saved once (R907, 2026-11-19)

**Why.** The DBA console's review left R907 open: the Insights app's **Stop now** cancels the control's run, which may be saving a session's history, and then saves that session again. The coordinator asked that the activity notebook's save of one session be idempotent, with tests for a save cut off after some tables and run again, and for a first save that's unchanged; that the history model's measures and the Insights app's queries not double-count; and that the agent loop's `database_agent` finding and T5's history stay as they are.

**What duplicated.** `NB_DatabaseHub_LiveActivity` gave each run a run ID of its own (its time and 8 hex characters), deleted only that run's rows before each append, and wrote the session's `scenario_runs` rows last; section 3 ends a run whose session row is already there. A run cut off after `telemetry_snapshots` and `analysis_findings`, before `scenario_runs`, left their rows, and the next run of the session saved them again under its own run ID. Stop now's save and the pre-check's pass no plan (`SESSION_PLAN`), so that run also took the session's beats for unexplained signals and merged them into `incident_windows` as detected episodes, beside the windows the first run had recorded. Run against the notebook before this change, the test's lakehouse ends with 18 telemetry rows of 9, 6 findings of 4, and 2 incident windows of 1, and running the persist cell twice in one run doubled `scenario_runs`.

**Work summary.**

- **One run ID per session:** with `SESSION_ID`, the run ID is `session-<id>` (helpers, part 1), so every run of a session saves under it.
- **Each table once per session** (`saved_earlier`, helpers, part 3): `write_delta` keeps a table that already has this run ID's rows from an earlier run, and `prepare_report_tables` doesn't merge the incident windows again when they have them; each says so in one line. A table this run saved (`SAVED_TABLES`) is replaced when the cell runs again, as before, and `scenario_runs` is now too: it was append-only since the first release, when other writers added rows to it.
- **Why not delete and replace:** the runs that save a session again pass no plan, so they'd replace the plan's correlation and `database_agent` findings with fewer, and an incident window can't be deleted by session, because a merge also updates other sessions' rows.
- **Narration:** section 11 says what a session's runs share and what the next run does after a save that a cancel cut off.

**The model and the app.** The telemetry measures take each bin's latest capture, and the findings' attention measures each finding's latest capture, so duplicates didn't change them; **Findings** and **Incidents** (`COUNTROWS`) and **Notebook Runs Captured** (distinct run IDs) counted them, and now there are none. The app's T4 and T5 history queries take the run of the latest finding and join its telemetry on the run ID, which all of a session's rows now share, whichever run saved them. Only **Validation Results**' run IDs are ordered, in the model and the app, and this notebook doesn't write that table.

**Changed files.** `fabric/notebooks/NB_DatabaseHub_LiveActivity.ipynb`; test `Fabric.Notebooks.Tests.ps1`; `CHANGELOG.md`, `fabric/README.md`, and this report.

**Validation.** The new test in `Fabric.Notebooks.Tests.ps1` runs the notebook's setup, section 3, and persist cells, with Python 3 and pandas, against a lakehouse in memory:

- A first save writes the same rows in the same order, the session's rows last, and deletes and keeps nothing.
- A save cut off before `scenario_runs`, then Stop now's without the plan: one copy of each row, one `database_agent` finding, and no detected twin of the beat.
- A save cut off after `telemetry_snapshots` is completed once, the session's rows last, and a run after it saves nothing.
- The persist cell run twice replaces its rows in every table.
- Two analyses without a session keep their own run IDs, read nothing more, and save their own rows, as before.

Against the notebook before this change, it fails. The full static validation (`./tests/Invoke-StaticValidation.ps1 -CI`, with Python 3.11 and pandas), over `origin/ignite-updates` at ab91ee5: PSScriptAnalyzer 0 findings in 386 files; Pester 4,886 tests, 4,881 passed, 1 failed, and 4 skipped (gitleaks isn't on this PC, 3; the history report generator's npm packages, 1), and no unit test reached the Azure CLI; Bicep, PSRule (302 rules), .NET, the Fabric app, and markdownlint pass. The failure was `DbHubDemo.Lifecycle.Tests.ps1`'s lock test, which probes a machine-wide named lock, while another worktree's Pester run on this PC held it; that file then passed, 258 of 258, three times in a row. Over c31878e, before the rebase, the same validation had no failure (4,780 tests, 4,776 passed, 4 skipped). No live run: the combined final tests of `ignite-updates` are its live proof.

**Risks.** R907 fixed; what stays open is in its row. ADR 0029's consequences still say that such a cancel can leave duplicate rows (R907); the DBA console's session owns that ADR.

**Why.** The coordinator's docs audit, for the same handoff as the review of ab91ee5: `PREFLIGHT.COST.MONTHLY` and `estimate-cost.ps1` never said the worst-case total they compare with the ceiling, so a user couldn't see why the check passed or failed; and the estimate counted one Bastion hour per session (S9, `bastionHoursPerSession`), though a default deployment has no Bastion.

**Work summary.**

1. **The total** (`Get-DemoCostEstimate`, `estimate-cost.ps1`): `PREFLIGHT.COST.MONTHLY` starts with "lowest-cost: the month's worst case is X USD, Y USD under (or over) the hard ceiling of Z USD. It counts idle plus 10 hours of use, A USD; T4's automatic restart for H hours, B USD; and T5's container for the running hours only (Session)", or all month (AlwaysOn). Its evidence adds `monthlyCeiling` and `monthlyMargin`, and the estimate's object `MonthlyWorstCase`, `MonthlyCeiling`, `MonthlyMargin`, and `BastionHours`; `estimate-cost.ps1` prints "The monthly check", a table of the same for each profile. `start-demo.ps1`'s guardrail reports the same `PREFLIGHT.COST.MONTHLY`, so it says it too; its `START.COST.ACTUAL` already gave its own total, the month's actual cost plus a session.

Only `start-demo.ps1 -Interactive` deploys it (the walkthrough adds it only for T2's optional missing-index story), and it goes after `bastionMaxHours`. So `bastionHoursPerSession` is 0; `start-demo.ps1 -Interactive` counts Bastion in its guardrail for up to `bastionMaxHours` and the session's length (`Test-DemoStartCost -BastionHours`), and `estimate-cost.ps1 -BastionHours` prices such a session.
